sentences.zh: 列傳二百七十二

translations.literal: Biography two hundred seventy-two
translations.idiomatic: Biography 272

sentences.zh: 文苑二

translations.literal: Literary Garden two
translations.idiomatic: Literary Figures, Part Two

sentences.zh: 諸錦厲鶚王峻何夢瑤劉大櫆李鍇沈炳震曹仁虎胡天游袁枚王又曾邵齊燾徐文靖朱仕琇蔣士銓趙翼嚴長明朱筠翁方綱姚鼐宋大樽章學誠祁韻士馮敏昌法式善惲敬黎簡張士元

translations.literal: Zhu Jin, Li E, Wang Jun, He Mengyao, Liu Dakui, Li Kai, Shen Bingzhen, Cao Renhu, Hu Tianyou, Yuan Mei, Wang Youceng, Shao Qidao, Xu Wenjing, Zhu Shixiu, Jiang Shiquan, Zhao Yi, Yan Changming, Zhu Yun, Weng Fanggang, Yao Nai, Song Dazun, Zhang Xuecheng, Qi Yunshi, Feng Minchang, Fa Shi Shan, Yun Jing, Li Jian, Zhang Shiyuan
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Jin, Li E, Wang Jun, He Mengyao, Liu Dakui, Li Kai, Shen Bingzhen, Cao Renhu, Hu Tianyou, Yuan Mei, Wang Youceng, Shao Qidao, Xu Wenjing, Zhu Shixiu, Jiang Shiquan, Zhao Yi, Yan Changming, Zhu Yun, Weng Fanggang, Yao Nai, Song Dazun, Zhang Xuecheng, Qi Yunshi, Feng Minchang, Fa Shi Shan, Yun Jing, Li Jian, and Zhang Shiyuan

sentences.zh: 諸錦，字襄七，秀水人。

translations.literal: Zhu Jin, styled Xiangqi, was a man of Xiushui.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Jin, whose style was Xiangqi, came from Xiushui.

sentences.zh: 少時家貧陋，輒就讀書肆，主人敬其勤學，恣所觀覽。

translations.literal: In youth his family was poor and mean; he would go to bookshops to read, and the shopkeepers, respecting his diligence in study, allowed him to view whatever he wished.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth his household was poor and humble; he would go to bookshops to read, and the proprietors, admiring his zeal for learning, let him browse their stock freely.

sentences.zh: 顧嗣立為之延譽，名大起。

translations.literal: Gu Sili spread his reputation for him, and his fame rose greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Sili championed him, and his name spread far and wide.

sentences.zh: 雍正二年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the second year of Yongzheng.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the second year of the Yongzheng reign.

sentences.zh: 乾隆初，試鴻博，授編修。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianlong, he sat for the Hongbo examination and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qianlong reign he took the special erudition examination and was appointed a Hanlin compiler.

sentences.zh: 閉門撰述，不詣權要。

translations.literal: He shut his doors to write, and did not call on the powerful.
translations.idiomatic: He shut himself away to write and never paid court to men in power.

sentences.zh: 至左贊善，遂告歸。

translations.literal: He rose to Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent, then requested leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Left Tutor of the Heir Apparent, then retired.

sentences.zh: 著有毛詩說、饗禮補亡、夏小正注及絳跗閣集。

translations.literal: His works include Expositions on the Mao Odes, Supplements to Lost Portions of the Feasting Rites, Commentary on the Xia Xiaozheng, and the Jiangfu Pavilion Collection.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Expositions on the Mao Odes, Supplements to Lost Portions of the Feasting Rites, a commentary on the Xia Xiaozheng, and the Jiangfu Pavilion Collection.

sentences.zh: 先是康熙己未徵博學鴻儒，得人稱盛。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the jiwai year of Kangxi, erudite scholars of broad learning were summoned, and the men obtained were acclaimed as outstanding.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the jiwai year of the Kangxi reign, the court had summoned men of broad erudition, and the scholars chosen were hailed as a brilliant cohort.

sentences.zh: 高宗御極，复舉行焉，內外薦達二百六十七人，試列一等者五人，錦第三；

translations.literal: When the Gaozong Emperor took the throne, the examination was held again; two hundred sixty-seven men were recommended from within and without the court; five ranked in the first class on the examination, Jin third among them;
translations.idiomatic: When the Gaozong Emperor came to the throne, the examination was held again; two hundred sixty-seven candidates were put forward from inside and outside the court; five placed in the first class, with Jin third;

sentences.zh: 二等十人。

translations.literal: ten in the second class.
translations.idiomatic: and ten in the second class.

sentences.zh: 明年補試，續取四人，錢塘陈兆崙、仁和沈廷芳、高郵夏之蓉，皆試列二等者也。

translations.literal: The next year a supplementary examination was held and four more were taken: Chen Zhaolun of Qiantang, Shen Tingfang of Renhe, and Xia Zhirong of Gaoyou—all had ranked in the second class on the examination.
translations.idiomatic: The following year a supplementary examination added four more: Chen Zhaolun of Qiantang, Shen Tingfang of Renhe, and Xia Zhirong of Gaoyou—all had placed in the second class.

sentences.zh: 兆崙自有傳。

translations.literal: Zhaolun has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaolun has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 廷芳，字畹叔。

translations.literal: Tingfang, styled Wanshu.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Tingfang, whose style was Wanshu,

sentences.zh: 由監生舉鴻博，授編修，遷御史。

translations.literal: was nominated for the Hongbo examination as a student of the Imperial Academy, appointed compiler, and promoted to censor.
translations.idiomatic: entered through the Imperial Academy, was nominated for the erudition examination, appointed compiler, and later promoted to censor.

sentences.zh: 奏毀都城智化寺內明閹王振造像及李賢所撰頌德碑，報可。

translations.literal: He memorialized that the Ming eunuch Wang Zhen's image in Zhihua Temple in the capital and the eulogistic stele composed by Li Xian should be destroyed; the request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized for the destruction of the Ming eunuch Wang Zhen's statue in Zhihua Temple in the capital and of the encomiastic stele written by Li Xian; the court approved.

sentences.zh: 出為登萊青道，遷河南按察使。

translations.literal: He went out as intendant of Deng-Lai-Qing circuit and was transferred to Henan surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He served as intendant of the Deng-Lai-Qing circuit and was later transferred to Henan as surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 廷芳少從方苞遊，為文無纖佻之習。

translations.literal: Tingfang in youth associated with Fang Bao; his prose had none of the frivolous and affected manner.
translations.idiomatic: Tingfang had studied under Fang Bao in his youth, and his prose never took on a frivolous or affected tone.

sentences.zh: 詩學本查慎行。

translations.literal: His poetry took Zha Shenxing as its model.
translations.idiomatic: His poetry followed the model of Zha Shenxing.

sentences.zh: 著隱拙齋集及十三經註疏正字、續經義考等書。

translations.literal: He wrote the Yinzhuo Studio Collection, Correct Characters in the Thirteen Classics with Commentaries, Continuation of the Examination of the Meanings of the Classics, and other books.
translations.idiomatic: His works include the Yinzhuo Studio Collection, Correct Characters in the Thirteen Classics with Commentaries, a continuation of the Examination of the Meanings of the Classics, and other books.

sentences.zh: 之蓉，字芙裳。

translations.literal: Zhirong, styled Fushang.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Zhirong, whose style was Fushang,

sentences.zh: 雍正十一年進士。

translations.literal: became a jinshi in the eleventh year of Yongzheng.
translations.idiomatic: became a jinshi in the eleventh year of the Yongzheng reign.

sentences.zh: 舉鴻博，以檢討典試福建，又督廣東、湖南學政。

translations.literal: He was nominated for the Hongbo examination, served as reviser while presiding over the Fujian provincial examination, and later supervised education in Guangdong and Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: He was nominated for the erudition examination, served as reviser while presiding over the Fujian provincial examination, and later supervised education in Guangdong and Hunan.

sentences.zh: 其校士也，必以通經學古為先。

translations.literal: In examining candidates he always put mastery of the classics and study of antiquity first.
translations.idiomatic: In selecting scholars he always gave first place to mastery of the classics and learning drawn from antiquity.

sentences.zh: 當時試一等者，劉綸居首，次則南城潘安禮、金壇於振、錢塘杭世駿；

translations.literal: Among those who ranked first class at the time, Liu Lun stood first; next came Pan Anli of Nancheng, Yu Zhen of Jintan, and Hang Shijun of Qiantang;
translations.idiomatic: Of those who placed in the first class at that examination, Liu Lun ranked first, followed by Pan Anli of Nancheng, Yu Zhen of Jintan, and Hang Shijun of Qiantang;

sentences.zh: 二等自兆崙等三人外，為無錫楊度汪，菏澤劉玉麟，休寧汪士湟、程恂，錢塘陳士璠，天台齊召南，會稽周長登。

translations.literal: among the second class, besides Zhaolun and the other three, were Yang Duwang of Wuxi, Liu Yulin of Heze, Wang Shihuang and Cheng Xun of Xiuning, Chen Shifan of Qiantang, Qi Zhaonan of Tiantai, and Zhou Changdeng of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: among the second class, besides Zhaolun and the other three, were Yang Duwang of Wuxi, Liu Yulin of Heze, Wang Shihuang and Cheng Xun of Xiuning, Chen Shifan of Qiantang, Qi Zhaonan of Tiantai, and Zhou Changdeng of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 其續取者，一等宜興萬松齡，二等桐鄉朱荃、南安洪世澤、石屏張漢，凡十九人。

translations.literal: Among those taken in the supplementary round, first class: Wan Songling of Yixing; second class: Zhu Quan of Tongxiang, Hong Shize of Nan'an, and Zhang Han of Shiping—nineteen in all.
translations.idiomatic: Those added in the supplementary round included Wan Songling of Yixing in the first class and Zhu Quan of Tongxiang, Hong Shize of Nan'an, and Zhang Han of Shiping in the second—nineteen men in all.

sentences.zh: 惟綸、玉麟官最顯，而世駿、召南及兆崙尤知名於世云。

translations.literal: Only Lun and Yulin attained the most eminent offices, yet Shijun, Zhaonan, and Zhaolun were especially renowned in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Only Lun and Yulin rose to the highest offices, but Shijun, Zhaonan, and Zhaolun were especially celebrated.

sentences.zh: 厲鶚，字太鴻，錢塘人。

translations.literal: Li E, styled Taihong, was a man of Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: Li E, whose style was Taihong, came from Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 家貧，性孤峭，不苟合。

translations.literal: His family was poor; his nature aloof and stern; he would not compromise himself.
translations.idiomatic: His family was poor; he was aloof and uncompromising by nature and would not curry favor.

sentences.zh: 始為詩即得佳句。

translations.literal: From the time he first wrote poetry he produced fine lines.
translations.idiomatic: From his earliest attempts at poetry he produced memorable lines.

sentences.zh: 於學無所不窺，一發之於詩。

translations.literal: In learning there was nothing he did not investigate; he poured it all forth in poetry.
translations.idiomatic: There was no branch of learning he did not explore, and he poured it all into his verse.

sentences.zh: 康熙五十九年，李紱典試浙江，得鶚卷，閱其謝表，曰：「此必詩人也！」

translations.literal: In the fifty-ninth year of Kangxi, Li Fu presided over the Zhejiang provincial examination, obtained E's paper, read his letter of thanks, and said, "This must be a poet!"
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-ninth year of the Kangxi reign, Li Fu presided over the Zhejiang provincial examination, came upon E's paper, read his letter of thanks, and said, "This must be a poet!"

sentences.zh: 亟錄之。

translations.literal: He immediately passed him.
translations.idiomatic: He passed him at once.

sentences.zh: 計偕入都，尤以詩見賞湯右曾。

translations.literal: When he went to the capital for the metropolitan examination, Tang Youzeng especially admired his poetry.
translations.idiomatic: When he went to the capital for the metropolitan examination, Tang Youzeng was especially taken with his poetry.

sentences.zh: 再試禮部不第。

translations.literal: He sat for the Ministry of Rites examination again and failed.
translations.idiomatic: He failed the Ministry of Rites examination on a second attempt.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，舉鴻博，誤寫論置詩前，又報罷。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong he was nominated for the Hongbo examination, but mistakenly placed his essay before his poems and was rejected again.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qianlong he was nominated for the erudition examination, but placed his essay before his poems by mistake and was rejected again.

sentences.zh: 其後赴都銓，行次天津，留友人查為仁水西莊，觴詠數月，不就選，歸。

translations.literal: Later he went to the capital for appointment; on the way he stopped at Tianjin and stayed at his friend Zha Weiren's Shuixi Manor, drinking and composing for several months, and did not take up his appointment but returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Later, on his way to the capital for official appointment, he stopped at Tianjin and stayed for months at his friend Zha Weiren's Shuixi Manor, drinking and composing verse; he never took up his appointment and returned home.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十一。

translations.literal: He died at the age of sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 鶚蒐奇嗜博。

translations.literal: E collected curiosities and loved breadth of learning.
translations.idiomatic: Li E collected curiosities and was insatiably learned.

sentences.zh: 揚州馬曰琯小玲瓏山館富藏書，鶚久客其所，多見宋人集，為宋詩紀事一百卷。

translations.literal: Ma Yueguan of Yangzhou's Little Exquisite Hill Lodge was rich in book collections; E was a long-term guest there, saw many Song anthologies, and compiled the Song Poetry Historical Records in one hundred juan.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Yueguan of Yangzhou kept a magnificent library at his Little Exquisite Hill Lodge; Li E lodged there for years, gained access to many Song anthologies, and compiled the Song Poetry Historical Records in one hundred juan.

sentences.zh: 又南宋畫院錄、遼史拾遺、東城雜記諸書，皆博洽詳贍。

translations.literal: His Records of the Southern Song Painting Academy, gleanings from the Liao History, and Miscellaneous Notes on the Eastern City and other works were all broad, thorough, and ample.
translations.idiomatic: His Records of the Southern Song Painting Academy, gleanings from the Liao History, Miscellaneous Notes on the Eastern City, and other works were all learned and comprehensive.

sentences.zh: 詩刻鍊，尤工五言，有自得之趣。

translations.literal: His poetry was carved and refined; he was especially skilled in pentasyllabic verse and had a flavor all his own.
translations.idiomatic: His poetry was finely wrought; he excelled especially in pentasyllabic verse and achieved a distinctive voice of his own.

sentences.zh: 詩馀亦擅南宋諸家之長。

translations.literal: In lyric poetry too he mastered the strengths of the Southern Song masters.
translations.idiomatic: In lyric poetry as well he mastered the strengths of the Southern Song masters.

sentences.zh: 先世本慈谿，徙居錢塘，故仍以四明山樊榭名其集雲。

translations.literal: His forebears were originally from Cixi but moved to Qiantang; therefore he still named his collection after Fan Pavilion on Siming Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestors were originally from Cixi but had moved to Qiantang; he still named his collected works after Fan Pavilion on Siming Mountain.

sentences.zh: 鶚嘗與趙信、符曾等人各為南宋雜事詩一百首，自採諸書為之注，徵引浩博，考史事者重之。

translations.literal: E once joined Zhao Xin, Fu Ceng, and others, each writing one hundred poems on miscellaneous Southern Song matters; he gathered material from various books to annotate them himself; the citations were vast and those who investigate historical events prize the work.
translations.idiomatic: Li E once joined Zhao Xin, Fu Ceng, and others in writing one hundred poems each on miscellaneous Southern Song topics, annotating them with material drawn from many books; the citations are vast, and historians still rely on the work.

sentences.zh: 汪沆，字師李。

translations.literal: Wang Hang, styled Shili.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hang, whose style was Shili,

sentences.zh: 少從鶚受詩，亦試鴻博報罷。

translations.literal: In youth studied poetry under E; he too sat for the Hongbo examination and was rejected.
translations.idiomatic: studied poetry under Li E in his youth and likewise took the erudition examination without success.

sentences.zh: 其後大學士史貽直將以經學薦，以母老辭。

translations.literal: Later Grand Secretary Shi Yizhi was about to recommend him for classical learning, but he declined on account of his aged mother.
translations.idiomatic: Later Grand Secretary Shi Yizhi was about to recommend him for his classical scholarship, but he declined because his mother was elderly.

sentences.zh: 同時浙江舉鴻博未錄用者，符曾，字幼魯。

translations.literal: Among those from Zhejiang nominated for the Hongbo examination at the same time but not employed was Fu Ceng, styled Youru.
translations.idiomatic: Among contemporaries from Zhejiang nominated for the erudition examination but not appointed was Fu Ceng, whose style was Youru.

sentences.zh: 官戶部郎中。

translations.literal: He served as director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He served as a director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 鄞縣陳撰最推服其詩。

translations.literal: Chen Zhuan of Yin county most admired his poetry.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zhuan of Yin county admired his poetry above all others.

sentences.zh: 撰，字楞山，毛奇齡弟子。

translations.literal: Zhuan, styled Lengshan, was a disciple of Mao Qiling.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zhuan, whose style was Lengshan, was a disciple of Mao Qiling.

sentences.zh: 以布衣薦，未就試。

translations.literal: Recommended as a commoner, he did not sit for the examination.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended as a commoner, he never sat for the examination.

sentences.zh: 仁和趙昱，字功平。

translations.literal: Zhao Yu of Renhe, styled Gongping.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yu of Renhe, whose style was Gongping,

sentences.zh: 貢生。

translations.literal: was a tribute student.
translations.idiomatic: was a tribute student.

sentences.zh: 弟信，字辰垣。

translations.literal: His younger brother Xin, styled Chenyuan,
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Xin, whose style was Chenyuan,

sentences.zh: 國學生。

translations.literal: was a student of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: was a student of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 兄弟同舉。

translations.literal: The brothers were nominated together.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers were nominated together.

sentences.zh: 家有池館之勝，喜購書。

translations.literal: Their household had the charm of pools and pavilions; they delighted in buying books.
translations.idiomatic: Their household boasted fine gardens and pools, and they delighted in acquiring books.

sentences.zh: 連江陳氏世善堂書散出，皆歸之。

translations.literal: When the books of the Chen family Shishan Hall of Lianjiang were dispersed, all came to them.
translations.idiomatic: When the library of the Chen family's Shishan Hall in Lianjiang was broken up, they acquired it all.

sentences.zh: 王峻，字艮齋，常熟人。

translations.literal: Wang Jun, styled Genzhai, was a man of Changshu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun, whose style was Genzhai, came from Changshu.

sentences.zh: 少與同里宋君玉師事陳祖範，一時並稱王宋。

translations.literal: In youth he and Song Junyu of the same district studied under Chen Zufan; at the time they were jointly called Wang and Song.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he and his fellow townsman Song Junyu studied under Chen Zufan; at the time they were known together as Wang and Song.

sentences.zh: 雍正二年進士，授編修。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the second year of Yongzheng and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in the second year of the Yongzheng reign and was appointed a Hanlin compiler.

sentences.zh: 歷典浙江、貴州、雲南鄉試。

translations.literal: He successively presided over the provincial examinations of Zhejiang, Guizhou, and Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: He successively presided over the provincial examinations in Zhejiang, Guizhou, and Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 乾隆初，改御史，拜官甫三日，劾左都御史彭維新矯詐苛鄙，直聲震都下。

translations.literal: Early in Qianlong he was transferred to censor; three days after taking office he impeached the Left Censor-in-Chief Peng Weixin for pretension, deceit, harshness, and meanness; his upright reputation shook the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qianlong reign he was transferred to censor; three days after taking office he impeached Left Censor-in-Chief Peng Weixin for pretension, deceit, harshness, and meanness, and his forthright reputation resounded through the capital.

sentences.zh: 以母憂去官，遂不出。

translations.literal: He left office on account of his mother's mourning and never went out again.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his mother and never served again.

sentences.zh: 主講安定、雲龍、紫陽書院。

translations.literal: He lectured at the Anding, Yunlong, and Ziyang academies.
translations.idiomatic: He lectured at the Anding, Yunlong, and Ziyang academies.

sentences.zh: 其學長於史，尤精地理。

translations.literal: His learning excelled in history and was especially refined in geography.
translations.idiomatic: His scholarship excelled in history and was especially refined in geography.

sentences.zh: 嘗以水經正文及注混淆，欲一一釐定之，而補唐以後水道之遷變，及地名之同異，為水經廣注，手自屬稿，未暇成也。

translations.literal: He once found the main text and commentary of the Water Classic confused and wished to distinguish them one by one, while supplementing changes in waterways after the Tang and similarities and differences in place-names, making an Expanded Commentary on the Water Classic; he drafted it with his own hand but had no leisure to finish it.
translations.idiomatic: Finding the main text and commentary of the Water Classic hopelessly confused, he planned to distinguish them line by line while supplementing post-Tang changes in waterways and variant place-names in an Expanded Commentary on the Water Classic; he drafted it himself but never had time to finish it.

sentences.zh: 惟成漢書正誤四卷。

translations.literal: He only completed Corrections to Errors in the Han History in four juan.
translations.idiomatic: He did complete Corrections to Errors in the Han History in four juan.

sentences.zh: 錢大昕謂駕三劉氏、吳氏刊誤上也。

translations.literal: Qian Daxin said it surpassed the three Liu families and Wu's emendations.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Daxin said it surpassed the emendations of the three Liu scholars and of Wu.

sentences.zh: 書法橅李北海，所書碑碣盛行於時。

translations.literal: His calligraphy modeled Li Beihai; the steles and tablets he wrote were widely popular in his time.
translations.idiomatic: His calligraphy followed the model of Li Beihai, and the steles and tablets he wrote were widely sought in his day.

sentences.zh: 王延年，字介眉，錢塘人。

translations.literal: Wang Yannian, styled Jiemei, was a man of Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yannian, whose style was Jiemei, came from Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 雍正四年舉人。

translations.literal: He became a provincial graduate in the fourth year of Yongzheng.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examination in the fourth year of the Yongzheng reign.

sentences.zh: 乾隆初，舉鴻博，後官國子監學政。

translations.literal: Early in Qianlong he was nominated for the Hongbo examination; later he served as educational intendant of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qianlong reign he was nominated for the erudition examination and later served as educational intendant of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 十七年，會試，以耆年晉司業，賜翰林院侍講銜。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, at the metropolitan examination, on account of his advanced age he was promoted to vice director of studies and granted the brevet rank of Hanlin attendant reader.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year, at the metropolitan examination, he was promoted to vice director of studies on account of his advanced age and granted the brevet rank of Hanlin attendant reader.

sentences.zh: 延年史學洽熟，嘗補袁樞通鑑紀事本末，以原書不言田制，則度地居民之法亡；

translations.literal: Yannian's historical learning was thorough and practiced; he once supplemented Yuan Shu's Comprehensive Mirror Historical Narratives in Full, arguing that because the original work does not speak of the field system, the methods of surveying land and settling the people are lost;
translations.idiomatic: Yannian's historical learning was thorough; he once supplemented Yuan Shu's Comprehensive Mirror Historical Narratives in Full, arguing that because the original says nothing about the field system, the methods of surveying land and settling the people are lost;

sentences.zh: 不言漕運，則鑿渠引河之利塞；

translations.literal: because it does not speak of grain transport by canal, the benefits of digging channels and drawing rivers are blocked;
translations.idiomatic: that because it says nothing about canal transport, the benefits of digging channels and drawing rivers are lost;

sentences.zh: 不言府兵，則耕牧戰守之功隳。

translations.literal: because it does not speak of fubing militia, the achievements of farming, herding, fighting, and defending are ruined.
translations.idiomatic: and that because it says nothing about the fubing militia, the achievements of farming, herding, fighting, and defending are undone.

sentences.zh: 至於耶律鴟張遼海，而陳邦瞻書不究其終；

translations.literal: As for the Liao prince spreading his wings over the Liao Sea while Chen Bangzhan's book does not pursue the outcome to the end;
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan spread their power over the Liao region, Chen Bangzhan's book does not pursue the outcome to the end;

sentences.zh: 党項虎視河、湟，薛應旂書不詳其始。

translations.literal: the Tangut glaring like tigers at the He and Huang rivers while Xue Yingqi's book does not detail the beginning.
translations.idiomatic: when the Tangut glared like tigers at the He and Huang rivers, Xue Yingqi's book does not explain how it began.

sentences.zh: 紹建安者又如此，不可不亟正之也。

translations.literal: Those who continued the Jian'an tradition were again like this; it could not but be urgently corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Those who carried on the Jian'an tradition repeat the same omissions; the work urgently needed correction.

sentences.zh: 杭世駿序之，比延年於唐杜君卿、宋劉中原父雲。

translations.literal: Hang Shijun wrote a preface for it, comparing Yannian to Du Junqing of Tang and Liu Zhongyuanfu of Song.
translations.idiomatic: Hang Shijun wrote a preface comparing Yannian to Du Junqing of the Tang and Liu Zhongyuanfu of the Song.

sentences.zh: 晚年，大學士蔣溥、劉統勳皆以經學薦，又自進呈所著書，上嘉許焉。

translations.literal: In his later years Grand Secretaries Jiang Pu and Liu Tongxun both recommended him for classical learning; he also presented his own writings to the throne, and the emperor praised them.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years Grand Secretaries Jiang Pu and Liu Tongxun both recommended him for his classical scholarship; he also presented his own writings to the throne, and the emperor commended them.

sentences.zh: 何夢瑤，字報之，南海人。

translations.literal: He Mengyao, styled Baozhi, was a man of Nanhai.
translations.idiomatic: He Mengyao, whose style was Baozhi, came from Nanhai.

sentences.zh: 惠士奇視學廣東，一以通經學古為教。

translations.literal: Hui Shiqi inspected learning in Guangdong and taught solely through mastery of the classics and study of antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: When Hui Shiqi served as Guangdong education commissioner, he taught solely through mastery of the classics and study of antiquity.

sentences.zh: 夢瑤與同里勞孝輿、吳世忠，順德羅天尺、蘇珥、陳世和、陳海六，番禺吳秋一時並起，有「惠門八子」之目。

translations.literal: Mengyao, together with Lao Xiaoyu and Wu Shizhong of the same district, Luo Tianchi, Su Er, Chen Shihe, and Chen Hailiu of Shunde, and Wu Qiu of Panyu, rose together at one time and were called the Eight Sons of the Hui School.
translations.idiomatic: Mengyao rose together with his fellow townsman Lao Xiaoyu and Wu Shizhong, with Luo Tianchi, Su Er, Chen Shihe, and Chen Hailiu of Shunde, and with Wu Qiu of Panyu; they were known as the Eight Sons of the Hui School.

sentences.zh: 雍正八年成進士，出宰粵西，治獄明慎，終奉天遼陽知州。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yongzheng he became a jinshi, went out as magistrate in western Guangdong, handled legal cases with clarity and care, and ended as prefect of Liaoyang in Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in the eighth year of the Yongzheng reign, served as a magistrate in western Guangdong with clarity and care in legal matters, and ended his career as prefect of Liaoyang in Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 性長於詩，兼通音律算術。

translations.literal: By nature he excelled in poetry and was also versed in pitch pipes, music, and mathematics.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he excelled in poetry and was also versed in music theory and mathematics.

sentences.zh: 謂蔡元定律呂新書，本原九章，為之訓釋。

translations.literal: He held that Cai Yuanding's New Book on the Pitch Pipes and Temperament derived from the Nine Chapters and wrote exegesis for it.
translations.idiomatic: He held that Cai Yuanding's New Book on the Pitch Pipes and Temperament derived from the Nine Chapters and wrote a commentary on it.

sentences.zh: 更取御製律呂正義研究八音協律和聲之用，述其大要。

translations.literal: He further took the imperially commissioned Correct Meaning of the Pitch Pipes and Temperament to investigate the use of the eight tones in harmonizing pitch pipes and blending sounds, and set forth its main points.
translations.idiomatic: He further studied the imperial Correct Meaning of the Pitch Pipes and Temperament to explain how the eight tones harmonize pitch pipes and blend sounds, and summarized its main points.

sentences.zh: 參以曹廷棟琴學，為書一編。

translations.literal: He compared this with Cao Tingdong's Studies of the Qin and made one book.
translations.idiomatic: Drawing also on Cao Tingdong's Studies of the Qin, he compiled a single treatise.

sentences.zh: 時稱其決擇精當。

translations.literal: At the time he was praised for the precision and fitness of his judgments.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries praised the precision of his judgments.

sentences.zh: 又著算迪，述梅氏之學，兼闡數理精蘊、歷象考成之旨。

translations.literal: He also wrote Arithmetic Explained, expounding the learning of the Mei family while clarifying the purport of the Essence of Mathematical Principles and the Investigation of Calendrical and Astronomical Phenomena.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote Arithmetic Explained, expounding the Mei family's mathematics while clarifying the purport of the Essence of Mathematical Principles and the Investigation of Calendrical and Astronomical Phenomena.

sentences.zh: 江籓謂近世為此學者，知有法，不知法之所以然；

translations.literal: Jiang Fan said that among recent scholars in this field, they know there are methods but do not know why the methods are so;
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Fan said that among recent scholars in this field, most know the methods but not why the methods work;

sentences.zh: 知之者，惟夢瑤也。

translations.literal: the one who knew why was only Mengyao.
translations.idiomatic: Mengyao alone truly understood why.

sentences.zh: 孝輿，字阮齋。

translations.literal: Xiaoyu, styled Ruanzhai.
translations.idiomatic: Lao Xiaoyu, whose style was Ruanzhai,

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，召試鴻博，未用。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong, he was summoned to test for the Hongbo examination and was not employed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qianlong he was summoned to the erudition examination but was not appointed.

sentences.zh: 以拔貢生廷試第五，出為黔中令。

translations.literal: As a selected tribute student he ranked fifth in the palace examination and was sent out as magistrate of Qianzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Having entered as a selected tribute student and placed fifth in the palace examination, he was appointed magistrate in Qianzhong.

sentences.zh: 治古州屯務，足繭萬山中。

translations.literal: He administered the military colony affairs of Guzhou, his feet calloused from trudging through myriad mountains.
translations.idiomatic: He administered military colony affairs at Guzhou, trudging through countless mountain passes until his feet were calloused.

sentences.zh: 將去，民攀轅曰：「公勞苦以衣食我！」

translations.literal: When he was about to depart, the people clung to his carriage axletree and said: "The lord has toiled to clothe and feed us!"
translations.idiomatic: When he was about to leave, the people clung to his carriage and cried, "You have toiled to provide us with clothing and food!"

sentences.zh: 皆泣下。

translations.literal: All wept.
translations.idiomatic: All wept.

sentences.zh: 歷錦屏、龍泉、鎮遠諸邑，皆有績。

translations.literal: He served successively in Jinping, Longquan, Zhenyuan, and other districts, and in each achieved merit.
translations.idiomatic: He later served in Jinping, Longquan, Zhenyuan, and other districts, distinguishing himself in each post.

sentences.zh: 卒於官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 天尺，字履先。

translations.literal: Tianchi, styled Lüxian.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Tianchi, whose style was Lüxian,

sentences.zh: 年十七，應學使試。

translations.literal: At seventeen he sat for the provincial education commissioner's examination.
translations.idiomatic: At seventeen he sat for the provincial education commissioner's examination.

sentences.zh: 士奇手錄其賦、詩示諸生，名大起。

translations.literal: Shiqi copied out his fu and poems by hand to show the students, and his fame rose greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Hui Shiqi copied out his fu and poems by hand to show the students, and his reputation spread swiftly.

sentences.zh: 徵鴻博，念親老不就，以舉人終。

translations.literal: He was summoned for the Hongbo examination, but thinking his parents were old he did not accept and ended his career as a provincial graduate.
translations.idiomatic: When summoned for the erudition examination, he declined out of concern for his aged parents and remained a provincial graduate for life.

sentences.zh: 雍正時修一統志，與孝輿同纂粵乘。

translations.literal: When the Comprehensive Gazetteer was compiled in the Yongzheng reign, he joined Xiaoyu in compiling the Guangdong Gazetteer.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongzheng reign he helped compile the Comprehensive Gazetteer and worked with Lao Xiaoyu on the Guangdong Gazetteer.

sentences.zh: 孝輿忤俗，被口語，天尺力白之。

translations.literal: Xiaoyu offended public opinion and was subject to gossip; Tianchi vigorously cleared his name.
translations.idiomatic: When Lao Xiaoyu offended local opinion and came under slander, Luo Tianchi vigorously defended him.

sentences.zh: 所居里曰石湖，世以前有范石湖，因稱後石湖以別之云。

translations.literal: The hamlet where he lived was called Stone Lake; because Fan Stone Lake had lived there earlier, it was called Later Stone Lake to distinguish them, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in a hamlet called Stone Lake; because Fan Chengda, known as Stone Lake, had lived there earlier, locals called it Later Stone Lake to distinguish the two.

sentences.zh: 珥，字瑞一。

translations.literal: Er, styled Ruiyi.
translations.idiomatic: Su Er, whose style was Ruiyi,

sentences.zh: 為文長於序記，詩有別趣，書法亦工。

translations.literal: In prose he excelled at prefaces and records; his poetry had a distinctive flavor, and his calligraphy was also accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: His prose excelled in prefaces and commemorative essays, his poetry had a distinctive flavor, and his calligraphy was also accomplished.

sentences.zh: 惠士奇稱之曰「南海明珠」。

translations.literal: Hui Shiqi called him "Pearl of the South Sea."
translations.idiomatic: Hui Shiqi called him "Pearl of the South Sea."

sentences.zh: 舉鴻博，以母老，辭不試。

translations.literal: He was nominated for the Hongbo examination, but because his mother was old he declined and did not sit for it.
translations.idiomatic: Nominated for the erudition examination, he declined to sit because his mother was elderly.

sentences.zh: 乾隆初鄉舉，一試禮部，遂不出。

translations.literal: Early in Qianlong he passed the provincial examination, tried the Ministry of Rites once, and then did not go out again.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qianlong reign he passed the provincial examination, made one attempt at the metropolitan examination, and then withdrew from public life.

sentences.zh: 時粵東舉鴻博者，又有番禺車騰芳，字圖南。

translations.literal: At the time among those from eastern Guangdong nominated for the Hongbo examination there was also Che Tengfang of Panyu, styled Tunan.
translations.idiomatic: Among those from eastern Guangdong nominated for the erudition examination at the time was Che Tengfang of Panyu, whose style was Tunan.

sentences.zh: 康熙末，與里人許遂同徵。

translations.literal: At the end of Kangxi he was summoned together with his fellow townsman Xu Sui.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Kangxi reign he was summoned to the capital together with his fellow townsman Xu Sui.

sentences.zh: 至京後期，即乞終養歸。

translations.literal: After reaching the capital he missed the deadline and immediately requested leave for permanent care of his parents and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: After reaching the capital he missed the deadline and immediately petitioned to return home and care for his parents permanently.

sentences.zh: 後為海豐學官。

translations.literal: Later he became educational official of Haifeng.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as educational official of Haifeng.

sentences.zh: 學使吳鴻雅重之，嘗從容問其諸子頗有應試者乎，騰芳以皆失學對，吳益嘆異焉。

translations.literal: Education intendant Wu Hong held him in high esteem; once he casually asked whether any of his sons had sat for examinations, and Tengfang answered that all had lost their schooling; Wu sighed in wonder all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Education intendant Wu Hong held him in high regard and once casually asked whether any of his sons had sat for the examinations; Tengfang replied that none had been able to pursue their studies, and Wu marveled at him all the more.

sentences.zh: 遂，字揚雲。

translations.literal: Sui, styled Yangyun.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Sui, whose style was Yangyun,

sentences.zh: 康熙中舉人。

translations.literal: In the Kangxi reign he became a provincial graduate.
translations.idiomatic: He became a provincial graduate during the Kangxi reign.

sentences.zh: 為清河令，蠲逋賦，民德之。

translations.literal: He served as magistrate of Qinghe, remitted overdue taxes, and the people were grateful to him.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate of Qinghe he remitted overdue taxes, and the people were deeply grateful.

sentences.zh: 坐事去職。

translations.literal: Because of an affair he left office.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed from office after an incident.

sentences.zh: 巡撫薦應鴻博，格於部議，未試歸。

translations.literal: The governor recommended him for the Hongbo examination, but it was blocked by deliberation in the ministry, and he returned without sitting for it.
translations.idiomatic: The provincial governor recommended him for the erudition examination, but the ministry rejected the nomination, and he returned home without sitting for it.

sentences.zh: 韓海，字偉五，亦番禺人也。

translations.literal: Han Hai, styled Weiwu, was also a man of Panyu.
translations.idiomatic: Han Hai, whose style was Weiwu, was also from Panyu.

sentences.zh: 雍正十一年進士，官封川教諭。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Yongzheng he became a metropolitan graduate and served as instructor of Fengchuan.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the eleventh year of Yongzheng and served as instructor of Fengchuan.

sentences.zh: 大府欲薦應鴻博，海賦詩以見志，大府覽詩愕然，遂不復強。

translations.literal: The grand prefecture wished to recommend him for the Hongbo examination; Hai wrote a poem to reveal his intent, and when the grand prefect read the poem he was startled and did not press him further.
translations.idiomatic: When the provincial authorities wished to recommend him for the erudition examination, Hai wrote a poem declaring his intent; the officials read it, were taken aback, and did not press him further.

sentences.zh: 海亦旋卒。

translations.literal: Hai also soon died.
translations.idiomatic: Han Hai soon died as well.

sentences.zh: 李鍇，字鐵君，漢軍正黃旗人。

translations.literal: Li Kai, styled Tiejun, was a man of the Han Eight Banners' Plain Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Li Kai, whose style was Tiejun, was a member of the Han Eight Banners' Plain Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 祖恆忠，副都統。

translations.literal: His grandfather Hengzhong was vice commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Hengzhong served as vice commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 湖廣總督輝祖子。

translations.literal: He was the son of Huizu, governor-general of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: He was the son of Huizu, governor-general of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 鍇娶大學士索額圖女，家世貴盛，其於榮利泊如也。

translations.literal: Kai married the daughter of Grand Secretary Sonin; his family was noble and flourishing, yet toward honor and profit he was indifferent.
translations.idiomatic: Kai married the daughter of Grand Secretary Sonin; though his family was eminent and prosperous, he remained indifferent to rank and gain.

sentences.zh: 性友愛，兄伊山、祈山仕不遂，鍇省伊山戍所，累月乃歸。

translations.literal: By nature he was affectionate toward his brothers; his elder brothers Yishan and Qishan did not succeed in office, and Kai visited Yishan at his garrison post, staying for months before returning.
translations.idiomatic: Affectionate by nature, he cared deeply for his elder brothers Yishan and Qishan when their official careers faltered; he traveled to Yishan's garrison post and stayed for months before returning home.

sentences.zh: 祈山罷官還，無宅，以己屋授之，並鬻產為清宿逋。

translations.literal: When Qishan was dismissed and returned without a house, Kai gave him his own dwelling and also sold property to clear old debts.
translations.idiomatic: When Qishan was dismissed and returned home without a house, Kai gave him his own dwelling and sold property to clear his old debts.

sentences.zh: 嘗一充官庫筆帖式，旋棄去。

translations.literal: Once he served as a clerk in the government treasury, but soon abandoned the post.
translations.idiomatic: He once served briefly as a clerk in the government treasury but soon resigned.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，舉鴻博，未中選。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong he was nominated for the Hongbo examination but was not selected.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qianlong he was nominated for the erudition examination but was not selected.

sentences.zh: 十五年，詔舉經學，大臣交章論薦，以老疾辭。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year an edict called for recommendations in classical learning; great ministers submitted memorial after memorial recommending him, but he declined on grounds of age and illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year an edict called for recommendations in classical learning; leading ministers repeatedly recommended him, but he declined on grounds of age and illness.

sentences.zh: 少好山水，遊蹤所至，務窮其奇。

translations.literal: From youth he loved mountains and rivers; wherever his travels took him, he strove to exhaust their marvels.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he loved mountains and rivers and, wherever he traveled, sought out their most remarkable sights.

sentences.zh: 苦嗜茗，為鐵鐺瓦缶，一奴負以從。

translations.literal: He was passionately fond of tea, made an iron kettle and earthen jar, and had one servant carry them to follow him.
translations.idiomatic: Passionately fond of tea, he had an iron kettle and earthen jar made and kept a servant to carry them wherever he went.

sentences.zh: 客江南，嘗月夜挾琴客泛舟採石，彈大雅之章，扣舷和之，水宿者皆驚起，人莫測其致也。

translations.literal: While sojourning in Jiangnan, once on a moonlit night he took his qin aboard a guest boat and drifted on the water at Caishi; he played pieces in the grand style and beat the gunwale in accompaniment; those sleeping on the water all started up in alarm, and no one could fathom his intent.
translations.idiomatic: While sojourning in Jiangnan, he once took his qin aboard a boat on a moonlit night at Caishi, played grand old pieces, and beat the gunwale in time; those sleeping on the water all started up in alarm, and no one could fathom his purpose.

sentences.zh: 鍇既以屋讓兄，乃築室盤山廌青峰下，閉戶躭吟，罕接人事。

translations.literal: After Kai had given his house to his brother, he built a dwelling below Zhiqing Peak on Pan Mountain, closed his door and immersed himself in poetry, and rarely received visitors.
translations.idiomatic: After giving his house to his brother, Kai built a dwelling below Zhiqing Peak on Pan Mountain, shut himself in to compose poetry, and rarely received visitors.

sentences.zh: 歲一至城中，一二日即去。

translations.literal: Once a year he went to the city, and after one or two days he left.
translations.idiomatic: He visited the city only once a year and stayed but a day or two.

sentences.zh: 居盤山二十載而歿。

translations.literal: He lived on Pan Mountain for twenty years and then died.
translations.idiomatic: He lived on Pan Mountain for twenty years before he died.

sentences.zh: 詩古奧峭削。

translations.literal: His poetry was archaic, abstruse, steep, and austere.
translations.idiomatic: His poetry was archaic, dense, and sharply austere.

sentences.zh: 著睫巢集，又著原易及春秋通義、尚史。

translations.literal: He wrote Collected Works from the Eyelash Nest, and also wrote Original Commentary on the Changes, Comprehensive Meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals, and Respectful History.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Collected Works from the Eyelash Nest, as well as Original Commentary on the Changes, Comprehensive Meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals, and Respectful History.

sentences.zh: 陳景元，字石閭，漢軍鑲紅旗人。

translations.literal: Chen Jingyuan, styled Shilü, was a man of the Han Eight Banners' Bordered Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jingyuan, whose style was Shilü, was a member of the Han Eight Banners' Bordered Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 詩擬孟郊、賈島。

translations.literal: His poetry modeled Meng Jiao and Jia Dao.
translations.idiomatic: His poetry followed the manner of Meng Jiao and Jia Dao.

sentences.zh: 有石閭集。

translations.literal: He had the Shilü Collection.
translations.idiomatic: He left the Shilü Collection.

sentences.zh: 與戴亨、長海為「遼東三老」。

translations.literal: Together with Dai Heng and Chang Hai he was called one of the "Three Elders of Liaodong."
translations.idiomatic: Together with Dai Heng and Chang Hai he was known as one of the "Three Elders of Liaodong."

sentences.zh: 亨，字通乾，號遂堂，瀋陽人，原籍錢塘。

translations.literal: Heng, styled Tongqian and sobriquet Suitang, was a man of Shenyang with original domicile in Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Heng, whose style was Tongqian and art name Suitang, was from Shenyang but originally registered in Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 父梓，以事戍遼，見藝術傳。

translations.literal: His father Zi was banished to Liaodong on account of an affair; see the Treatise on Arts.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zi was banished to Liaodong after an incident; see the Treatise on Arts.

sentences.zh: 亨，康熙六十年進士。

translations.literal: Heng became a metropolitan graduate in the sixtieth year of Kangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Heng passed the metropolitan examination in the sixtieth year of Kangxi.

sentences.zh: 官山東齊河縣知縣，以抗直忤上官，解組去。

translations.literal: He served as magistrate of Qihe County in Shandong; because of his upright bluntness he offended his superiors and resigned his seal and left.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Qihe County in Shandong, but his blunt integrity offended his superiors and he resigned.

sentences.zh: 寄居京師，家益貧，晏如也。

translations.literal: He lodged in the capital; his family grew ever poorer, yet he was serene.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in the capital as a guest; though his family grew ever poorer, he remained serene.

sentences.zh: 為人篤於至性，不輕然諾，夙敦風義。

translations.literal: As a man he was deeply rooted in true feeling, did not lightly give his word, and from early on honored righteousness and friendship.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply rooted in genuine feeling, he did not lightly give his word and had long honored loyalty and friendship.

sentences.zh: 其詩宗杜少陵，上溯漢、魏，卓然名家。

translations.literal: His poetry took Du Fu as its master, traced back to Han and Wei, and stood out as that of an established master.
translations.idiomatic: His poetry took Du Fu as its model, looked back to Han and Wei, and established him as a master in his own right.

sentences.zh: 有慶芝堂詩集。

translations.literal: He had the Collected Poems from the Hall of Celebrated Fungus.
translations.idiomatic: He left the Collected Poems from the Hall of Celebrated Fungus.

sentences.zh: 長海，字彙川，納喇氏，滿洲鑲白旗人，鎮安將軍瑪奇子。

translations.literal: Chang Hai, styled Huichuan, of the Nara clan, was a man of the Manchu Bordered White Banner and son of Zhen'an General Maqi.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Hai, whose style was Huichuan, was of the Nara clan, a member of the Manchu Bordered White Banner, and the son of Zhen'an General Maqi.

sentences.zh: 例予廕，長海不就。

translations.literal: By regulation he was granted hereditary office, but Chang Hai did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: By regulation he was granted hereditary office, but Chang Hai refused it.

sentences.zh: 檄補戶部庫使，又逃，曰：「庫使司帑藏，歲豐入，懼焉。

translations.literal: He was ordered by dispatch to fill the post of Ministry of Revenue treasury clerk, but fled again and said: "The treasury clerk manages the store of funds; when harvests are abundant and revenues pour in, I am afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered by dispatch to fill the post of Ministry of Revenue treasury clerk, he fled again and said, "The treasury clerk manages the store of funds; when harvests are abundant and revenues pour in, I am afraid.

sentences.zh: 逃死，非逃富貴也。」

translations.literal: To flee is to flee death, not to flee wealth and rank."
translations.idiomatic: I flee death, not wealth and rank."

sentences.zh: 其母賢，聽之，遂布衣終其身。

translations.literal: His mother was worthy and allowed it; he thus ended his life as a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: His worthy mother consented, and he lived out his life as a commoner.

sentences.zh: 衝遠任真，趣無容心。

translations.literal: Aloof and distant, he was true to himself, with no room in his disposition for calculation.
translations.idiomatic: Aloof and sincere by nature, he harbored no hidden designs.

sentences.zh: 博古多識，嗜金石書畫，當意則傾囊購之。

translations.literal: Broad in antiquarian learning and rich in knowledge, he loved bronzes, stones, books, and paintings; when something pleased him he emptied his purse to buy it.
translations.idiomatic: Erudite in antiquities, he loved bronzes, stones, books, and paintings and would empty his purse to buy anything that pleased him.

sentences.zh: 嘗襲裘行吊，解裘以濟戚喪。

translations.literal: Once, wearing a fur coat on his way to offer condolences, he took off the coat to aid a bereaved family.
translations.idiomatic: Once, wearing a fur coat on his way to offer condolences, he took off the coat to help a bereaved family.

sentences.zh: 歸塗見未見書，買之，复解其衣。

translations.literal: On the return journey he saw a book he had never seen before, bought it, and again took off his clothing.
translations.idiomatic: On the way home he came upon a book he had never seen, bought it, and again stripped off his clothing to pay for it.

sentences.zh: 由是中寒疾，乃夷然曰：「獲多矣！」

translations.literal: Thereupon he contracted a chill from the cold; he then said calmly: "I have gained much!"
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon contracted a chill from the cold and said calmly, "I have gained much!"

sentences.zh: 中歲愛易水雷溪之勝，築大★E5菴，因以為號。

translations.literal: In mid-life he came to love the scenery of the Yishui and Leixi region, built the Great Lei Hermitage, and took it as his style name.
translations.idiomatic: In mid-life he came to love the scenery of the Yishui and Leixi region, built the Great Lei Hermitage, and took it as his style name.

sentences.zh: 晚入京居委巷，又顏其閣曰「玉衡」，懸畫四壁，對之吟諷。

translations.literal: Late in life he entered the capital and lived in a narrow lane; he also inscribed his pavilion "Jade Measure" and hung paintings on all four walls, chanting and reciting before them.
translations.idiomatic: Late in life he moved to the capital and lived in a narrow lane; he named his studio Jade Measure, hung paintings on every wall, and chanted poetry before them.

sentences.zh: 其詩矩矱古人，而不膠於固，斷句尤冠絕一時。

translations.literal: His poetry took the ancients as its rule and measure, yet was not stuck in rigidity; his regulated couplets especially stood supreme in his age.
translations.idiomatic: His poetry took the ancients as its model without becoming rigid, and his regulated couplets were unmatched in his day.

sentences.zh: 論詩以性情為主，舉靡麗之習而空之。

translations.literal: In discussing poetry he took native disposition as the main thing and swept away the habit of ornate luxury.
translations.idiomatic: In his theory of poetry he held that genuine feeling should come first and rejected the habit of ornate display.

sentences.zh: 有雷溪草堂詩。

translations.literal: He had Poems from the Leixi Thatched Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He left Poems from the Leixi Thatched Hall.

sentences.zh: 乾隆九年，卒，年六十有七。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Qianlong he died, aged sixty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the ninth year of Qianlong, at the age of sixty-seven.

sentences.zh: 遼東以詩文名者，又有吳麟，字子瑞，號晚亭，滿洲鑲黃旗人。

translations.literal: Among those in Liaodong famed for poetry and prose there was also Wu Lin, styled Zirui and sobriquet Wanting, a man of the Manchu Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Among those in Liaodong famed for poetry and prose was Wu Lin, whose style was Zirui and art name Wanting, a member of the Manchu Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 康熙四十九年舉人，授內閣中書。

translations.literal: In the forty-ninth year of Kangxi he became a provincial graduate and was appointed Secretariat drafter.
translations.idiomatic: He became a provincial graduate in the forty-ninth year of Kangxi and was appointed a Secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 與鍇同舉鴻博，與修明史，纂本紀，充明史綱目纂修官。

translations.literal: Together with Kai he was nominated for the Hongbo examination; he joined in compiling the History of Ming, edited the basic annals, and served as compiler of the Outline of the History of Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Like Li Kai he was nominated for the erudition examination; he helped compile the History of Ming, edited the basic annals, and served as compiler of the Outline of the History of Ming.

sentences.zh: 善詩文，兼工山水。

translations.literal: He was skilled in poetry and prose and also accomplished in landscape painting.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled in poetry and prose and was also accomplished in landscape painting.

sentences.zh: 著有黍谷山房集。

translations.literal: He wrote the Taigu Mountain Studio Collection.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Taigu Mountain Studio Collection.

sentences.zh: 曹寅，字楝亭，漢軍正白旗人，世居瀋陽，工部尚書璽子。

translations.literal: Cao Yin, styled Lanting, was a man of the Han Eight Banners' Plain White Banner who for generations lived in Shenyang and was the son of Minister of Works Cao.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Yin, whose style was Lanting, was a member of the Han Eight Banners' Plain White Banner from a Shenyang family and was the son of Minister of Works Cao.

sentences.zh: 累官通政使、江寧織造。

translations.literal: He rose through offices to transmission commissioner and Jiangning textile commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to serve as transmission commissioner and Jiangning textile commissioner.

sentences.zh: 有楝亭詩文詞鈔。

translations.literal: He had the Lanting Collection of Poetry, Prose, and Lyrics.
translations.idiomatic: He left the Lanting Collection of Poetry, Prose, and Lyrics.

sentences.zh: 鮑珍，字冠亭，秘書院大學士鮑承先裔。

translations.literal: Bao Zhen, styled Guanting, was a descendant of Grand Secretary Bao Chengxian of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Zhen, whose style was Guanting, was a descendant of Grand Secretary Bao Chengxian of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 乾隆初，官嘉興海防同知。

translations.literal: Early in Qianlong he served as coastal defense subprefect of Jiaxing.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qianlong reign he served as coastal defense subprefect of Jiaxing.

sentences.zh: 有道腴堂全集。

translations.literal: He had the Complete Works from the Hall of the Way's Sustenance.
translations.idiomatic: He left the Complete Works from the Hall of the Way's Sustenance.

sentences.zh: 高鶚，字蘭墅，亦漢軍旗人。

translations.literal: Gao E, styled Lanshu, was also a man of the Han Eight Banners.
translations.idiomatic: Gao E, whose style was Lanshu, was also a member of the Han Eight Banners.

sentences.zh: 乾隆六十年進士。

translations.literal: In the sixtieth year of Qianlong he became a metropolitan graduate.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the sixtieth year of Qianlong.

sentences.zh: 有蘭墅詩鈔。

translations.literal: He had the Lanshu Collection of Poetry.
translations.idiomatic: He left the Lanshu Collection of Poetry.

sentences.zh: 至道光年則有劉文麟，字仙樵，遼陽人。

translations.literal: By the Daoguang reign there was Liu Wenlin, styled Xianqiao, a man of Liaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: By the Daoguang reign there was Liu Wenlin, whose style was Xianqiao, from Liaoyang.

sentences.zh: 九歲能詩。

translations.literal: At nine he could compose poetry.
translations.idiomatic: At nine he could already compose poetry.

sentences.zh: 以進士用廣東知縣，總督林則徐器之。

translations.literal: As a metropolitan graduate he was appointed magistrate in Guangdong; Governor-General Lin Zexu valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed a Guangdong county magistrate after passing the metropolitan examination, he was valued by Governor-General Lin Zexu.

sentences.zh: 權平遠，兼長樂。

translations.literal: He acted as magistrate of Pingyuan and concurrently of Changle.
translations.idiomatic: He served as acting magistrate of Pingyuan and concurrently of Changle.

sentences.zh: 俗悍，喜械鬥，文麟甫往任，單輿遽入解之，眾羅拜，皆釋兵，俗為之易。

translations.literal: The local custom was fierce; people loved armed brawls; as soon as Wenlin went to his post he entered alone in a single carriage to settle them; the crowd bowed in a ring, all laid down their weapons, and the custom thereby changed.
translations.idiomatic: The local people were fierce and prone to armed brawls; as soon as Wenlin took up his post he drove in alone to settle a fight; the crowd bowed before him, all laid down their weapons, and the local customs changed.

sentences.zh: 補文昌，丁憂。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Wenchang and then entered mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Wenchang and then entered mourning for a parent.

sentences.zh: 再選河南沈丘。

translations.literal: He was selected again for Shenqiu in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he was appointed to Shenqiu in Henan.

sentences.zh: 時患匪，設方略擒其渠，盜賊息跡。

translations.literal: At the time bandits were a problem; he devised plans and captured their ringleaders, and robbers ceased their activity.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the region suffered from banditry; he devised stratagems, captured the ringleaders, and banditry ceased.

sentences.zh: 以忤上官劾降，遂歸，主瀋陽書院。

translations.literal: Because he offended his superiors he was impeached and demoted; he then returned home and headed the Shenyang Academy.
translations.idiomatic: After offending his superiors he was impeached and demoted, returned home, and became director of the Shenyang Academy.

sentences.zh: 論詩以婉至為宗，語必有寄託。

translations.literal: In discussing poetry he took graceful perfection as his standard, and his words always bore some deeper meaning.
translations.idiomatic: In his poetic theory he made graceful perfection his ideal, and every line carried some deeper meaning.

sentences.zh: 英光偉氣，一發之於詩。

translations.literal: His noble brilliance and grand spirit he unleashed entirely in his poetry.
translations.idiomatic: His heroic brilliance and lofty spirit found their full expression in his poetry.

sentences.zh: 論者謂足繼遼東三老。

translations.literal: Critics said he fully inherited the tradition of the Three Elders of Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Critics held that he fully carried on the tradition of the Three Elders of Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 有仙樵詩鈔。

translations.literal: He had the Xianqiao Collection of Poetry.
translations.idiomatic: He left the Xianqiao Collection of Poetry.

sentences.zh: 其門人王乃新，字雪樵，承德人。

translations.literal: His disciple Wang Naixin, styled Xueqiao, was a man of Chengde.
translations.idiomatic: His disciple Wang Naixin, whose style was Xueqiao, came from Chengde.

sentences.zh: 亦能詩，有雪樵詩賸。

translations.literal: He could also compose poetry; he had the Xueqiao Leftover Poems.
translations.idiomatic: He too wrote poetry and left the Xueqiao Leftover Poems.

sentences.zh: 沈炳震，字東父，歸安人。

translations.literal: Shen Bingzhen, styled Dongfu, was a man of Guian.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Bingzhen, whose style was Dongfu, came from Guian.

sentences.zh: 少喜博覽，讀史於年月世系，人所忽者，必默識之。

translations.literal: From youth he loved wide reading; when reading history, in matters of dates and genealogies that others overlooked, he always committed them silently to memory.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he read widely; when studying history he silently memorized dates and genealogies that others passed over.

sentences.zh: 嘗著新舊唐書合鈔，紀傳以舊書為綱，分注新書為目；

translations.literal: He once compiled a Combined Transcription of the Old and New Books of Tang, taking the Old Book as the framework for annals and biographies and appending the New Book in notes;
translations.idiomatic: He compiled a Combined Transcription of the Old and New Books of Tang, using the Old Book as the main framework for biographies and annals with the New Book cited in marginal notes;

sentences.zh: 舊志多舛略，則以新書為綱，分注舊書為目。

translations.literal: Where the Old Book's treatises were full of errors and omissions, he took the New Book as the framework and appended the Old Book in notes.
translations.idiomatic: Where the Old Book's monographs were erroneous or incomplete, he reversed the arrangement, making the New Book the framework and citing the Old Book in notes.

sentences.zh: 又補列方鎮表，拜罷承襲諸節目，積數十寒暑乃成。

translations.literal: He also supplemented and compiled a table of military governors, covering appointments, dismissals, and succession in all its particulars—a work accumulated over many decades before it was finished.
translations.idiomatic: He also compiled a supplementary table of provincial military governors, recording appointments, removals, and successions in full; the work took decades to complete.

sentences.zh: 又著二十四史四譜：一紀元，二封爵，三宰執，四諡法。

translations.literal: He also wrote the Four Registers of the Twenty-Four Histories: first, reign eras; second, enfeoffments and titles; third, chief ministers; fourth, posthumous naming.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote the Four Registers of the Twenty-Four Histories, covering reign eras, enfeoffments and titles, chief ministers, and posthumous naming conventions.

sentences.zh: 其體出於表歷，而變其旁行斜上為標目。

translations.literal: Its form derived from calendar tables, but he changed the diagonal columns into headings.
translations.idiomatic: The format derived from calendrical tables, but he adapted the diagonal columns into section headings.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，與弟炳謙皆以貢生試鴻博，報罷。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong he and his younger brother Bingqian both took the erudition examination as provincial nominees, and both failed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qianlong he and his younger brother Bingqian both sat the erudition examination as provincial graduates, and both were rejected.

sentences.zh: 逾年，卒，年五十九。

translations.literal: The following year he died, aged fifty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he died at the age of fifty-nine.

sentences.zh: 卒後六年，侍郎錢陳群奏進其唐書合鈔，詔付書局，採錄唐書考證中。

translations.literal: Six years after his death, Vice Minister Qian Chenqun memorialized presenting his Combined Transcription of the Books of Tang; an edict ordered it sent to the imperial printing bureau and selections incorporated into Tang History Notes and Verification.
translations.idiomatic: Six years after his death, Vice Minister Qian Chenqun presented his Combined Transcription of the Books of Tang to the throne; the court ordered it sent to the imperial printing bureau and selections from it incorporated into Tang History Notes and Verification.

sentences.zh: 炳謙，字幼孜，炳震季弟也。

translations.literal: Bingqian, styled Youzi, was Bingzhen's youngest brother.
translations.idiomatic: Bingqian, whose style was Youzi, was Bingzhen's youngest brother.

sentences.zh: 次弟炳巽，字繹旃。

translations.literal: His next younger brother Bingxun, styled Yizhan.
translations.idiomatic: His next younger brother Bingxun was styled Yizhan.

sentences.zh: 著水經註集釋訂譌，據明黃省曾刊本，以己意校定之。

translations.literal: He wrote Collected Exegesis and Emendation of the Commentary on the Water Classic, basing it on Huang Shengzeng's Ming edition and correcting it according to his own judgment.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Collected Exegesis and Emendation of the Commentary on the Water Classic, working from Huang Shengzeng's Ming edition and revising it according to his own judgment.

sentences.zh: 遍檢古籍，錄其文字異同者，間附諸家考訂之說。

translations.literal: He searched exhaustively through ancient texts, recording textual variants, and occasionally appended the emendations of various scholars.
translations.idiomatic: He searched exhaustively through ancient texts, recording textual variants and occasionally appending emendations from other scholars.

sentences.zh: 州縣沿革，則悉以今名釋焉。

translations.literal: For the histories of prefectures and counties, he explained them all with present-day names.
translations.idiomatic: For changes in administrative units he consistently glossed place names with their modern equivalents.

sentences.zh: 初未見朱謀㙔本，後求得，多與之合。

translations.literal: At first he had not seen Zhu Miqian's edition; later, when he obtained it, his readings largely agreed with it.
translations.idiomatic: At first he had not seen Zhu Miqian's edition, but when he later obtained it he found that his readings largely agreed.

sentences.zh: 同時治水經者，有全祖望、趙一清。

translations.literal: Among those who at the same time worked on the Water Classic were Quan Zuwang and Zhao Yiqing.
translations.idiomatic: Others working on the Water Classic at the same time included Quan Zuwang and Zhao Yiqing.

sentences.zh: 一清，字誠夫，仁和人。

translations.literal: Yiqing, styled Chengfu, was a man of Renhe.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yiqing, whose style was Chengfu, came from Renhe.

sentences.zh: 國子監生。

translations.literal: A student of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He was a student of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 父昱，季父信，見厲鶚傳。

translations.literal: His father Yu and his youngest uncle Xin are mentioned in the biography of Li E.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yu and his youngest uncle Xin are discussed in the biography of Li E.

sentences.zh: 一清禀其家學，博極群書。

translations.literal: Yiqing inherited his family's learning and mastered a vast range of books.
translations.idiomatic: Yiqing inherited his family's scholarship and mastered an enormous range of books.

sentences.zh: 水經註傳寫訛奪，歐陽玄、王禕稱其經、注混淆，祖望又謂道元注中有注。

translations.literal: The Commentary on the Water Classic had suffered corruption in transmission; Ouyang Xuan and Wang Yi said its main text and commentary were confused, and Zuwang further said that within Li Daoyuan's commentary there were further layers of commentary.
translations.idiomatic: Textual corruption had blurred the main text and commentary of the Water Classic; Ouyang Xuan and Wang Yi noted that text and gloss were confused, and Quan Zuwang argued further that Li Daoyuan's commentary contained embedded notes within notes.

sentences.zh: 一清因從其說，辨驗文義，離析之，使文屬而語不雜。

translations.literal: Yiqing followed this view, examined the meaning of the text, separated the layers, so that the text belonged together and the language was not mixed.
translations.idiomatic: Yiqing adopted this view, verified the sense of the text, and separated the layers so that the main text cohered and the language was no longer mixed.

sentences.zh: 又唐六典注稱桑欽所引天下之水百三十七，江、河在焉，今少二十一水。

translations.literal: Moreover, the Tang Six Offices Commentary notes that Sang Qin cited one hundred thirty-seven rivers under Heaven, including the Yangtze and Yellow River, but the present text lacks twenty-one rivers.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang Six Offices Commentary states that Sang Qin cited 137 rivers throughout the realm, including the Yangtze and Yellow River, but the present text is short by twenty-one rivers.

sentences.zh: 考崇文總目，水經註三十六卷，蓋宋代已佚其五卷。

translations.literal: Examining the Comprehensive Catalog of the Chongwen Pavilion, the Commentary on the Water Classic originally had thirty-six scrolls; probably five scrolls had already been lost by the Song dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: According to the Comprehensive Catalog of the Chongwen Pavilion, the Commentary on the Water Classic ran to thirty-six scrolls; five scrolls had probably already been lost by Song times.

sentences.zh: 此二十一水，即在所佚中。

translations.literal: These twenty-one rivers were among the lost portions.
translations.idiomatic: These twenty-one missing rivers belonged to the lost portions.

sentences.zh: 於是雜採他書，證以本注，得滏、洺等十八水。

translations.literal: He then gathered materials from other books and verified them against the original commentary, recovering eighteen rivers such as the Fu and Ming.
translations.idiomatic: He then drew on other sources and checked them against the original commentary, recovering eighteen rivers including the Fu and Ming.

sentences.zh: 又分㶟水、㶟餘水，清、濁漳，大小遼水，增多二十一，與六典注合。

translations.literal: He further separated the Huo River and Huoyu River, the Clear and Muddy Zhang Rivers, and the Greater and Lesser Liao Rivers, thereby restoring all twenty-one rivers and matching the Six Offices Commentary.
translations.idiomatic: By further separating the Huo and Huoyu rivers, the Clear and Muddy Zhang rivers, and the Greater and Lesser Liao rivers, he accounted for all twenty-one missing rivers in accord with the Six Offices Commentary.

sentences.zh: 為水經註釋，又成水經箋刊誤，以正朱謀㙔之失。

translations.literal: He wrote a Commentary on the Water Classic Notes, and also completed textual notes and corrections to restore what Zhu Miqian had gotten wrong.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote his Commentary on the Water Classic and also completed Exegetical Corrections to the Water Classic to rectify Zhu Miqian's errors.

sentences.zh: 方觀承督直隸，撰直隸河渠志，一清所草創，而戴震要刪之。

translations.literal: When Fang Guancheng supervised Zhili he compiled the Zhili River Conservancy Gazetteer, which Yiqing first drafted but which Dai Zhen insisted on drastically cutting.
translations.idiomatic: When Fang Guancheng served as governor-general of Zhili he compiled the Zhili River Conservancy Gazetteer; Yiqing drafted it, but Dai Zhen insisted on cutting much of it.

sentences.zh: 其自著有東潛文集。

translations.literal: His own writings included the Dongqian Collection.
translations.idiomatic: Among his own works was the Dongqian Collection.

sentences.zh: 曹仁虎，字來殷，嘉定人。

translations.literal: Cao Renhu, styled Laiyin, was a man of Jiading.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Renhu, whose style was Laiyin, came from Jiading.

sentences.zh: 少稱奇才。

translations.literal: In youth he was famed as a prodigy.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was acclaimed as a prodigy.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二十二年，南巡，獻賦，召試列一等，賜舉人，授內閣中書。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year of Qianlong, during the southern tour, he submitted a fu; called to examination he placed in the first class, was granted the rank of provincial graduate, and appointed a Secretariat drafter.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year of Qianlong, during the southern tour, he submitted a fu; at the imperial examination he placed first class, was granted the rank of provincial graduate, and appointed a Secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，成進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year he passed the metropolitan examination, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 每遇大禮，高文典冊，多出其手。

translations.literal: Whenever great ceremonial occasions arose, the lofty documents and classic protocols were mostly written by his hand.
translations.idiomatic: On every great ceremonial occasion the lofty state documents were largely drafted by his hand.

sentences.zh: 擢右中允，充日講起居注官，累遷侍講學士。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Right Sub-Reader, served as diarist of the emperor's lectures and daily conduct, and was progressively advanced to Reader-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Right Sub-Reader, served as diarist of the imperial lectures, and was promoted in due course to Reader-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 五十一年，視學粵東。

translations.literal: In the fifty-first year he served as educational commissioner in eastern Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-first year he served as educational intendant in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 方按試連州，聞母訃，酷暑奔喪，晝夜號泣，竟以毀，卒於途。

translations.literal: While conducting examinations at Lianzhou he heard his mother's death notice; amid the summer heat he rushed home in mourning, weeping day and night, and at last died from grief on the journey.
translations.idiomatic: While conducting examinations at Lianzhou he received word of his mother's death; he raced home through the midsummer heat, weeping day and night, and ultimately died of grief on the road.

sentences.zh: 仁虎以文字受主知，聲華冠都下，屢典文衡。

translations.literal: Renhu won the emperor's favor through his writing; his fame topped the capital, and he repeatedly presided over literary examinations.
translations.idiomatic: Renhu won imperial favor through his literary talent; his reputation stood foremost in the capital, and he repeatedly served as chief literary examiner.

sentences.zh: 詩宗三唐，而神明變化，一洗粗率佻巧之習。

translations.literal: In poetry he took the Three Tang as his masters, yet with inspired transformation he entirely washed away crude, careless, and frivolously clever habits.
translations.idiomatic: In poetry he followed the Three Tang masters yet infused his work with inspired transformation, entirely shedding the habits of crudeness, carelessness, and facile cleverness.

sentences.zh: 格律醇雅，醖釀深厚，為一時所推。

translations.literal: His metrical rules were refined and elegant, his flavor deep and rich; he was admired by the age.
translations.idiomatic: His metrical craft was refined and elegant and his style richly matured; he was acclaimed by his age.

sentences.zh: 著有宛委山房詩集、蓉鏡堂文稿。

translations.literal: He wrote the Wanwei Mountain Studio Poetry Collection and the Rongjing Hall Drafts.
translations.idiomatic: He authored the Wanwei Mountain Studio Poetry Collection and the Rongjing Hall Drafts.

sentences.zh: 與王鳴盛、王昶、錢大昕、趙文哲及吳泰來、黃文蓮稱「吳中七子」。

translations.literal: Together with Wang Mingsheng, Wang Chang, Qian Daxin, and Zhao Wenzhe, as well as Wu Tailai and Huang Wenlian, he was called the Seven Masters of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Wang Mingsheng, Wang Chang, Qian Daxin, Zhao Wenzhe, Wu Tailai, and Huang Wenlian he was known as the Seven Masters of Wu.

sentences.zh: 鳴盛等四人皆自有傳。

translations.literal: Mingsheng and the other three each have their own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Mingsheng and the other three each have biographies elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 泰來，字企晉，長洲人。

translations.literal: Tailai, styled Qijin, was a man of Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Tailai, whose style was Qijin, came from Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二十五年進士，用內閣中書。

translations.literal: A jinshi graduate in the twenty-fifth year of Qianlong, he served as a Secretariat drafter.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the metropolitan examination in the twenty-fifth year of Qianlong he served as a Secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 乞病歸，築遂初園於木瀆。

translations.literal: He begged leave on grounds of illness and returned home, building the Suichu Garden at Mudu.
translations.idiomatic: He requested leave on grounds of illness and returned home, where he built the Suichu Garden at Mudu.

sentences.zh: 藏書多宋、元善本。

translations.literal: His library held many fine Song and Yuan editions.
translations.idiomatic: His library contained many fine Song and Yuan editions.

sentences.zh: 畢沅延主關中及大樑書院，與洪亮吉輩往還唱和。

translations.literal: Bi Yuan invited him to head the Guanzhong and Daliang academies, and he exchanged poems with Hong Liangji and others.
translations.idiomatic: Bi Yuan invited him to direct the Guanzhong and Daliang academies, where he exchanged poems with Hong Liangji and others.

sentences.zh: 其詩一本漁洋，著有淨名軒、硯山堂等集。

translations.literal: His poetry wholly followed Wang Shizhen; he wrote the Jingming Studio and Yanshan Hall collections, among others.
translations.idiomatic: His poetry wholly followed Wang Shizhen's example; he authored the Jingming Studio and Yanshan Hall collections, among others.

sentences.zh: 文蓮，字芳亭，上海人。

translations.literal: Wenlian, styled Fangting, was a man of Shanghai.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Wenlian, whose style was Fangting, came from Shanghai.

sentences.zh: 官知縣，有聽雨集。

translations.literal: He served as a county magistrate; he had the Listening to Rain Collection.
translations.idiomatic: He served as a county magistrate and left the Listening to Rain Collection.

sentences.zh: 胡天游，字稚威，山陰人，初姓方，名游。

translations.literal: Hu Tianyou, styled Zhiwei, was a man of Shanyin; his original surname was Fang and his given name You.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Tianyou, whose style was Zhiwei, came from Shanyin; he was originally surnamed Fang with the given name You.

sentences.zh: 副榜貢生。

translations.literal: A provincial graduate from the supplementary jinshi list.
translations.idiomatic: He was a provincial graduate placed on the supplementary jinshi list.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，尚書任蘭枝薦舉鴻博，次年補試，鼻衄大作，投卷出。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong Minister Ren Lanzhi recommended him for the erudition examination; the following year at the supplementary examination a severe nosebleed struck him and he handed in his paper and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qianlong Minister Ren Lanzhi recommended him for the erudition examination; at the supplementary test the following year he suffered a severe nosebleed, submitted his paper, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 時四方文士云集京師，每置酒高會，分題命賦，天游輒出數千言，沉博絕麗，見者咸驚服。

translations.literal: At the time literary men from all quarters gathered in the capital; at each grand banquet they would assign topics and demand compositions, and Tianyou would produce several thousand characters—profound, encyclopedic, and surpassingly beautiful—astonishing all who saw them.
translations.idiomatic: Literary men from across the realm had gathered in the capital; at every grand gathering topics were assigned and compositions demanded, and Tianyou would produce thousands of characters—profound, encyclopedic, and surpassingly beautiful—leaving all who read them in awe.

sentences.zh: 性耿介，公卿欲招致一見，不可得。

translations.literal: By nature he was upright and unyielding; when high officials wished to summon him even for a single meeting, they could not obtain it.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was upright and unyielding; even when high officials wished to summon him for a single meeting, they could not obtain an audience.

sentences.zh: 後舉經學，再報罷。

translations.literal: Later he was nominated for the classical learning examination, but failed twice.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was twice nominated for the classical learning examination and twice rejected.

sentences.zh: 客山西，卒。

translations.literal: As a guest in Shanxi he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died while sojourning in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 著有石笥山房集。

translations.literal: He wrote the Shixiang Mountain Studio Collection.
translations.idiomatic: He left the Shixiang Mountain Studio Collection.

sentences.zh: 自言古文學韓愈，然往往澀險似劉蛻，非其至也。

translations.literal: He said himself that in ancient prose he studied Han Yu, yet often it was cramped and difficult like Liu Tui's—not his highest attainment.
translations.idiomatic: He claimed to study Han Yu in ancient prose, yet his writing often tended toward the cramped and difficult style of Liu Tui—not his highest attainment.

sentences.zh: 儷體文自三唐而下，日趨頹靡。

translations.literal: Parallel prose from the Three Tang downward daily grew more decadent.
