translations.idiomatic: Parallel prose from the Three Tang period onward had daily grown more decadent.

sentences.zh: 清初陳維崧、毛奇齡稍振起之，至天游奧衍入古，遂臻極盛。

translations.literal: Early in the Qing Chen Weisong and Mao Qiling slightly revived it; by Tianyou's recondite expansiveness and penetration into antiquity it reached the height of prosperity.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qing Chen Weisong and Mao Qiling had partly revived it; with Tianyou's recondite breadth and antiquarian depth parallel prose reached its peak.

sentences.zh: 而邵齊燾、孔廣森、洪亮吉輩繼起，才力所至，皆足名家。

translations.literal: Then Shao Qidao, Kong Guangsen, Hong Liangji, and others rose in succession; wherever their talent reached, each was sufficient to found a school.
translations.idiomatic: Then Shao Qidao, Kong Guangsen, Hong Liangji, and others arose in turn; each wielded talent sufficient to establish a distinct school.

sentences.zh: 後數十年而有鎮洋彭兆蓀，以選聲鍊色勝，名重一時。

translations.literal: Several decades later there was Peng Zhaosun of Zhenyang, who excelled in choosing sounds and refining hues, and his fame weighed heavy for a time.
translations.idiomatic: Several decades later came Peng Zhaosun of Zhenyang, who excelled in refining diction and polishing imagery, and for a time his reputation stood very high.

sentences.zh: 兆蓀，字湘涵。

translations.literal: Zhaosun, styled Xianghan.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Zhaosun was styled Xianghan.

sentences.zh: 少有才名，久困無所遇。

translations.literal: From youth he had a reputation for talent, but long remained in hardship without meeting opportunity.
translations.idiomatic: He enjoyed a reputation for talent from youth, but long remained in obscurity without advancement.

sentences.zh: 舉道光元年孝廉方正。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daoguang he passed the Filial and Incorrupt Recommended Scholars examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the Filial and Incorrupt Recommended Scholars examination in the first year of Daoguang.

sentences.zh: 胡克家為江蘇布政使，客其所。

translations.literal: When Hu Kejia was financial commissioner of Jiangsu, Zhaosun was his guest.
translations.idiomatic: When Hu Kejia served as Jiangsu financial commissioner, Zhaosun lodged at his residence.

sentences.zh: 時總督以國用不足議加賦，兆蓀為克家力陳其不可，事得寢。

translations.literal: At the time the governor-general, citing insufficient state revenue, proposed raising taxes; Zhaosun vigorously argued to Kejia that this was impossible, and the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: When the governor-general proposed raising taxes because state revenue was insufficient, Zhaosun forcefully argued to Kejia that this must not be done, and the proposal was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 又偕顧廣圻同校元本通鑑及文選，世稱其精槧。

translations.literal: He also joined Gu Guangqi in collating Yuan editions of the Comprehensive Mirror and the Literary Selections; the age praised their exquisite proofreading.
translations.idiomatic: He also collaborated with Gu Guangqi in collating Yuan editions of the Comprehensive Mirror and the Literary Selections; contemporaries praised their exacting editorial work.

sentences.zh: 晚依曾燠兩淮鹽運使署。

translations.literal: In his later years he relied on Zeng Ao at the salt transport commissioner's office of the Two Huai circuits.
translations.idiomatic: In later years he relied on Zeng Ao at the Two Huai salt transport commissioner's office.

sentences.zh: 著小謨觴館集，燠為點定之。

translations.literal: He wrote the Little Modang Hall Collection, which Ao revised and finalized.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Little Modang Hall Collection, which Zeng Ao edited and finalized.

sentences.zh: 天才穎異。

translations.literal: His native talent was brilliant and extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: His native talent was brilliant and extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 論詩主抒寫性靈，他人意所欲出，不達者悉為達之。

translations.literal: In discussing poetry he upheld the expression of one's inner spirit; what others wished to express but could not, he fully expressed for them.
translations.idiomatic: In poetic theory he upheld the expression of inner spirit; he could articulate what others wished to say but could not.

sentences.zh: 士多效其體。

translations.literal: Many scholars imitated his style.
translations.idiomatic: Many scholars imitated his style.

sentences.zh: 著，凡三十餘種。

translations.literal: His authored works numbered more than thirty kinds in all.
translations.idiomatic: He published more than thirty works in all.

sentences.zh: 上自公卿下至市井負販，皆知其名。

translations.literal: From high officials down to market peddlers, all knew his name.
translations.idiomatic: From high officials down to street peddlers, everyone knew his name.

sentences.zh: 海外有來求其書者。

translations.literal: From overseas there were those who came seeking his books.
translations.idiomatic: People even came from overseas seeking his books.

sentences.zh: 然喜聲色，其所作亦頗以滑易獲世譏云。

translations.literal: Yet he delighted in music and women, and his writings also rather earned worldly censure for their smoothness and ease.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he delighted in sensual pleasures, and his writings also drew worldly censure for their smoothness and ease.

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十二。

translations.literal: He died, aged eighty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of eighty-two.

sentences.zh: 兄，字。

translations.literal: His elder brother Wen'an, styled Haibai.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Wen'an, whose style was Haibai.

sentences.zh: 舉人。

translations.literal: A provincial graduate.
translations.idiomatic: He was a provincial graduate.

sentences.zh: 家居奉母，淡於榮利。

translations.literal: He lived at home serving his mother and was indifferent to fame and profit.
translations.idiomatic: He lived at home caring for his mother and was indifferent to fame and profit.

sentences.zh: 其詩才超逸，與有二難之目。

translations.literal: His poetic talent was transcendent; together with Wentao they had the designation of the Two Excellences.
translations.idiomatic: His poetic talent was transcendent; he and Wentao were styled the Two Excellences.

sentences.zh: 王又曾，字受銘，秀水人。

translations.literal: Wang Youceng, styled Shouming, was a man of Xiushui.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Youceng, whose style was Shouming, came from Xiushui.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十六年，南巡召試，賜舉人，授內閣中書。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Qianlong, during the southern tour he was called to examination, granted the rank of provincial graduate, and appointed a Secretariat drafter.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year of Qianlong, during the southern tour he was called to imperial examination, granted the rank of provincial graduate, and appointed a Secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 十九年，成進士，授刑部主事。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed a principal secretary in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he passed the metropolitan examination and was appointed a principal secretary in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 同縣錢載論詩宗黃庭堅，務縋深鑿險，不墮臼科。

translations.literal: Qian Zai of the same county, in discussing poetry, took Huang Tingjian as his master, striving to plumb depth and carve difficulty, and not falling into ruts.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Zai of the same county took Huang Tingjian as his model in poetry, striving to plumb depth and carve out difficulty without falling into conventional patterns.

sentences.zh: 又曾與朱沛然、陳向中、祝維誥和之，號「南郭五子」。

translations.literal: Youceng joined Zhu Peiran, Chen Xiangzhong, and Zhu Weigao in harmonizing with him, and they were called the Five Masters of Nanguo.
translations.idiomatic: Youceng joined Zhu Peiran, Chen Xiangzhong, and Zhu Weigao in a poetic fellowship with Qian Zai, and they styled themselves the Five Masters of Nanguo.

sentences.zh: 又有萬光泰、汪孟鋗、仲鈖皆與同時相鏃礪，力求捐棄塵壒，毋一語相襲取。

translations.literal: There were also Wan Guangtai, Wang Mengjun, and Zhong Chen, all sharpening one another at the same time, striving to cast off worldly dust, and never allowing a single line to be borrowed from another.
translations.idiomatic: Wan Guangtai, Wang Mengjun, and Zhong Chen were also their contemporaries; they honed one another's work, striving to cast off worldly vulgarity and never permitting a line to be borrowed from another poet.

sentences.zh: 為詩不異指趣，亦不同體格。

translations.literal: In composing poetry they did not differ in aim and direction, yet their forms and styles also differed.
translations.idiomatic: In poetry they shared the same aims, yet each cultivated a distinct form and style.

sentences.zh: 時目為秀水派，而又曾與維誥、光泰尤工。

translations.literal: At the time they were regarded as the Xiushui School; Youceng together with Weigao and Guangtai were especially accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: They were regarded at the time as the Xiushui school; among them, Youceng together with Weigao and Guangtai were especially accomplished.

sentences.zh: 又曾卒，其子復乞載定其詩，號丁辛老屋集。

translations.literal: When Youceng died, his son Fu asked Zai to revise and finalize his poems, titled the Dingxin Old House Collection.
translations.idiomatic: When Youceng died, his son Fu asked Qian Zai to revise and finalize his poems, which were published as the Dingxin Old House Collection.

sentences.zh: 畢沅為之序，謂於漢、魏、六朝及唐、宋諸家外，能融會變化自成一家，取材於眾所不經見，用意於前人所未發，尤又曾所獨到云。

translations.literal: Bi Yuan wrote a preface for it, saying that beyond the masters of Han, Wei, the Six Dynasties, and Tang and Song, he could merge and transform influences into a school of his own, drawing material rarely seen by others and putting intentions that predecessors had not developed—especially Youceng's unique attainments.
translations.idiomatic: Bi Yuan wrote a preface for it, saying that beyond the masters of Han, Wei, the Six Dynasties, and Tang and Song, Youceng could merge and transform influences into a school of his own, drawing on material rarely seen by others and pursuing intentions that predecessors had never developed—an achievement unique to Youceng.

sentences.zh: 維誥，字宣臣。

translations.literal: Weigao, styled Xuanchen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Weigao, whose style was Xuanchen.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三年舉人，官內閣中書。

translations.literal: A provincial graduate in the third year of Qianlong; he served as a Secretariat drafter.
translations.idiomatic: He became a provincial graduate in the third year of Qianlong and served as a Secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 有綠谿詩鈔。

translations.literal: He had the Green Stream Poetry Drafts.
translations.idiomatic: He published the Green Stream Poetry Drafts.

sentences.zh: 光泰，字循初。

translations.literal: Guangtai, styled Xunchu.
translations.idiomatic: Wan Guangtai, whose style was Xunchu.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年舉人。

translations.literal: A provincial graduate in the first year of Qianlong.
translations.idiomatic: He became a provincial graduate in the first year of Qianlong.

sentences.zh: 有柘坡居士集。

translations.literal: He had the Zhepo Hermit Collection.
translations.idiomatic: He published the Zhepo Hermit Collection.

sentences.zh: 維誥詩，全祖望稱其俊雅，李鍇稱其醇靜。

translations.literal: Of Weigao's poetry, Quan Zuwang praised its refined elegance, and Li Kai praised its mellow stillness.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Zuwang praised Weigao's poetry for its refined elegance, and Li Kai praised it for its mellow stillness.

sentences.zh: 光泰詩，杭世駿稱其秀朗，載亦稱其綺麗。

translations.literal: Of Guangtai's poetry, Hang Shijun praised its graceful clarity, and Zai also praised its exquisite beauty.
translations.idiomatic: Hang Shijun praised Guangtai's poetry for its graceful clarity, and Qian Zai also praised its exquisite beauty.

sentences.zh: 蓋雖宗庭堅，而鍛鍊精到，絕無西江槎枒詰屈之習。

translations.literal: For although they took Huang Tingjian as their master, their forging was precise and thorough, entirely without the knotty and contorted habits of the Xijiang school.
translations.idiomatic: For although they took Huang Tingjian as their model, their craftsmanship was precise and thorough, entirely free of the knotty, contorted manner of the Xijiang school.

sentences.zh: 沛然，舉人，知高安縣，卒官。

translations.literal: Peiran was a provincial graduate, served as magistrate of Gao'an County, and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Peiran was a provincial graduate who served as magistrate of Gao'an County and died in office.

sentences.zh: 向中客死涼州，詩傳者差少。

translations.literal: Xiangzhong died abroad at Liangzhou; comparatively few of his poems have been transmitted.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xiangzhong died abroad in Liangzhou; comparatively few of his poems survive.

sentences.zh: 孟鋗，進士，吏部主事；

translations.literal: Mengjun was a jinshi and a principal secretary in the Ministry of Personnel;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mengjun was a jinshi and a principal secretary in the Ministry of Personnel;

sentences.zh: 仲鈖，舉人：皆有集。

translations.literal: Zhong Chen was a provincial graduate: both had collections.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Chen was a provincial graduate: both had published collections.

sentences.zh: 而復與載子世錫，維誥子喆相與稱。

translations.literal: Fu joined in mutual acclaim with Zai's son Shi Xi and Weigao's son Zhe.
translations.idiomatic: Fu exchanged mutual acclaim with Qian Zai's son Shi Xi and Zhu Weigao's son Zhe.

sentences.zh: 詩守家法。

translations.literal: Their poetry kept to the family tradition.
translations.idiomatic: Their poetry adhered to the family tradition.

sentences.zh: 世錫已見載傳，有麂山老屋集。

translations.literal: Shi Xi has already appeared in Zai's biography; he had the Jishan Old House Collection.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xi has already appeared in Qian Zai's biography; he published the Jishan Old House Collection.

sentences.zh: 復，字敦初。

translations.literal: Fu, styled Dunchu.
translations.idiomatic: Fu, whose style was Dunchu.

sentences.zh: 官河南鄢陵知縣。

translations.literal: He served as magistrate of Yanling in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Yanling in Henan.

sentences.zh: 有樹萱堂、晚晴軒二集。

translations.literal: He had two collections: Shuxuan Hall and Wanqing Studio.
translations.idiomatic: He published two collections: the Shuxuan Hall and Wanqing Studio collections.

sentences.zh: 沅採入吳會英才集。

translations.literal: Yuan included him in the Wu-Hui Talents Collection.
translations.idiomatic: Bi Yuan included him in the Wu-Hui Talents Collection.

sentences.zh: 喆，字明甫。

translations.literal: Zhe, styled Mingfu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhe, whose style was Mingfu.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二十五年舉人。

translations.literal: A provincial graduate in the twenty-fifth year of Qianlong.
translations.idiomatic: He became a provincial graduate in the twenty-fifth year of Qianlong.

sentences.zh: 有西澗詩鈔。

translations.literal: He had the West Brook Poetry Drafts.
translations.idiomatic: He published the West Brook Poetry Drafts.

sentences.zh: 孟鋗子如洋，乾隆四十五年會試，廷試皆第一，亦與復等唱和。

translations.literal: Mengjun's son Ruyang ranked first in both the metropolitan and palace examinations in the forty-fifth year of Qianlong; he also exchanged poems with Fu and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Mengjun's son Ruyang ranked first in both the metropolitan and palace examinations in the forty-fifth year of Qianlong and also exchanged poems with Fu and the others.

sentences.zh: 邵齊燾，字叔宀，昭文人。

translations.literal: Shao Qidao, styled Shujun, was a man of Zhaowen.
translations.idiomatic: Shao Qidao, whose style was Shujun, came from Zhaowen.

sentences.zh: 幼異敏，甫受書即能了大義。

translations.literal: As a child he was unusually quick and keen; as soon as he began reading texts he could grasp their essential meaning.
translations.idiomatic: As a child he was unusually quick and keen; as soon as he began reading texts he could grasp their essential meaning.

sentences.zh: 乾隆七年進士，以編修居詞館十年。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the seventh year of Qianlong, he served as compiler in the Hanlin Academy for ten years.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in the seventh year of Qianlong and served as a compiler in the Hanlin Academy for ten years.

sentences.zh: 嘗獻東巡頌，時稱班、揚之亞，群公爭欲致門下。

translations.literal: He once submitted an Eastern Tour Eulogy; contemporaries called him second only to Ban and Yang, and leading men all vied to bring him into their circles.
translations.idiomatic: He once submitted an Eastern Tour Eulogy; contemporaries ranked him second only to Ban Gu and Yang Xiong, and leading men all vied to bring him into their circles.

sentences.zh: 齊燾意度夷曠，殊落落也。

translations.literal: Qidao's bearing was free and unconstrained—utterly detached.
translations.idiomatic: Qidao's bearing was free and unconstrained—utterly detached.

sentences.zh: 年三十六，即罷歸。

translations.literal: At the age of thirty-six he resigned and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: At the age of thirty-six he resigned and returned home.

sentences.zh: 自顏其室曰「道山祿隱」。

translations.literal: He inscribed his study with the name "Salary-and-Retirement on Dao Mountain."
translations.idiomatic: He inscribed his study with the name "Salary-and-Retirement on Dao Mountain."

sentences.zh: 主常州龍城書院，洪亮吉、黃景仁皆從受學。

translations.literal: He headed the Longcheng Academy in Changzhou; Hong Liangji and Huang Jingren both studied under him.
translations.idiomatic: He headed the Longcheng Academy in Changzhou; Hong Liangji and Huang Jingren both studied under him.

sentences.zh: 善為儷體文，氣格排奡，意欲矯陳維崧、吳綺、章藻功三家之失。

translations.literal: He excelled at parallel prose; his force and style were bold and sweeping, and he intended to correct the faults of the three masters Chen Weisong, Wu Qi, and Zhang Zaogong.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at parallel prose; his force and style were bold and sweeping, and he intended to correct the faults of Chen Weisong, Wu Qi, and Zhang Zaogong.

sentences.zh: 卒，年五十有二。

translations.literal: He died, aged fifty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of fifty-two.

sentences.zh: 著玉芝堂集。

translations.literal: He authored the Yuzhi Hall Collection.
translations.idiomatic: He authored the Yuzhi Hall Collection.

sentences.zh: 王太岳，字基平，定興人。

translations.literal: Wang Taiyue, styled Jiping, was a man of Dingxing.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Taiyue, whose style was Jiping, came from Dingxing.

sentences.zh: 齊燾同年進士，授檢討。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the same year as Qidao, he was appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi in the same year as Qidao, he was appointed reviser.

sentences.zh: 由侍讀出補甘肅平慶道，調西安，遷湖南按察使。

translations.literal: From Reader he went out to serve as intendant of Ping-Qing circuit in Gansu, was transferred to Xi'an, and was promoted to Hunan surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Leaving his post as Reader, he served as intendant of Ping-Qing circuit in Gansu, was transferred to Xi'an, and was promoted to Hunan surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 調雲南，擢布政使，坐事落職。

translations.literal: Transferred to Yunnan, he was promoted to provincial administration commissioner, then was dismissed from office for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Yunnan, he was promoted to provincial administration commissioner, then was dismissed from office for an offense.

sentences.zh: 命充四庫館總纂官。

translations.literal: He was ordered to serve as chief compiler at the Siku Library.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to serve as chief compiler at the Siku Library.

sentences.zh: 四十三年，仍授檢討。

translations.literal: In the forty-third year he was again appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-third year of Qianlong he was again appointed reviser.

sentences.zh: 後遷司業，卒。

translations.literal: Later he was promoted to Vice Director of the Imperial College, then died.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was promoted to Vice Director of the Imperial College, then died.

sentences.zh: 太岳蒞官有惠政，尤留心水利，與齊燾最善，駢文清剛簡直亦相近。

translations.literal: Taiyue's governance was marked by benevolent policies; he was especially attentive to waterworks. He was closest to Qidao, and his parallel prose likewise shared a clear, firm, and straightforward quality.
translations.idiomatic: Taiyue's governance was marked by benevolent policies, and he was especially attentive to waterworks. He was closest to Qidao, and his parallel prose likewise shared a clear, firm, and straightforward quality.

sentences.zh: 有清虛山房集。

translations.literal: He had the Clear Void Mountain Studio Collection.
translations.idiomatic: He published the Clear Void Mountain Studio Collection.

sentences.zh: 吳錫麒，字穀人，錢塘人。

translations.literal: Wu Xiqi, styled Guren, was a man of Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xiqi, whose style was Guren, came from Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 性至孝。

translations.literal: By nature he was deeply filial.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was deeply filial.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四十年進士，授編修。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the fortieth year of Qianlong, he was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in the fortieth year of Qianlong and was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 累遷祭酒，以親老乞養歸。

translations.literal: He rose successively to Grand Master of the Imperial Academy; when his parents aged he requested leave to retire and care for them.
translations.idiomatic: He rose successively to Grand Master of the Imperial Academy; when his parents grew old he requested leave to retire and care for them.

sentences.zh: 主講揚州安定樂儀書院。

translations.literal: He lectured at the Anding Leyi Academy in Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served as lecturer at the Anding Leyi Academy in Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 錫麒工應制詩文，兼善倚聲。

translations.literal: Xiqi was skilled at court-style poetry and prose and also excelled at lyric poetry.
translations.idiomatic: Xiqi was skilled at court-style poetry and prose and also excelled at lyric poetry.

sentences.zh: 浙中詩派，前有朱彝尊、查慎行，繼之者杭世駿、厲鶚。

translations.literal: In the Zhejiang poetry tradition, Zhu Yizun and Zha Shenxing came first; Hang Shijun and Li E followed them.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhejiang poetry tradition, Zhu Yizun and Zha Shenxing came first; Hang Shijun and Li E followed them.

sentences.zh: 二人殂謝後，推錫麒，藝林奉為圭臬焉。

translations.literal: After the two men passed away, Xiqi was upheld; the world of letters revered him as the standard.
translations.idiomatic: After the two men passed away, Xiqi was upheld as their successor, and the world of letters revered him as the standard.

sentences.zh: 著有正山房集。

translations.literal: He authored the Zheng Mountain Studio Collection.
translations.idiomatic: He authored the Zheng Mountain Studio Collection.

sentences.zh: 全椒吳鼒嘗輯錄齊燾、亮吉、錫麒及劉星煒、袁枚、孫星衍、孔廣森、曾燠之文為八家四六雲。

translations.literal: Wu Zi of Quanjiao once compiled the prose of Qidao, Liangji, Xiqi, Liu Xingwei, Yuan Mei, Sun Xingyan, Kong Guangsen, and Zeng Ao into the Eight Masters' Parallel-Prose Collection.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zi of Quanjiao once compiled the prose of Qidao, Liangji, Xiqi, Liu Xingwei, Yuan Mei, Sun Xingyan, Kong Guangsen, and Zeng Ao into the Eight Masters' Parallel-Prose Collection.

sentences.zh: 此八家​​外，有金匱楊芳燦，與弟揆並負時名。

translations.literal: Beyond these eight masters, there was Yang Fangcan of Jin Gui, who together with his younger brother Kui both enjoyed renown in their day.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond these eight masters, there was Yang Fangcan of Jin Gui, who together with his younger brother Kui both enjoyed renown in their day.

sentences.zh: 芳燦，字蓉裳。

translations.literal: Fangcan, styled Rongshang.
translations.idiomatic: Fangcan, whose style was Rongshang.

sentences.zh: 母夢五色雀集庭樹而生。

translations.literal: His mother dreamed of a five-colored bird alighting on the courtyard tree before she gave birth to him.
translations.idiomatic: His mother dreamed of a five-colored bird alighting on the courtyard tree before she gave birth to him.

sentences.zh: 詩文華贍，學使彭元瑞大異之。

translations.literal: His poetry and prose were splendidly rich; educational commissioner Peng Yuanrui was greatly impressed.
translations.idiomatic: His poetry and prose were splendidly rich; educational commissioner Peng Yuanrui was greatly impressed.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四十二年拔貢生。

translations.literal: A selected tribute student in the forty-second year of Qianlong.
translations.idiomatic: He became a selected tribute student in the forty-second year of Qianlong.

sentences.zh: 廷試得知縣，補甘肅之伏羌。

translations.literal: In the palace examination he was appointed magistrate and was assigned to Fuxiang in Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: In the palace examination he was appointed magistrate and was assigned to Fuxiang in Gansu.

sentences.zh: 回民田五反，縣民馬稱驥應之。

translations.literal: The Hui rebel Tian Wu rose in revolt, and county resident Ma Chenji responded.
translations.idiomatic: The Hui rebel Tian Wu rose in revolt, and the county resident Ma Chenji responded.

sentences.zh: 未發，芳燦從稱驥甥馬映龍偵得，立捕斬之，因城守。

translations.literal: Before the plot unfolded, Fangcan learned of it through Chenji's nephew Ma Yinglong, immediately had Chenji arrested and executed, and fortified the city.
translations.idiomatic: Before the plot unfolded, Fangcan learned of it through Chenji's nephew Ma Yinglong, immediately had Chenji arrested and executed, and fortified the city.

sentences.zh: 賊奄至，以無應，解圍去。

translations.literal: The rebels arrived unexpectedly; finding no response, they broke the siege and departed.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels arrived unexpectedly; finding no one to join them, they broke the siege and departed.

sentences.zh: 憾映龍洩其謀，揚言映龍故與通，約五日後獻城也。

translations.literal: Resentful that Yinglong had leaked their plot, they spread word that Yinglong had deliberately colluded with them and had agreed to surrender the city in five days.
translations.idiomatic: Resentful that Yinglong had leaked their plot, they spread word that Yinglong had deliberately colluded with them and had agreed to surrender the city in five days.

sentences.zh: 阿桂逮映龍，將殺之，卒以芳燦言得免。

translations.literal: Agui arrested Yinglong and was about to execute him; in the end, thanks to Fangcan's testimony, he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Agui arrested Yinglong and was about to execute him; in the end, thanks to Fangcan's testimony, he was spared.

sentences.zh: 敘功，擢知靈州，顧不樂外吏，入貲為戶部員外郎。

translations.literal: His merits were recorded; he was promoted to magistrate of Lingzhou, but unwilling to serve as an outer official he purchased an appointment as a vice director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: His merits were recorded and he was promoted to magistrate of Lingzhou, but unwilling to serve as an outer official he purchased an appointment as a vice director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 與修會典，益務記覽。

translations.literal: While assisting in compiling the Collected Statutes, he strove all the more to broaden his learning and memory.
translations.idiomatic: While assisting in compiling the Collected Statutes, he strove all the more to broaden his learning and memory.

sentences.zh: 為詞章，嘗曰：「色不欲麗，氣不欲縱，沉博奧衍，斯駢體之能事矣。」

translations.literal: On composing literary works he once said: "Color should not seek to be ornate, breath should not seek to be unrestrained; profound, broad, abstruse, and far-reaching—such are the fullest attainments of parallel prose."
translations.idiomatic: On belles-lettres he once said: "Color should not seek splendor, spirit should not seek unrestraint; depth, breadth, and abstruse extension—these are what parallel prose can fully accomplish."

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，貧甚，鬻書以歸。

translations.literal: Upon completing mourning for his mother he was very poor and sold books to return home.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his mother he was destitute and sold books to pay for his return home.

sentences.zh: 著芙蓉山館詩文鈔。

translations.literal: He authored the Furong Mountain Studio Poetry and Prose Drafts.
translations.idiomatic: He authored the Furong Mountain Studio Poetry and Prose Drafts.

sentences.zh: 揆，字荔裳。

translations.literal: Kui, styled Lishang.
translations.idiomatic: Kui, whose style was Lishang.

sentences.zh: 乾隆中，召試舉人，授中書。

translations.literal: In the Qianlong era, summoned to examination as provincial graduate, he was appointed Secretariat drafter.
translations.idiomatic: In the Qianlong era he was summoned to imperial examination as a provincial graduate and was appointed a Secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 從福康安徵衛藏。

translations.literal: He followed Fu Kang'an on the campaign to Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied Fu Kang'an on the campaign to Tibet.

sentences.zh: 官至四川布政使。

translations.literal: He rose to Sichuan provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Sichuan provincial administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 有藤花館稿。

translations.literal: He had the Wisteria Flower Studio Drafts.
translations.idiomatic: He published the Wisteria Flower Studio Drafts.

sentences.zh: 鼒，字山尊。

translations.literal: Zi, styled Shanzun.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zi, whose style was Shanzun.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶四年進士，終侍講學士。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the fourth year of Jiaqing; he ended his career as Lecturer-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in the fourth year of Jiaqing and ended his career as Lecturer-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 以母老告歸，主講揚州。

translations.literal: Citing his mother's age, he requested leave to return home and lectured in Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Citing his mother's age, he requested leave to return home and lectured in Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 亦長駢體，有夕蔡書屋集。

translations.literal: He also excelled at parallel prose and had the Evening Cai Studio Collection.
translations.idiomatic: He also excelled at parallel prose and published the Evening Cai Studio Collection.

sentences.zh: 徐文靖，字位山，當塗人。

translations.literal: Xu Wenjing, styled Weishan, was a man of Dangtu.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Wenjing, whose style was Weishan, came from Dangtu.

sentences.zh: 父章達，以孝義稱鄉里。

translations.literal: His father Zhangda was famed in the village for filial piety and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhangda was famed in the village for filial piety and integrity.

sentences.zh: 文靖務古學，無所不窺。

translations.literal: Wenjing devoted himself to classical learning and left nothing unexplored.
translations.idiomatic: Wenjing devoted himself to classical learning and left nothing unexplored.

sentences.zh: 著述甚富，皆援據經史。

translations.literal: His writings were extremely abundant, all supported with evidence from the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: His writings were extremely abundant, all supported with evidence from the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 雍正改元，年五十七，始舉江南鄉試。

translations.literal: When Yongzheng's reign began, at age fifty-seven he first passed the Jiangnan provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: When Yongzheng's reign began, at the age of fifty-seven he first passed the Jiangnan provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 侍郎黃叔琳典試還朝，以得三不朽士自矜，蓋指文靖及任啟運、陳祖範也。

translations.literal: Vice Minister Huang Shulin, returning from supervising the examination, prided himself on having obtained three men of the three immortals—referring to Wenjing, Ren Qiyun, and Chen Zufan.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Huang Shulin, returning from supervising the examination, prided himself on having discovered three men of enduring worth—Wenjing, Ren Qiyun, and Chen Zufan.

sentences.zh: 乾隆改元，試鴻博，不遇。

translations.literal: When Qianlong's reign began, he sat for the Hongbo examination and was not selected.
translations.idiomatic: When Qianlong's reign began, he sat for the Hongbo examination and was not selected.

sentences.zh: 詹事張鵬翀以所著山河兩戒考、管城碩記進呈，賜國子監學正。

translations.literal: Junior Sub-Prefect Zhang Pengchong presented his Investigation of the Two Boundaries of Mountains and Rivers and Substantial Records of Brush City to the throne; he was granted the post of Instructor at the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Junior Sub-Prefect Zhang Pengchong presented Wenjing's Investigation of the Two Boundaries of Mountains and Rivers and Substantial Records of Brush City to the throne; he was granted the post of Instructor at the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 十七年，徵經學，入都。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, classical learning was summoned; he entered the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year, when classical learning was summoned, he entered the capital.

sentences.zh: 會開萬壽恩科，遂與試，年八十六，以老壽賜檢討，給假歸。

translations.literal: When the Longevity Enthusiastic Examination was opened, he took the examination; at eighty-six he was granted reviser on account of age and longevity, and was given leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: When the Longevity Enthusiastic Examination was opened, he took part; at eighty-six he was granted the rank of reviser on account of age and longevity and was given leave to return home.

sentences.zh: 卒，年九十馀。

translations.literal: He died, aged over ninety.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of ninety or more.

sentences.zh: 其所著又有周易拾遺、禹貢會箋、竹書統箋諸書。

translations.literal: His other works include Gathered Remnants of the Book of Changes, Collaborative Commentary on the Tribute of Yu, Comprehensive Commentary on the Bamboo Annals, and other books.
translations.idiomatic: His other works include Gathered Remnants of the Book of Changes, Collaborative Commentary on the Tribute of Yu, Comprehensive Commentary on the Bamboo Annals, and other books.

sentences.zh: 趙青藜，字然一，涇縣人。

translations.literal: Zhao Qingli, styled Ranyi, was a man of Jing County.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Qingli, whose style was Ranyi, came from Jing County.

sentences.zh: 九歲能文，乾隆元年，舉會試第一，選庶吉士，授編修，充浙江鄉試考官。

translations.literal: At nine he could compose prose; in the first year of Qianlong he ranked first in the metropolitan examination, was selected as a bachelor, appointed compiler, and served as provincial examiner for Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: At nine he could compose prose; in the first year of Qianlong he ranked first in the metropolitan examination, was selected as a bachelor, appointed compiler, and served as provincial examiner for Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 遷御史，再充浙江考官，母憂歸，服闋，還台，又充湖南考官。

translations.literal: He was transferred to censor, again served as Zhejiang examiner, returned upon mourning for his mother, and after the mourning period resumed his post at the Censorate and again served as Hunan examiner.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to censor, again served as Zhejiang examiner, returned home upon mourning for his mother, and after the mourning period resumed his post at the Censorate and again served as Hunan examiner.

sentences.zh: 在台前後五年，有直聲。

translations.literal: In five years before and after the censorate he had a reputation for uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: During his five years at the Censorate he earned a reputation for uprightness.

sentences.zh: 如請清屯田、歸運丁、弛米禁、濟民食、提耗羨歸公、興西北水利；

translations.literal: Such as memorializing to clarify military colonies, restore transport laborers, relax rice prohibitions, aid the people's food supply, propose returning surplus fees to the public treasury, and promote waterworks in the northwest;
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized, among other things, to clarify military colonies, restore transport laborers, relax rice prohibitions, aid the people's food supply, return surplus fees to the public treasury, and promote waterworks in the northwest;

sentences.zh: 又劾總督高斌、侍郎周學健奏開捐例，啟言利之端，為害甚大。

translations.literal: He also impeached Governor-General Gao Bin and Vice Minister Zhou Xuejian for memorializing to open purchase-by-donation quotas, opening the door to profit-seeking and causing great harm.
translations.idiomatic: He also impeached Governor-General Gao Bin and Vice Minister Zhou Xuejian for memorializing to open purchase-by-donation quotas, arguing that this opened the door to profit-seeking and would cause great harm.

sentences.zh: 所言能持大體，不為激切之論。

translations.literal: What he said could uphold the larger principles and was not inflammatory argument.
translations.idiomatic: His memorials upheld the larger principles of governance and avoided inflammatory rhetoric.

sentences.zh: 尋以耳疾乞休，年八十馀，卒。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he requested retirement on account of ear ailment; aged over eighty, he died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he requested retirement on account of an ear ailment; he died at the age of eighty or more.

sentences.zh: 青藜外和內嚴，以不欺為主。

translations.literal: Qingli was outwardly gentle and inwardly strict, taking freedom from deception as his principle.
translations.idiomatic: Qingli was outwardly gentle and inwardly strict, and made integrity his guiding principle.

sentences.zh: 受古文義法於方苞，苞稱及門中如青藜者，可信其操行之終不迷。

translations.literal: He received the principles of ancient-style prose from Fang Bao; Bao said that among his disciples, men like Qingli could be trusted never to lose their way in conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He studied the principles of ancient-style prose under Fang Bao, who said that among his disciples, men like Qingli could be trusted never to stray from the path of integrity.

sentences.zh: 著有漱芳居集，讀左管窺，於春秋二百四十二年穿穴甚深。

translations.literal: He authored the Shufang Studio Collection and A Narrow View through Reading the Zuo Commentary, penetrating deeply into the two hundred forty-two years of the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: He authored the Shufang Studio Collection and A Narrow View through Reading the Zuo Commentary, in which his investigation of the two hundred forty-two years covered by the Spring and Autumn Annals was exceptionally thorough.

sentences.zh: 先是青藜同郡以史學稱者，推南陵汪越，字師退。

translations.literal: Earlier, among those in Qingli's prefecture famed for historical learning, Nanling's Wang Yue, styled Shitui, was held foremost.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, among those in Qingli's prefecture famed for historical learning, Wang Yue of Nanling, whose style was Shitui, was held foremost.

sentences.zh: 康熙四十四年舉人。

translations.literal: A provincial graduate in the forty-fourth year of Kangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He became a provincial graduate in the forty-fourth year of Kangxi.

sentences.zh: 食貧勵節，守令咸折節致敬。

translations.literal: Though poor he cultivated integrity; magistrates all lowered themselves to show him respect.
translations.idiomatic: Though poor, he cultivated integrity, and local magistrates all treated him with deference.

sentences.zh: 不妄幹謁。

translations.literal: He did not presumptuously seek audiences.
translations.idiomatic: He never presumptuously sought audiences with the powerful.

sentences.zh: 著綠影草堂集，沖淡典博。

translations.literal: He authored the Green Shadow Studio Collection, mild, restrained, classical, and broad.
translations.idiomatic: He authored the Green Shadow Studio Collection, a work mild in tone, restrained in manner, and rich in classical learning.

sentences.zh: 其讀史記十表，排比舊文，鉤稽微義，所得尤多。

translations.literal: In his reading of the Ten Tables of the Records of the Grand Historian, arranging the old text in order and probing subtle meanings, his gains were especially great.
translations.idiomatic: In his study of the Ten Tables of the Records of the Grand Historian, arranging the old text in order and probing subtle meanings, his gains were especially great.

sentences.zh: 朱仕琇，字斐瞻，建寧人。

translations.literal: Zhu Shixiu, styled Feizhan, was a man of Jianning.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Shixiu, whose style was Feizhan, came from Jianning.

sentences.zh: 資性朗悟，而記誦拙，日可數十言，援筆為文輒立就。

translations.literal: By nature he was bright and quick, yet clumsy at memorization—only a few dozen words a day—but when he took up the brush to write, the essay was instantly complete.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was bright and quick, yet clumsy at memorization and could retain only a few dozen words a day; when he took up the brush to write, however, the essay was instantly complete.

sentences.zh: 從南豐汪世麟學古文，臨別請益，世麟曰：「子但通習諸經，則世無與抗矣。」

translations.literal: He studied ancient-style prose under Wang Shilin of Nanfeng; on parting he asked for further instruction, and Shilin said: "If you simply master the classics thoroughly, there will be no one in the world to rival you."
translations.idiomatic: He studied ancient-style prose under Wang Shilin of Nanfeng; on parting he asked for further instruction, and Shilin said, "If you simply master the classics thoroughly, there will be no one in the world to rival you."

sentences.zh: 仕琇驚詫其言，遂以己意求之經傳，旁及百家諸子書，一以昌黎為宗。

translations.literal: Shixiu was startled by these words; he then pursued the classics and commentaries according to his own understanding, extending also to the writings of the hundred schools, taking Han Yu as his sole master.
translations.idiomatic: Shixiu was startled by these words; he then pursued the classics and commentaries according to his own understanding, extending also to the writings of the hundred schools, and took Han Yu as his sole model.

sentences.zh: 副都御史雷鋐見其文，嘆為醇古衝澹，近古大家，自是名大著。

translations.literal: Vice Censor-in-Chief Lei Qian saw his writing and exclaimed that it was pure, ancient, mild, and restrained—a master of recent antiquity—and from then his fame greatly spread.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Censor-in-Chief Lei Qian saw his writing and exclaimed that it was pure, ancient, mild, and restrained—the work of a master in the ancient manner—and from then his fame greatly spread.

sentences.zh: 乾隆九年，舉鄉試第一。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Qianlong he ranked first in the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Qianlong he ranked first in the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 逾四年，成進士，選庶吉士。

translations.literal: After four more years he became a jinshi and was selected as a bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: Four years later he became a jinshi and was selected as a bachelor.

sentences.zh: 散館，出知夏津縣，民為之謠曰：「夏津清，我公能。」

translations.literal: After leaving the Hanlin Academy he went out to serve as magistrate of Xiajin County; the people made a song about him saying: "Xiajin is clean—our lord can do it."
translations.idiomatic: After leaving the Hanlin Academy he went out to serve as magistrate of Xiajin County, and the people made a song about him: "Xiajin is clean—our lord can do it."

sentences.zh: 在任七年，以河決，改福寧府學教授。

translations.literal: In seven years in office, because of a breach in the river, he was transferred to professor at the Funing Prefectural School.
translations.idiomatic: After seven years in office, because of a breach in the river, he was transferred to professor at the Funing Prefectural School.

sentences.zh: 歸，主鰲峰講席者十年，卒，年六十六。

translations.literal: Returning home, he headed the Aofeng lecture chair for ten years, then died, aged sixty-six.
translations.idiomatic: Returning home, he headed the Aofeng lecture chair for ten years, then died at the age of sixty-six.

sentences.zh: 仕琇以古文辭自力，其意欲追古之立言者。

translations.literal: Shixiu exerted himself through ancient-style prose, his intention being to follow the ancient masters who established words.
translations.idiomatic: Shixiu exerted himself through ancient-style prose, intending to follow the ancient masters who gave enduring expression to truth.

sentences.zh: 以為清穆者惟天，澹泊者惟水，含之咀之，得其妙以為文者惟人。

translations.literal: He held that only Heaven is clear and solemn, only water is plain and unadorned; to hold and chew them and obtain their subtlety to make writing—only human beings can do this.
translations.idiomatic: He held that only Heaven is clear and solemn and only water is plain and unadorned; to hold and savor them and distill their subtlety into writing is something only human beings can do.

sentences.zh: 嘗與友人書曰：「為文在先高其志。

translations.literal: He once wrote to a friend saying: "In writing, one must first elevate one's aim.
translations.idiomatic: He once wrote to a friend, saying, "In writing, one must first elevate one's aim.

sentences.zh: 其心有以自得，則吾心猶古人之心也，以觀古人之言，猶吾言也。

translations.literal: When the mind has something by which it can find satisfaction within itself, then my mind is like the minds of the ancients; in viewing the words of the ancients, they are like my own words.
translations.idiomatic: When the mind has something by which it can find satisfaction within itself, then my mind is like the minds of the ancients, and in reading the words of the ancients, I hear my own voice.

sentences.zh: 然後辨其是非焉，究其誠偽焉，定其高下焉，如黑白之判於前矣。

translations.literal: Then one distinguishes right and wrong, investigates truth and falsity, and determines high and low, as black and white are decided before one.
translations.idiomatic: Then one can distinguish right from wrong, investigate truth and falsity, and determine what is superior and inferior, as clearly as black and white set before the eyes.

sentences.zh: 於是順其節次焉，還其訓詁焉，沉潛其義蘊焉，調和其心氣焉，久則自然合之，又久則變化生之。

translations.literal: Thereupon one follows its order and sequence, restores its glosses, sinks deeply into its meaning and substance, harmonizes one's mind and breath—and in time one naturally merges with it; after longer still, transformation and generation arise.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon one follows its order and sequence, restores its glosses, sinks deeply into its meaning, and harmonizes one's mind and spirit—and in time one naturally merges with it; after longer still, transformation and new creation arise.

sentences.zh: 於是文之高也，如累土之成台，如鴻漸之在天，有莫知其所以然者。」

translations.literal: Then the loftiness of writing is like piling earth to form a terrace, like the wild goose gradually ascending into the sky—there is something one cannot know the reason for."
translations.idiomatic: Then the loftiness of writing is like piling earth to form a terrace, like the wild goose gradually ascending into the sky—something achieved in a way one cannot fully explain."

sentences.zh: 仕琇與大興朱筠及弟珪友善，筠推服其文甚至。

translations.literal: Shixiu was on friendly terms with Zhu Yun of Daxing and his younger brother Gui; Yun admired his writing to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Shixiu was on friendly terms with Zhu Yun of Daxing and Yun's younger brother Gui; Zhu Yun admired his writing to the utmost.

sentences.zh: 著梅崖文集。

translations.literal: He authored the Meiya Collected Writings.
translations.idiomatic: He authored the Meiya Collected Writings.

sentences.zh: 福建古文之學自仕琇。

translations.literal: The study of ancient-style prose in Fujian began with Shixiu.
translations.idiomatic: The study of ancient-style prose in Fujian began with Shixiu.

sentences.zh: 其後再傳有高澍然，字雨農，光澤人。

translations.literal: Two generations later there was Gao Shuran, styled Yunong, a man of Guangze.
translations.idiomatic: Two generations later there was Gao Shuran of Guangze, whose style was Yunong.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶七年舉人，授內閣中書。

translations.literal: A provincial graduate in the seventh year of Jiaqing; he was appointed a Secretariat drafter.
translations.idiomatic: He became a provincial graduate in the seventh year of Jiaqing and was appointed a Secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 未幾，移病歸。

translations.literal: Before long he cited illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he cited illness and returned home.

sentences.zh: 研說經傳，尤篤嗜昌黎集。

translations.literal: He studied and expounded the classics and commentaries, especially devoted to the collected works of Han Yu.
translations.idiomatic: He studied and expounded the classics and commentaries and was especially devoted to the collected works of Han Yu.

sentences.zh: 其文陳義正，言不過物，高視塵壒之表。

translations.literal: His writing set forth principles correctly; his words did not exceed their objects, and he looked down from above the dust and clamor.
translations.idiomatic: His writing set forth principles correctly; his words never exceeded their proper objects, and he looked down from above the dust and clamor of the world.

sentences.zh: 名不如仕琇，要其自得之趣，有不求人知能自樹立者。

translations.literal: His fame did not match Shixiu's, yet in the pleasures he found within himself there was one who sought no recognition from others and could stand on his own.
translations.idiomatic: His fame did not match Shixiu's, yet in the pleasures he found within himself he sought no recognition from others and could stand firmly on his own.

sentences.zh: 著春秋釋經、論語私記、韓文故及抑快軒文集。

translations.literal: He authored Exegesis of the Spring and Autumn Annals, Private Notes on the Analects, Old Notes on Han Yu's Writings, and the Collected Writings of the Yikuai Studio.
translations.idiomatic: He authored Exegesis of the Spring and Autumn Annals, Private Notes on the Analects, Old Notes on Han Yu's Writings, and the Collected Writings of the Yikuai Studio.

sentences.zh: 蔣士銓，字心馀，鉛山人。

translations.literal: Jiang Shiquan, styled Xinyu, was a man of Yanshan.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Shiquan, whose style was Xinyu, came from Yanshan.

sentences.zh: 家故貧，四歲，母鍾氏授書，斷竹篾為點畫，攢簇成字教之。

translations.literal: His family was originally poor; at four, his mother, née Zhong, taught him reading, cutting bamboo splints into strokes and assembling them into characters to instruct him.
translations.idiomatic: His family was originally poor; at the age of four his mother, née Zhong, taught him to read by cutting bamboo splints into strokes and assembling them into characters.

sentences.zh: 既長，工為文，喜吟詠。

translations.literal: When grown, he was skilled at writing and fond of poetry and song.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew up, he was skilled at prose and fond of poetry.

sentences.zh: 由舉人官中書。

translations.literal: From provincial graduate he served as a Secretariat drafter.
translations.idiomatic: As a provincial graduate he served as a Secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二十二年，成進士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year of Qianlong he became a jinshi and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year of Qianlong he became a jinshi and was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 文名藉甚，裘曰修、彭元瑞並薦其才。

translations.literal: His literary fame was very great; Qiu Yuexiu and Peng Yuanrui both recommended his talent.
translations.idiomatic: His literary fame was very great, and Qiu Yuexiu and Peng Yuanrui both recommended his talent.

sentences.zh: 旋乞病歸。

translations.literal: Soon he requested leave on grounds of illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he requested leave on grounds of illness and returned home.

sentences.zh: 帝屢從元瑞詢之，元瑞之士銓母老對。

translations.literal: The emperor repeatedly inquired about him through Yuanrui; Yuanrui replied that Shiquan's mother was old.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor repeatedly inquired about him through Peng Yuanrui, who replied that Shiquan's mother was old.

sentences.zh: 帝賜詩元瑞，有「江西兩名士」之句。

translations.literal: The emperor bestowed a poem on Yuanrui containing the line "Two famous scholars of Jiangxi."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor bestowed a poem on Peng Yuanrui containing the line "Two famous scholars of Jiangxi."

sentences.zh: 士銓感恩眷，力疾起補官，記名以御史用。

translations.literal: Shiquan, grateful for imperial favor, forced himself up despite illness to resume office; his name was recorded for use as censor.
translations.idiomatic: Shiquan, grateful for the emperor's favor, forced himself up despite illness to resume office, and his name was recorded for appointment as censor.

sentences.zh: 未幾，仍以病乞休，遂卒，年六十二。

translations.literal: Before long he again requested retirement on grounds of illness, then died, aged sixty-two.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he again requested retirement on grounds of illness, then died at the age of sixty-two.

sentences.zh: 士銓賦性悱惻，以古賢者自勵，急人之難如不及。

translations.literal: Shiquan was by nature compassionate and tender, taking ancient worthies as his model, rushing to others' distress as if he could not arrive soon enough.
translations.idiomatic: Shiquan was by nature compassionate and tender, took ancient worthies as his model, and rushed to others' distress as if he could not arrive soon enough.

sentences.zh: 詩詞雄傑，至★述節烈，能使讀者感泣。

translations.literal: His poetry and lyrics were bold and powerful; when it came to portraying loyal martyrs, he could move readers to tears.
translations.idiomatic: His poetry and lyrics were bold and powerful, and when portraying loyal martyrs he could move readers to tears.

sentences.zh: 著忠雅堂集。

translations.literal: He authored the Zhongya Hall Collection.
translations.idiomatic: He authored the Zhongya Hall Collection.

sentences.zh: 少時與武寧汪軔、南昌楊垕為昆弟交，出入必偕，財物與共。

translations.literal: In youth he formed brotherly friendship with Wang Ren of Wuning and Yang Hou of Nanchang; they always went out together and shared possessions.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he formed a brotherly bond with Wang Ren of Wuning and Yang Hou of Nanchang; they always went out together and shared their possessions.

sentences.zh: 軔，字魚亭，優貢生。

translations.literal: Ren, styled Yuting, was an outstanding tribute student.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ren, whose style was Yuting, was an outstanding tribute student.

sentences.zh: 垕，字子載，舉人，本天全六番招討宣慰使孫，雍正初，改土歸流，安置江西，遂為南昌人。

translations.literal: Hou, styled Zizai, was a provincial graduate, originally grandson of the Pacification Commissioner of the Six Fan of Tianquan; in the early Yongzheng era, when native domains were converted to direct rule, he was resettled in Jiangxi and thus became a man of Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hou, whose style was Zizai, was a provincial graduate and originally the grandson of the Pacification Commissioner of the Six Fan of Tianquan; in the early Yongzheng era, when native domains were converted to direct rule, he was resettled in Jiangxi and thus became a man of Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 詩名與軔相埒。

translations.literal: His poetic fame matched Ren's.
translations.idiomatic: His poetic fame matched Wang Ren's.

sentences.zh: 士銓甚推服之。

translations.literal: Shiquan greatly admired them.
translations.idiomatic: Shiquan greatly admired them both.

sentences.zh: 同時有南豐趙由儀，字山南。

translations.literal: At the same time there was Zhao Youyi of Nanfeng, styled Shannan.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time there was Zhao Youyi of Nanfeng, whose style was Shannan.

sentences.zh: 與士銓等並稱四子。

translations.literal: Together with Shiquan and the others they were styled the Four Masters.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Shiquan and the others they were styled the Four Masters.

sentences.zh: 其後繼起者，曰東鄉吳嵩梁、臨川樂鈞。

translations.literal: Those who rose afterward were Wu Songliang of Dongxiang and Le Jun of Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Those who rose afterward were Wu Songliang of Dongxiang and Le Jun of Linchuan.

sentences.zh: 嵩梁，字蘭雪。

translations.literal: Songliang, styled Lanxue.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Songliang, whose style was Lanxue.

sentences.zh: 以舉人官中書，選知黔西州。

translations.literal: As provincial graduate he served as Secretariat drafter and was selected to serve as prefect of Qianxi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: As a provincial graduate he served as a Secretariat drafter and was selected to serve as prefect of Qianxi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 著香蘇山館集。

translations.literal: He authored the Xiangsu Mountain Studio Collection.
translations.idiomatic: He authored the Xiangsu Mountain Studio Collection.

sentences.zh: 聲播外夷，朝鮮吏曹判書金魯敬以梅花一龕供奉之，稱為詩佛。

translations.literal: His fame spread to foreign lands; Jin Lujing, Minister of Personnel of Korea, enshrined a niche of plum blossoms in his honor and called him the Buddha of Poetry.
translations.idiomatic: His fame spread abroad; Jin Lujing, Minister of Personnel of Korea, enshrined a niche of plum blossoms in his honor and called him the Buddha of Poetry.

sentences.zh: 日本賈人斥四金購其詩扇。

translations.literal: Japanese merchants spent four ounces of gold to buy his poetry fans.
translations.idiomatic: Japanese merchants spent four ounces of gold to buy his poetry fans.

sentences.zh: 其名重如此。

translations.literal: His fame weighed so heavily.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the weight of his fame.

sentences.zh: 鈞，初名宮譜，字元淑。

translations.literal: Jun, originally named Gongpu, styled Yuanshu.
translations.idiomatic: Le Jun, originally named Gongpu, whose style was Yuanshu.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶六年舉人。

translations.literal: A provincial graduate in the sixth year of Jiaqing.
translations.idiomatic: He became a provincial graduate in the sixth year of Jiaqing.

sentences.zh: 與嵩梁同為翁方綱弟子。

translations.literal: Together with Songliang he was a disciple of Weng Fanggang.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Songliang he was a disciple of Weng Fanggang.

sentences.zh: 著青芝山館集。

translations.literal: He authored the Green Fungus Mountain Studio Collection.
translations.idiomatic: He authored the Green Fungus Mountain Studio Collection.

sentences.zh: 後出知。

translations.literal: Later he went out to serve as prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Later he went out to serve as prefect of Zhen'an Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 民輸穀常社倉，用竹筐，以權代概。

translations.literal: The people delivered grain to the communal granary in bamboo baskets, using steelyard weights in place of bushel measures.
translations.idiomatic: The people delivered grain to the communal granary in bamboo baskets, using steelyard weights in place of bushel measures.

sentences.zh: 有司因購馬濟，別置大筐斂穀，後遂不革，民苦之。

translations.literal: Officials, because of purchasing horses to aid the army, separately set up large baskets to collect grain; afterward this was never reformed, and the people suffered from it.
translations.idiomatic: Officials, because of purchasing horses to aid the army, separately set up large baskets to collect grain; afterward this practice was never reformed, and the people suffered from it.

sentences.zh: 聽民用舊筐​​，自權，持羨去，民由是感激，每出行，爭肩輿過其村。

translations.literal: He allowed the people to use the old baskets, weigh for themselves, and take the surplus away; the people were thereby grateful, and whenever he went out they vied to carry his sedan chair past their villages.
translations.idiomatic: He allowed the people to use the old baskets, weigh for themselves, and keep the surplus; the people were deeply grateful, and whenever he went out they vied to carry his sedan chair past their villages.

sentences.zh: 先是民入土為奸，捕獲百馀人，顧逸去，前守以是罷官。

translations.literal: Earlier, when residents went into the territory to commit wrongdoing, over a hundred were captured, but Gu escaped; the previous prefect was dismissed from office for this.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when a local man named Fu Feng went into Yunnan to commit wrongdoing, over a hundred accomplices were captured, but Fu Feng escaped; the previous prefect was dismissed from office for this.

sentences.zh: 已而死，驗其屍良是。

translations.literal: Before long he died; examination of the corpse confirmed it was indeed he.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Fu Feng died; examination of the corpse confirmed that it was indeed he.

sentences.zh: 總督疑其為前守道地，申辨，總督怒，劾之。

translations.literal: The governor-general suspected that the previous prefect had given him cover; he pleaded his case, the governor-general grew angry, and impeached him.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Li Shiyao suspected that the previous prefect had given Fu Feng cover; Zhao Yi pleaded his case, the governor-general grew angry, and impeached him.

sentences.zh: 適朝廷用兵，命赴軍贊畫，乃追劾疏還。

translations.literal: Just then the court was deploying troops; he was ordered to go to the army as strategic planner, and the impeachment memorial was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: Just then the court was deploying troops; he was ordered to the army as strategic planner, and the impeachment memorial was recalled.

sentences.zh: 既至，經略兵事，議以大兵渡，別遣偏師從進。

translations.literal: Once he arrived, he directed military affairs and proposed that the main force cross the river while a detached column advanced from another route.
translations.idiomatic: Once Fu Heng arrived in Yunnan, he directed military affairs and proposed that the main force cross the Gajiang River while a detached column advanced from Pu'er.

sentences.zh: 謂距四千餘里，不如由江東岸近地取，如其策入告。

translations.literal: He said the distance was over four thousand li and that it would be better to take the nearer ground along the eastern bank of the river; following his plan, the report was submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yi said Pu'er was more than four thousand li away and that it would be better to take the nearer ground along the eastern bank of the river at Mengmi; following his plan, the report was submitted to the throne.

sentences.zh: 其後兵遭瘴多疾病，而所統江東岸一軍獨完，卒以蕆事。

translations.literal: Afterward the troops suffered malaria and many fell ill, but the single army he commanded on the eastern bank remained intact, and in the end the affair was concluded.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward the troops crossing the Gajiang suffered malaria and many fell ill, but the single army Agui commanded on the eastern bank remained intact, and in the end the campaign was successfully concluded.

sentences.zh: 尋調守，擢兵備道。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to serve as prefect and was promoted to defense circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to serve as prefect of Guangzhou and was promoted to defense circuit intendant of Guixi.

sentences.zh: 以讞獄舊案降級，遂乞歸，不復出。

translations.literal: Because of an old case in adjudicating criminal matters he was demoted, then requested to return home and never went out again.
translations.idiomatic: Because of an old case in adjudicating criminal matters in Guangzhou he was demoted, then requested to return home and never served again.

sentences.zh: 五十二年，反，赴治軍，邀與俱。

translations.literal: In the fifty-second year there was a rebellion; he went to manage the army and invited him to go together.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-second year of Qianlong, when Lin Shuangwen rebelled, Li Shiyao went to manage the army in Taiwan and invited Zhao Yi to accompany him.

sentences.zh: 時總兵城守半載，以易子析骸入告。

translations.literal: At the time the regional commander had defended the city for half a year and memorialized that the people were reduced to exchanging children and splitting corpses for food.
translations.idiomatic: At the time General Ming Rui had defended the city for half a year and memorialized that the people were reduced to exchanging children and splitting corpses for food.

sentences.zh: 帝意動，諭以兵護民內渡。

translations.literal: The emperor's resolve wavered and he ordered that troops escort the people inland across the strait.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's resolve wavered, and he ordered that troops escort the people inland across the strait.

sentences.zh: 以詢，曰：「總兵欲內渡久矣，憚國法故不敢。

translations.literal: When asked, he said: "The regional commander has long wished to cross inland but dared not because he feared the law of the state.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Yi was consulted, he said, "The regional commander has long wished to cross inland but dared not because he feared the law of the state.

sentences.zh: 今一棄城，則為賊有，全休矣！

translations.literal: Now if the city is abandoned once, it will fall to the rebels and all will be lost!
translations.idiomatic: Now if the city is abandoned once, it will fall to the rebels and all will be lost!

sentences.zh: 即大兵至，無路可入。

translations.literal: Even when the great army arrives, there will be no way to enter.
translations.idiomatic: Even when the main army arrives, there will be no way to enter.

sentences.zh: 宜封還此旨。」

translations.literal: This edict should be sealed and returned."
translations.idiomatic: This edict should be sealed and returned unopened."

sentences.zh: 悟，從之，明日接追還前旨之諭，膺殊賞；

translations.literal: Understanding, he followed this advice; the next day he received the order recalling the previous edict and was granted special reward;
translations.idiomatic: Li Shiyao understood and followed this advice; the next day he received the order recalling the previous edict and was granted special reward;

sentences.zh: 而大將軍續至，遂得由進兵破賊，皆計也。

translations.literal: and when the grand general arrived in succession, they were able to advance and break the rebels—all owing to his plan.
translations.idiomatic: and when the grand general arrived in succession, they were able to advance and defeat the rebels—all owing to Zhao Yi's plan.

sentences.zh: 事平，辭歸，以著述自娛。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled he declined and returned home, taking scholarly writing for his pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was settled he declined and returned home, devoting himself to scholarly writing.

sentences.zh: 尤邃史學，著、、、、。

translations.literal: He was especially versed in historical learning and authored several works, titles omitted in the source text.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially versed in historical learning and authored Notes on the Twenty-Two Histories, Collected Remnants from the Hillside, Notes Written in the Sun, and the Ou Bei Collection.

sentences.zh: 十五年，重宴鹿鳴，賜三品銜。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he again attended the Luming banquet and was granted third-rank insignia.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Jiaqing he again attended the Luming banquet and was granted third-rank insignia.

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十六。

translations.literal: He died, aged eighty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of eighty-six.

sentences.zh: 同時、與齊名，而有經世之略，未盡其用。

translations.literal: At the same time certain men were equally famous with him, names omitted in the source text, yet he had the breadth of vision to manage the world and his talents were not fully used.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time Yuan Mei and Jiang Shiquan were equally famous with him, yet he had the breadth of vision to manage affairs of state and his talents were not fully used.

sentences.zh: 所為詩無不如人意所欲為，亦其才優也。

translations.literal: In the poetry he composed there was none that did not accord with what people wished to express—this too showed the superiority of his talent.
translations.idiomatic: In the poetry he composed there was none that did not give full expression to what people wished to say—this too showed the superiority of his talent.

sentences.zh: 其同里學人後於而知名者，有、、、、、、，號為「七子」。

translations.literal: Among fellow-townsmen scholars who came after him and became well known, there were several, names omitted in the source text, styled the "Seven Masters."
translations.idiomatic: Among scholars from his native place who came after Zhao Yi and became well known were Hong Liangji, Sun Xingyan, Zhao Huaiyu, Huang Jingren, Yang Lun, Lü Xingyuan, and Xu Shushou, styled the "Seven Masters."

sentences.zh: 、、自有傳。

translations.literal: Hong Liangji, Sun Xingyan, and Zhao Huaiyu each have their own biographies.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Liangji, Sun Xingyan, and Zhao Huaiyu each have their own biographies elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 嚴長明，​​字道甫，江寧人。

translations.literal: Yan Changming, styled Daofu, was a man of Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Changming, styled Daofu, was a native of Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 幼奇慧。

translations.literal: In youth he was extraordinarily clever.
translations.idiomatic: As a child he was extraordinarily clever.

sentences.zh: 年十一，為李紱所賞，告方苞曰：「國器也！」

translations.literal: At the age of eleven he was admired by Li Fu, who told Fang Bao, "This is material for a pillar of state!"
translations.idiomatic: At the age of eleven he won the admiration of Li Fu, who told Fang Bao, "This boy is material for a pillar of state!"

sentences.zh: 遂從苞受業。

translations.literal: Thereupon he followed Bao and received instruction from him.
translations.idiomatic: Changming thereupon became Fang Bao's pupil.

sentences.zh: 尋假館揚州馬氏，盡讀其藏書。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he took lodging with the Ma family of Yangzhou and read through their entire book collection.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he lodged with the Ma family of Yangzhou and read through their entire library.

sentences.zh: 高宗二十七年南巡，以諸生獻賦，賜舉人，用內閣中書，入軍機。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year of the Gaozong reign, when the emperor made his southern tour, Changming submitted a fu as a common student, was granted the rank of provincial graduate, appointed secretary in the Grand Secretariat, and entered the Grand Council.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year of Qianlong, when the emperor made his southern tour, Changming submitted a fu as a common student, was granted the rank of provincial graduate, appointed secretary in the Grand Secretariat, and entered the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 長明通古今，多智數，工於奏牘，大學士劉統勳最奇其才。

translations.literal: Changming was versed in antiquity and the present, possessed much shrewd calculation, and excelled at memorial drafts; Grand Secretary Liu Tongxun most admired his talent.
translations.idiomatic: Changming was versed in past and present affairs, possessed great shrewdness, and excelled at drafting memorials; Grand Secretary Liu Tongxun admired his talent above all others.

sentences.zh: 戶部奏天下錢糧雜項名目繁多，請併入地丁徵收，長明曰：「今之雜項折徵銀，皆古正供也。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Revenue memorialized that the miscellaneous items in land tax and grain dues throughout the empire were too numerous in name and requested that they be merged into the land-and-poll tax for collection. Changming said, "The miscellaneous items now collected in converted silver are all ancient regular tribute.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Revenue memorialized that the miscellaneous items in land tax and grain dues throughout the empire were too numerous and requested that they be merged into the land-and-poll tax for collection. Changming said, "The miscellaneous items now collected in converted silver are all ancient regular tribute.

sentences.zh: 若去其名，他日吏忘之，謂其物官所需，必且再徵，是使民重困也。」

translations.literal: If their names are removed, then someday clerks will forget them, take the goods to be what the government needs, and surely levy them again—this would make the people suffer doubly."
translations.idiomatic: If their names are removed, clerks will someday forget what they were, assume the goods are whatever the government happens to need, and levy them again—doubling the people's burden."

sentences.zh: 統勳曰善，乃奏已之。

translations.literal: Tongxun said this was good, and the memorial was then withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: Tongxun approved, and the proposal was withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 大學士溫福徵大金川，欲長明從行，長明固辭。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Wen Fu was dispatched to campaign in Jinchuan and wanted Changming to accompany him, but Changming firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Secretary Wen Fu was dispatched to campaign in Jinchuan, he wanted Changming to accompany him, but Changming firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 退，有咎之者，答曰：「是將敗沒，吾奈何從之！」

translations.literal: After he withdrew, some blamed him, and he replied, "That expedition is going to end in defeat and ruin—how could I follow it!"
translations.idiomatic: Afterward some blamed him, and he replied, "That expedition is going to end in defeat and ruin—how could I follow it!"

sentences.zh: 既而溫福果軍潰以死，隨往者皆盡。

translations.literal: Before long Wen Fu indeed met with routed armies and died, and all who had followed him perished.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Wen Fu's army was indeed routed and he died, and all who had followed him perished.

sentences.zh: 長明在軍機七年，幹敏異眾，然亦以是見嫉。

translations.literal: Changming served in the Grand Council for seven years; his efficiency and keenness surpassed the rest, yet for that very reason he also aroused envy.
translations.idiomatic: Changming served in the Grand Council for seven years. His efficiency and keenness surpassed everyone else's, yet for that very reason he also aroused envy.

sentences.zh: 其救羅浩源事，人尤喜稱之​​。

translations.literal: His rescue of Luo Haoyuan was especially praised by people.
translations.idiomatic: People especially praised his rescue of Luo Haoyuan.

sentences.zh: 浩源，雲南糧道也。

translations.literal: Haoyuan was grain intendant of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Haoyuan was grain intendant of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 分償屬吏汪應繳所虧帑金，有詔逾期即誅。

translations.literal: He was to share in repaying the treasury shortfall owed by his subordinate Wang Ying, and an edict decreed that if the deadline was exceeded he would be executed.
translations.idiomatic: He had been ordered to share in repaying a treasury shortfall owed by his subordinate Wang Ying, and an edict decreed execution if the deadline was missed.

sentences.zh: 浩源繳不如數，逾期十日，牒請弛限。

translations.literal: Haoyuan paid in less than the required amount, exceeded the deadline by ten days, and submitted a petition requesting an extension.
translations.idiomatic: Haoyuan paid in less than the required amount, exceeded the deadline by ten days, and submitted a petition requesting an extension.

sentences.zh: 上下其議，時統勳主試禮部，秋曹無敢任其事者。

translations.literal: The matter was passed up and down for deliberation. At the time Tongxun was presiding over the Ministry of Rites examination, and no one in the autumn office dared take responsibility for the case.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was passed up and down for deliberation. Tongxun was then presiding over the Ministry of Rites examination, and no one in the autumn office dared take responsibility for the case.

sentences.zh: 長明因撾鼓入闈，見統勳，為言汪已捐复，將曳組綬出都，獨坐浩源，義未協，宜仍責汪自繳。

translations.literal: Changming therefore beat the drum to enter the examination compound, saw Tongxun, and explained that Wang had already made restitution by donation and was about to drag his official sash out of the capital, while Haoyuan alone was being punished—the justice did not accord; Wang should still be held to pay on his own.
translations.idiomatic: Changming beat the drum to enter the examination compound, saw Tongxun, and explained that Wang had already made restitution by donation and was about to leave the capital in official dress while Haoyuan alone was being punished—the justice did not accord; Wang should still be held to pay on his own.

sentences.zh: 統勳曰：「具疏稿乎？」

translations.literal: Tongxun said, "Do you have a memorial draft ready?"
translations.idiomatic: Tongxun said, "Do you have a memorial draft ready?"

translations.literal: He said, "It is ready."
translations.idiomatic: Changming said, "It is ready."

sentences.zh: 即振袖出之，辭義明晰。

translations.literal: He immediately shook out his sleeve and produced it; its language and argument were clear.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately shook out his sleeve and produced it; its language and argument were perfectly clear.

sentences.zh: 疏入報可，獄遂解。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted and approved, and the case was thereupon resolved.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted and approved, and the case was resolved.

sentences.zh: 其他事多類此。

translations.literal: His other affairs were mostly of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Most of his other deeds were of this kind.

sentences.zh: 人有圖其像祀之者。

translations.literal: Some people painted his portrait and offered sacrifice to it.
translations.idiomatic: Some people painted his portrait and worshipped it.

sentences.zh: 三十六年，擢侍讀。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year he was promoted to attendant reader.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-sixth year of Qianlong he was promoted to attendant reader.

sentences.zh: 嘗扈蹕木蘭，大雪中失橐扆並所裝物，越日故吏以扆至。

translations.literal: He once accompanied the imperial procession at Mulan and in a heavy snowfall lost his traveling screen and everything packed with it; the next day a former clerk brought the screen back.
translations.idiomatic: He once accompanied the imperial procession at Mulan and in a heavy snowfall lost his traveling screen and everything packed with it; the next day a former clerk returned with the screen.

sentences.zh: 問「何以知為吾物」，曰：「軍機官披羊裘者獨君耳。」

translations.literal: He asked, "How did you know it was mine?" The man said, "Among Grand Council officials, you alone wear a sheepskin coat."
translations.idiomatic: Changming asked, "How did you know it was mine?" The man said, "Among Grand Council officials, you alone wear a sheepskin coat."

sentences.zh: 長明勞而遣之。

translations.literal: Changming rewarded him and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: Changming rewarded him and sent him on his way.

sentences.zh: 後以憂歸，遂不復出。

translations.literal: Later he returned home on account of mourning and never went out again.
translations.idiomatic: Later he returned home on account of mourning and never took office again.

sentences.zh: 客畢沅所，為定奏詞。

translations.literal: He was a guest at Bi Yuan's residence and drafted memorial language for him.
translations.idiomatic: He stayed as a guest at Bi Yuan's residence and drafted memorial language for him.

sentences.zh: 又主講廬陽書院。

translations.literal: He also served as chief lecturer at the Luyang Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He also served as chief lecturer at the Luyang Academy.

sentences.zh: 博學強記，所讀書，或舉問，無不能對。

translations.literal: Broadly learned and with a powerful memory, whatever book he had read, if any passage was cited in questioning, there was none he could not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Broadly learned and with a powerful memory, he could answer any question drawn from whatever he had read.

sentences.zh: 為詩文用思周密，和易而當於情。

translations.literal: In composing poetry and prose his thought was thorough and careful, mild and easy yet fitting to feeling.
translations.idiomatic: In composing poetry and prose his thought was thorough and careful, his tone mild and easy yet true to feeling.

sentences.zh: 著毛詩地理疏證、五經算術補正、三經三史答問、石經考異、漢金石例、獻徵馀錄等書。

translations.literal: He authored Geographical Evidential Commentary on the Mao Odes, Corrections and Supplements to Arithmetic in the Five Classics, Questions and Answers on Three Classics and Three Histories, Examination of Differences in Stone Classics, Han Epigraphic Precedents, Remaining Records of Offered Testimony, and other books.
translations.idiomatic: He authored Geographical Evidential Commentary on the Mao Odes, Corrections and Supplements to Arithmetic in the Five Classics, Questions and Answers on Three Classics and Three Histories, Examination of Differences in Stone Classics, Han Epigraphic Precedents, Remaining Records of Offered Testimony, and other works.

sentences.zh: 子觀，字子進。

translations.literal: His son Guan, styled Zijin.
translations.idiomatic: His son Guan, styled Zijin.

sentences.zh: 嗜學，好金石文字。

translations.literal: He loved learning and delighted in epigraphic writing on metal and stone.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning and delighted in epigraphic inscriptions on metal and stone.

sentences.zh: 父乞歸後，築歸求草堂，藏書二萬卷，觀丹黃幾滿。

translations.literal: After his father requested leave to return home, he built the Guiqiu Thatched Hall, collected twenty thousand juan of books, and Guan's red-and-yellow annotations nearly filled them all.
translations.idiomatic: After his father retired, he built the Guiqiu Thatched Hall, amassed twenty thousand juan of books, and Guan's red-and-yellow annotations nearly filled them all.

sentences.zh: 著江寧金石記，錢大昕甚高其品節。

translations.literal: He authored Records of Metal and Stone in Jiangning, and Qian Daxin greatly esteemed his character and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: He authored Records of Metal and Stone in Jiangning, and Qian Daxin greatly esteemed his character and integrity.

sentences.zh: 詔求遺書，奏言翰林院藏內多古書，請開局校輯。

translations.literal: When an edict sought lost books, he memorialized that within the Hanlin Academy collection of the Yongle Encyclopedia were many ancient books and requested that a bureau be opened to collate and edit them.
translations.idiomatic: When an edict sought lost books, Zhu Yun memorialized that the Hanlin Academy's copy of the Yongle Encyclopedia contained many ancient works and requested that a bureau be opened to collate and edit them.

sentences.zh: 旋奉上諭：「軍機大臣議復條奏校核一節，已派軍機大臣為總裁。
