translations.literal: Soon an imperial rescript followed: "On the section in the Grand Council ministers' deliberative reply concerning Zhu Yun's memorial on collating and verifying the Yongle Encyclopedia, Grand Council ministers have already been appointed as chief compilers.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an imperial rescript followed: "On the section in the Grand Council ministers' reply concerning Zhu Yun's memorial on collating and verifying the Yongle Encyclopedia, Grand Council ministers have already been appointed as chief compilers.

sentences.zh: 又所奏將擇取繕寫，各自為書，及每書校其得失，撮舉大旨，敘於本書卷首之處，即令承辦各員，將各原書詳細檢閱，並書中要旨總敘厓略，呈候裁定；

translations.literal: Further, as Zhu Yun memorialized, selections from the Yongle Encyclopedia are to be copied out, each forming a separate book; for each book its errors and merits are to be collated, its main purport summarized, and an account placed at the head of the book. Let each official in charge thoroughly examine each original work and submit a general outline of the essential points of each book for approval;
translations.idiomatic: Further, as Zhu Yun proposed, selections from the Yongle Encyclopedia are to be copied out as separate books; for each book its errors and merits are to be collated, its main purport summarized, and an account placed at the head of the volume. Each official in charge is to thoroughly examine the original works and submit a general outline of each book's essential points for approval;

sentences.zh: 又將來書成，著名。」

translations.literal: and when the books are completed in future, they are to be titled Complete Library of the Four Treasuries."
translations.idiomatic: and when the books are completed, they are to be titled Complete Library of the Four Treasuries."

sentences.zh: 自此始。

translations.literal: From this the Complete Library of the Four Treasuries began.
translations.idiomatic: From this the Complete Library of the Four Treasuries began.

sentences.zh: 又請仿、故事，校正文字，勒石太學。

translations.literal: Yun also requested that, following the precedents of the Han Xiping and Tang Kaicheng stone classics, the text of the Thirteen Classics be corrected and cut into stone at the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yun also requested that, following the precedents of the Han Xiping and Tang Kaicheng stone classics, the text of the Thirteen Classics be corrected and cut into stone at the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 未幾，坐事降編修，充纂修官，兼修。

translations.literal: Before long, on account of an offense he was demoted to compiler, appointed a compilation officer of the Complete Library of the Four Treasuries, and also assigned to compile Records of Old Matters in the Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, on account of an offense he was demoted to compiler, appointed a compilation officer of the Complete Library of the Four Treasuries, and also assigned to compile Records of Old Matters in the Capital.

sentences.zh: 嘗稱學問文章殊過人。

translations.literal: The Gaozong Emperor once praised Yun's learning and literary attainments as greatly surpassing others.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong once praised Zhu Yun's learning and literary attainments as greatly surpassing others.

sentences.zh: 尋，復督學。

translations.literal: Before long he again supervised education.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was again appointed educational commissioner.

sentences.zh: 歸，卒，年五十有三。

translations.literal: He returned home, died, aged fifty-three.
translations.idiomatic: He returned home and died at the age of fifty-three.

sentences.zh: 子，舉人，知縣。

translations.literal: His son Jingheng was a provincial graduate and served as magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jingheng was a provincial graduate and served as magistrate.

sentences.zh: 有雋才，故工書，學其筆法，能亂真。

translations.literal: He had outstanding talent; Nai was skilled at calligraphy, and Jingheng studied his brush method and could produce work indistinguishable from the genuine.
translations.idiomatic: He had outstanding talent; Yao Nai was skilled at calligraphy, and Jingheng studied his brush method so well that his copies could pass for the genuine article.

sentences.zh: 當、間，傳古文法者，有、諸人，自有傳。

translations.literal: During the Jiaqing and Daoguang reigns, among those who transmitted the methods of ancient-style prose were Wu Dexuan of Yixing, Mei Zengliang of Shangyuan, and others; Zengliang has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jiaqing and Daoguang reigns, among those who transmitted the methods of ancient-style prose were Wu Dexuan of Yixing, Mei Zengliang of Shangyuan, and others; Zengliang has his own biography.

translations.literal: Dexuan, styled Zhonglun.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Dexuan, styled Zhonglun.

sentences.zh: 諸生。

translations.literal: He was a common student.
translations.idiomatic: He was a common student.

sentences.zh: 以古文鳴。

translations.literal: He was renowned for ancient-style prose.
translations.idiomatic: He was renowned for ancient-style prose.

sentences.zh: 與、以文相砥鏃。

translations.literal: Together with Yun Jing of Yanghu and Lü Huang of Yongfu he sharpened one another's writing.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Yun Jing of Yanghu and Lü Huang of Yongfu he sharpened one another's writing.

sentences.zh: 詩亦高澹絕俗，有。

translations.literal: His poetry too was lofty, plain, and utterly beyond the vulgar; he had the Chuyue Studio Collection.
translations.idiomatic: His poetry too was lofty, plain, and utterly beyond the vulgar; he authored the Chuyue Studio Collection.

sentences.zh: 宋大樽，字左彝，仁和人。

translations.literal: Song Dazun, styled Zuoyi, was a man of Renhe.
translations.idiomatic: Song Dazun, styled Zuoyi, was a native of Renhe.

sentences.zh: 弱歲，刲股愈母疾，讓產其弟。

translations.literal: In his youth he cut flesh from his thigh to cure his mother's illness and yielded his inheritance to his younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he cut flesh from his thigh to cure his mother's illness and yielded his inheritance to his younger brother.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三十九年舉人，為國子監助教，以母老引疾歸。

translations.literal: In the thirty-ninth year of Qianlong he became a provincial graduate, served as assistant instructor in the Imperial Academy, and on account of his mother's age pleaded illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-ninth year of Qianlong he became a provincial graduate, served as assistant instructor in the Imperial Academy, and on account of his mother's age pleaded illness and returned home.

sentences.zh: 豪於飲酒，善鼓琴，時時出遊佳山水，助其詩興。

translations.literal: He was bold in drinking wine, skilled at playing the zither, and from time to time traveled to fine mountains and waters to aid the inspiration of his poetry.
translations.idiomatic: He was bold in drinking wine, skilled at playing the zither, and often traveled to fine mountains and waters to stir his poetic inspiration.

sentences.zh: 其詩由唐人而上溯之，極於古歌謠而止，才力足以相儷。

translations.literal: His poetry traced upward from the Tang and stopped at ancient songs and ballads; his talent and strength were sufficient to match them.
translations.idiomatic: His poetry traced upward from the Tang poets and stopped at ancient songs and ballads; his talent and strength were sufficient to match them.

sentences.zh: 有茗香論詩、學古集、牧牛村舍詩鈔。

translations.literal: He had Tea-Fragrance Discussions on Poetry, Collection of Learning from Antiquity, and Poems from the Oxherd's Village Cottage.
translations.idiomatic: He authored Tea-Fragrance Discussions on Poetry, Collection of Learning from Antiquity, and Poems from the Oxherd's Village Cottage.

sentences.zh: 同縣錢林，字金粟。

translations.literal: Qian Lin of the same county, styled Jinshu.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Lin of the same county, styled Jinshu.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十三年進士，由編修至侍讀學士，左遷庶子。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the thirteenth year of Jiaqing, rose from compiler to attendant reader of the Hanlin Academy, and was demoted to tutor of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in the thirteenth year of Jiaqing, rose from compiler to attendant reader of the Hanlin Academy, and was demoted to tutor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 林熟於本朝名臣言行，及河漕、鹽榷、錢法諸大政。

translations.literal: Lin was thoroughly familiar with the words and deeds of eminent ministers of the present dynasty, as well as major policies such as canal transport, salt monopoly, and currency.
translations.idiomatic: Lin was thoroughly familiar with the words and deeds of eminent ministers of the present dynasty, as well as major policies such as canal transport, salt monopoly, and currency.

sentences.zh: 詩亦醖釀於漢、魏、六朝。

translations.literal: His poetry too was steeped in the Han, Wei, and Six Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: His poetry too was steeped in the styles of the Han, Wei, and Six Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 阮元督學浙江，稱為華實兼茂之士。

translations.literal: When Ruan Yuan supervised education in Zhejiang, he called him a man in whom flower and fruit were equally flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruan Yuan supervised education in Zhejiang, he called him a man in whom literary grace and solid substance were equally flourishing.

sentences.zh: 著文獻徵存錄、玉山草堂詩集。

translations.literal: He authored Records of Literary Survivals and the Yushan Thatched Hall Poetry Collection.
translations.idiomatic: He authored Records of Literary Survivals and the Yushan Thatched Hall Poetry Collection.

sentences.zh: 端木國瑚，青田人。

translations.literal: Duanmu Guohu was a man of Qingtian.
translations.idiomatic: Duanmu Guohu was a native of Qingtian.

sentences.zh: 青田故產鶴，國瑚生而清傲似鶴，其大父字之曰鶴田。

translations.literal: Qingtian formerly produced cranes; Guohu was born pure and aloof like a crane, and his grandfather gave him the courtesy name Hetian, "Crane Field."
translations.idiomatic: Qingtian was famed for its cranes; Guohu was born pure and aloof like a crane, and his grandfather gave him the courtesy name Hetian, "Crane Field."

sentences.zh: 阮元督學得之，恆誇示人曰：「此青田一鶴也！」

translations.literal: When Ruan Yuan obtained him while supervising education, he constantly showed him off to others, saying, "This is a Qingtian crane!"
translations.idiomatic: When Ruan Yuan discovered him while supervising education, he constantly showed him off to others, saying, "This is a Qingtian crane!"

sentences.zh: 命賦使署定香亭，賦成，一時傳誦。

translations.literal: He ordered him to compose a fu on the Dingxiang Pavilion in the commissioner's yamen; when the fu was finished it was transmitted and recited throughout the age.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered him to compose a fu on the Dingxiang Pavilion in the commissioner's yamen; when the fu was finished it was transmitted and recited far and wide.

sentences.zh: 國瑚好學深思，通天文之奧。

translations.literal: Guohu loved learning and thought deeply, and was versed in the mysteries of astronomy.
translations.idiomatic: Guohu loved learning and thought deeply, and was versed in the mysteries of astronomy.

sentences.zh: 嘗被召相山陵，敘勞官中書。

translations.literal: He was once summoned to inspect imperial tombs and was rewarded with appointment as secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He was once summoned to inspect imperial tombs and was rewarded with appointment as secretary.

sentences.zh: 道光十三年進士，選用知縣。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the thirteenth year of Daoguang and was selected for appointment as magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in the thirteenth year of Daoguang and was selected for appointment as magistrate.

sentences.zh: 性不耐劇，投牒就原官。

translations.literal: By nature he could not endure strenuous duties and submitted a petition to resume his former office.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he could not endure strenuous duties and submitted a petition to resume his former office.

sentences.zh: 著周易指，屬稿二十六年而後成。

translations.literal: He authored Pointer to the Book of Changes, drafting it for twenty-six years before it was completed.
translations.idiomatic: He authored Pointer to the Book of Changes, drafting it for twenty-six years before it was completed.

sentences.zh: 詩才清麗，有太鶴山人集。

translations.literal: His poetic talent was clear and beautiful; he had the Collected Works of the Great Crane Mountain Man.
translations.idiomatic: His poetic talent was clear and beautiful; he authored the Collected Works of the Great Crane Mountain Man.

sentences.zh: 又著周易葬說、地理元文，後頗悔之，不輕為人營葬。

translations.literal: He also authored Burial Doctrine in the Book of Changes and Original Text on Geomancy, but later deeply regretted this and would not lightly undertake burial planning for others.
translations.idiomatic: He also authored Burial Doctrine in the Book of Changes and Original Text on Geomancy, but later deeply regretted this and would not lightly undertake burial planning for others.

sentences.zh: 吳文溥，字澹川，嘉興貢生。

translations.literal: Wu Wenpu, styled Danchuan, was a tribute student of Jiaxing.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Wenpu, styled Danchuan, was a tribute student of Jiaxing.

sentences.zh: 亦以詩名。

translations.literal: He too was famed for poetry.
translations.idiomatic: He too was famed for poetry.

sentences.zh: 其為人有韜略，超然不群，能作蘇門長嘯。

translations.literal: As a man he had strategic depth, stood aloof from the crowd, and could perform the long whistle of the Su Gate recluses.
translations.idiomatic: As a man he had strategic depth, stood aloof from the crowd, and could perform the long whistle of the Su Gate recluses.

sentences.zh: 著南野堂集。

translations.literal: He authored the Southern Wilds Hall Collection.
translations.idiomatic: He authored the Southern Wilds Hall Collection.

sentences.zh: 後百有餘年，有，字，人。

translations.literal: More than a hundred years later there was Yao Zhenzong, styled Haiqiao, a man of Shanyin.
translations.idiomatic: More than a hundred years later there was Yao Zhenzong, styled Haiqiao, a native of Shanyin.

sentences.zh: 著、，能訂之失。

translations.literal: He authored Evidential Commentary on the Han Bibliographic Treatise and Evidential Commentary on the Sui Bibliographic Treatise, and was able to correct Zongyuan's errors.
translations.idiomatic: He authored Evidential Commentary on the Han Bibliographic Treatise and Evidential Commentary on the Sui Bibliographic Treatise, and was able to correct Zhang Zongyuan's errors.

sentences.zh: 又補、兩。

translations.literal: He also supplemented the bibliographic treatises for Later Han and the Three Kingdoms.
translations.idiomatic: He also supplemented the bibliographic treatises for Later Han and the Three Kingdoms.

sentences.zh: 目錄之學，卓然大宗。

translations.literal: In the learning of bibliographic catalogues he stood as a great master.
translations.idiomatic: In bibliographic studies he stood as a great master.

sentences.zh: 論者謂足紹二章之傳。

translations.literal: Critics said he was fully able to continue the tradition of the two Zhangs.
translations.idiomatic: Critics said he was fully able to continue the tradition of Zhang Xuecheng and Zhang Zongyuan.

sentences.zh: 而同時有，字。

translations.literal: At the same time there was Wu Lanting of Gui'an, styled Xushi.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time there was Wu Lanting of Gui'an, styled Xushi.

sentences.zh: 三十九年舉人。

translations.literal: He became a provincial graduate in the thirty-ninth year.
translations.idiomatic: He became a provincial graduate in the thirty-ninth year of Qianlong.

sentences.zh: 稽古博聞，多所纂述。

translations.literal: He investigated antiquity with broad learning and compiled and wrote extensively.
translations.idiomatic: He investigated antiquity with broad learning and compiled and wrote extensively.

sentences.zh: 嘗以著有，因更取參校，為四卷。

translations.literal: Wu Zhen of Song had authored Corrections to Errors in the History of the Five Dynasties; Lanting therefore took Xue Juzheng's old history for further collation and produced four juan of supplementary corrections.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zhen of Song had authored Corrections to Errors in the History of the Five Dynasties; Lanting therefore took Xue Juzheng's old history for further collation and produced four juan of supplementary corrections.

sentences.zh: 同邑邃於經，熟於史，一時有「經史」之目。

translations.literal: Ding Jie of the same county was deep in the classics and Lanting was versed in history; for a time they were styled "Ding Classic and Wu History."
translations.idiomatic: Ding Jie of the same county was deep in the classics and Lanting was versed in history; for a time they were styled "Ding Classic and Wu History."

sentences.zh: 元年，與千叟宴。

translations.literal: In the first year he attended the banquet for a thousand elders.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jiaqing he attended the banquet for a thousand elders.

sentences.zh: 他所著又有、、。

translations.literal: His other works include Variant Readings in the History of the Five Dynasties, Reading Notes on the Comprehensive Mirror, and the Nanzhao Thatched Hall Collection.
translations.idiomatic: His other works include Variant Readings in the History of the Five Dynasties, Reading Notes on the Comprehensive Mirror, and the Nanzhao Thatched Hall Collection.

sentences.zh: 馮敏昌，字伯術，欽州人。

translations.literal: Feng Minchang, styled Boshu, was a man of Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Minchang, styled Boshu, was a native of Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 童年補諸生。

translations.literal: In childhood he was enrolled as a common student.
translations.idiomatic: In childhood he was enrolled as a common student.

sentences.zh: 翁方綱按試廉州，以拔貢選入國學。

translations.literal: When Weng Fanggang conducted the examination tour in Lianzhou, Minchang was selected as a nominated tribute student and entered the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: When Weng Fanggang conducted the examination tour in Lianzhou, Minchang was selected as a nominated tribute student and entered the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四十三年進士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the forty-third year of Qianlong he became a jinshi and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-third year of Qianlong he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 大考，改戶部主事，調補刑部。

translations.literal: At the grand examination he was transferred to secretary in the Ministry of Revenue and then reassigned to the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: At the grand examination he was transferred to secretary in the Ministry of Revenue and then reassigned to the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 性至孝友，聞父喪，一痛嘔血，大雪，徒跣竟日。

translations.literal: By nature he was deeply filial and fraternal; on hearing of his father's death he vomited blood in a single burst of grief, and in heavy snow went barefoot all day.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was deeply filial and fraternal; on hearing of his father's death he vomited blood in a single burst of grief, and in heavy snow went barefoot all day.

sentences.zh: 方綱憂曰：「敏昌萬無生理！」

translations.literal: Fanggang said in alarm, "Minchang has not the slightest chance of survival!"
translations.idiomatic: Fanggang said in alarm, "Minchang has not the slightest chance of survival!"

sentences.zh: 則持其母夫人書促令歸省。

translations.literal: He thereupon took a letter from Minchang's mother and urged him to return home to see her.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon took a letter from Minchang's mother and urged him to return home to see her.

sentences.zh: 及丁內艱，廬墓久，遂不復出。

translations.literal: When he entered mourning for his mother, he lived long by the tomb and never took office again.
translations.idiomatic: When he entered mourning for his mother, he lived long by the tomb and never took office again.

sentences.zh: 平生足跡半天下，嘗登岱，題名絕壁；

translations.literal: In life his footsteps covered half the empire; he once climbed Mount Tai and inscribed his name on a sheer cliff;
translations.idiomatic: In life his footsteps covered half the empire; he once climbed Mount Tai and inscribed his name on a sheer cliff;

sentences.zh: 遊廬阜，觀瀑布；

translations.literal: traveled to Mount Lu and viewed the waterfalls;
translations.idiomatic: traveled to Mount Lu and viewed the waterfalls;

sentences.zh: 抵華嶽，攀鐵纖，躋峽。

translations.literal: reached Mount Hua, climbed the iron cables, and ascended Qiong Gorge.
translations.idiomatic: reached Mount Hua, climbed the iron cables, and ascended Qiong Gorge.

sentences.zh: 在河陽時，親歷王屋、大行諸山。

translations.literal: While in Heyang he personally traversed Mount Wangwu, the Taihang range, and other mountains.
translations.idiomatic: While serving in Heyang he personally traversed Mount Wangwu, the Taihang range, and other mountains.

sentences.zh: 又以北岳去孟縣不千里，騎駿馬直造曲陽飛石之巔，窮雁門、長城而返。

translations.literal: Because Mount Heng was less than a thousand li from Meng County, he rode a swift horse straight to the Flying Stone summit at Quyang, explored Yanmen and the Great Wall, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Because Mount Heng lay less than a thousand li from Meng County, he rode a swift horse straight to the Flying Stone summit at Quyang, explored Yanmen and the Great Wall, and returned.

sentences.zh: 最後宿南嶽廟，升祝融峰，觀雲海。

translations.literal: At last he lodged at the Southern Marchmount Temple, ascended Zhurong Peak, and viewed the sea of clouds.
translations.idiomatic: At last he lodged at the Southern Marchmount Temple, ascended Zhurong Peak, and viewed the sea of clouds.

sentences.zh: 其悱惻之情，曠逸之抱，一寓於詩。

translations.literal: His tender feeling and his free, far-ranging spirit were all lodged in his poetry.
translations.idiomatic: His tender feeling and his free, far-ranging spirit found their full expression in his poetry.

sentences.zh: 著有小羅浮草堂詩集、孟縣志、華山小志、河陽金石錄。

translations.literal: He authored the Little Luofu Thatched Hall Poetry Collection, Gazetteer of Meng County, Short Account of Mount Hua, and Records of Metal and Stone in Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: He authored the Little Luofu Thatched Hall Poetry Collection, Gazetteer of Meng County, Short Account of Mount Hua, and Records of Metal and Stone in Heyang.

sentences.zh: 學者稱魚山先生。

translations.literal: Scholars called him Master Yushan.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars called him Master Yushan.

sentences.zh: 其後嶺南以詩名家者，有嘉應宋湘，字煥襄。

translations.literal: Later among those who became famed for poetry in Lingnan there was Song Xiang of Jiaying, styled Huanxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Later among those who became famed for poetry in Lingnan there was Song Xiang of Jiaying, styled Huanxiang.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶四年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the fourth year of Jiaqing.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the fourth year of Jiaqing.

sentences.zh: 以編修典試四川、貴州，出知曲靖府。

translations.literal: As compiler he presided over the provincial examinations in Sichuan and Guizhou, then went out to serve as prefect of Qujing.
translations.idiomatic: As compiler he presided over the provincial examinations in Sichuan and Guizhou, then went out to serve as prefect of Qujing.

sentences.zh: 教屬地種木棉，人稱「宋公佈」。

translations.literal: He taught his jurisdiction to plant cotton, and the people called it "Lord Song's cloth."
translations.idiomatic: He taught his jurisdiction to plant cotton, and the people called it "Lord Song's cloth."

sentences.zh: 署廣南、永昌，皆有績。

translations.literal: While acting in Guangnan and Yongchang he achieved merit in both posts.
translations.idiomatic: While acting in Guangnan and Yongchang he achieved merit in both posts.

sentences.zh: 永昌灣甸土州知州死，遠族景在東謀襲其職，據境專殺自恣，如是者五六年。

translations.literal: When the native prefect of Wandian in Yongchang died, a distant kinsman named Jing Zaidong plotted to seize the office, held the territory, and killed at will for five or six years.
translations.idiomatic: When the native prefect of Wandian in Yongchang died, a distant kinsman named Jing Zaidong plotted to seize the office, held the territory, and killed at will for five or six years.

sentences.zh: 當事怯，莫敢發。

translations.literal: The local authorities were timid and no one dared move against him.
translations.idiomatic: The local authorities were timid and no one dared move against him.

sentences.zh: 民、夷赴愬，湘請諸鎮帥，不允；

translations.literal: When commoners and tribesmen came to lodge complaints, Xiang appealed to the regional commander, but was refused;
translations.idiomatic: When commoners and tribesmen came to lodge complaints, Xiang appealed to the regional commander, but was refused;

sentences.zh: 乃率僚屬遊宴棲賢山，從容賦詩，密約鄉兵乘夜兼行，出不意，擒在東斬之，費銀八千兩，不取償公家，邊隅以靖。

translations.literal: he then led his subordinates on an excursion and banquet at Qixian Mountain, composed poetry at leisure, secretly arranged with local militia to march together by night, caught Zaidong off guard, seized and executed him, spent eight thousand taels of silver, and did not seek reimbursement from the government; the border was thereby pacified.
translations.idiomatic: he then led his subordinates on an excursion and banquet at Qixian Mountain, composed poetry at leisure, secretly arranged with local militia to march together by night, caught Zaidong off guard, seized and executed him, spent eight thousand taels of silver without seeking reimbursement from the government, and thereby pacified the border.

sentences.zh: 終湖北督糧道。

translations.literal: He ended his career as grain intendant of Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as grain intendant of Hubei.

sentences.zh: 詩學少陵，有不易居集。

translations.literal: His poetry followed Du Fu; he had the Collection of the Not-Easy Abode.
translations.idiomatic: His poetry followed Du Fu; he authored the Collection of the Not-Easy Abode.

sentences.zh: 敏昌同時又有趙希璜，字渭川，長寧人。

translations.literal: At the same time as Minchang there was also Zhao Xihuang, styled Weichuan, a man of Changning.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time as Minchang there was also Zhao Xihuang, styled Weichuan, a native of Changning.

sentences.zh: 少讀書羅浮山，與順德黎簡友善。

translations.literal: In youth he studied on Mount Luofu and was on friendly terms with Li Jian of Shunde.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he studied on Mount Luofu and was on friendly terms with Li Jian of Shunde.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四十四年舉人。

translations.literal: He became a provincial graduate in the forty-fourth year of Qianlong.
translations.idiomatic: He became a provincial graduate in the forty-fourth year of Qianlong.

sentences.zh: 知安陽縣，邑志久未修，希璜聘武億共成之。

translations.literal: As magistrate of Anyang County, where the local gazetteer had long gone unrevised, Xihuang engaged Wu Yi to complete it with him.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate of Anyang County, where the local gazetteer had long gone unrevised, Xihuang engaged Wu Yi to complete it with him.

sentences.zh: 紀昀推其體例合古法。

translations.literal: Ji Yun praised its format as conforming to ancient methods.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Yun praised its format as conforming to ancient methods.

sentences.zh: 末附金石錄十二卷，尤精確。

translations.literal: At the end was appended a twelve-juan record of metal and stone inscriptions, especially precise.
translations.idiomatic: At the end was appended a twelve-juan record of metal and stone inscriptions, especially precise.

sentences.zh: 希璜工詩，著有四百三十二峰草堂詩鈔。

translations.literal: Xihuang was skilled at poetry and authored the Four Hundred Thirty-Two Peaks Thatched Hall Poetry Manuscript.
translations.idiomatic: Xihuang was skilled at poetry and authored the Four Hundred Thirty-Two Peaks Thatched Hall Poetry Manuscript.

sentences.zh: 法式善，字開文，蒙古烏爾濟氏，隸內務府正黃旗。

translations.literal: Fa Shishan, styled Kaiwen, of the Mongol Wuerji clan, was registered in the Plain Yellow Banner of the Imperial Household Department.
translations.idiomatic: Fa Shishan, styled Kaiwen, of the Mongol Wuerji clan, was registered in the Plain Yellow Banner of the Imperial Household Department.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四十五年進士，授檢討，遷司業。

translations.literal: In the forty-fifth year of Qianlong he became a jinshi, was appointed reviser, and was promoted to vice director of studies.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fifth year of Qianlong he passed the jinshi examination, was appointed reviser, and was promoted to vice director of studies.

sentences.zh: 五十年，高宗臨雍，率諸生七十馀人聽講，禮成，賞賚有差。

translations.literal: In the fiftieth year, when the Gaozong Emperor lectured at the Imperial Academy, he led more than seventy students to listen; when the ceremony was completed, rewards were granted according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the fiftieth year of Qianlong, when Emperor Gaozong lectured at the Imperial Academy, Shishan led more than seventy students to listen; when the ceremony was completed, rewards were granted according to rank.

sentences.zh: 本名運昌，命改今名，國語言「竭力有為」也。

translations.literal: His original name was Yunchang; he was ordered to change it to his present name, which in Manchu means "to exert oneself and act with purpose."
translations.idiomatic: His original name was Yunchang; he was ordered to change it to his present name, which in Manchu means "to exert oneself and act with purpose."

sentences.zh: 由庶子遷侍讀學士，大考降員外郎，阿桂薦補左庶子。

translations.literal: From tutor of the heir apparent he was promoted to attendant reader of the Hanlin Academy; at the grand examination he was demoted to vice director of a ministry, then recommended by Agui for appointment as left tutor of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: From tutor of the heir apparent he was promoted to attendant reader of the Hanlin Academy; at the grand examination he was demoted to vice director of a ministry, then recommended by Agui for appointment as left tutor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 性好文，以宏獎風流為己任。

translations.literal: By nature he loved literature and took it as his mission to encourage talent and refinement on a grand scale.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he loved literature and took it as his mission to encourage talent and refinement on a grand scale.

sentences.zh: 顧數奇，官至四品即左遷。

translations.literal: Yet his fate was unlucky: whenever he reached the fourth rank he was demoted.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his fate was unlucky: whenever he reached the fourth rank he was demoted.

sentences.zh: 其後兩為侍講學士，一以大考改贊善，一坐修書不謹貶庶子，遂乞病歸。

translations.literal: Afterward he twice served as lecturer of the Hanlin Academy; once he was demoted to tutor at the grand examination, once he was reduced to tutor of the heir apparent for carelessness in book compilation, and he then pleaded illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he twice served as lecturer of the Hanlin Academy; once he was demoted to tutor at the grand examination, once he was reduced to tutor of the heir apparent for carelessness in book compilation, and he then pleaded illness and returned home.

sentences.zh: 所居後載門北，明李東陽西涯舊址也。

translations.literal: His residence was north of Houzai Gate, on the old site of Li Dongyang's Xiya Studio of the Ming.
translations.idiomatic: His residence was north of Houzai Gate, on the old site of Li Dongyang's Xiya Studio of the Ming.

sentences.zh: 構詩龕及梧門書屋，法書名畫盈棟幾，得海內名流詠贈，即投詩龕中。

translations.literal: He built a poetry shrine and the Wumen Studio; fine calligraphy and famous paintings filled beams and tables, and whenever he received poems of praise and gift from leading figures throughout the empire, he placed them in the poetry shrine.
translations.idiomatic: He built a poetry shrine and the Wumen Studio; fine calligraphy and famous paintings filled beams and tables, and whenever he received poems of praise and gift from leading figures throughout the empire, he placed them in the poetry shrine.

sentences.zh: 主盟壇坫三十年，論者謂接跡西涯無愧色。

translations.literal: For thirty years he presided over the literary world, and critics said he followed in Xiya's footsteps without shame.
translations.idiomatic: For thirty years he presided over the literary world, and critics said he followed in Xiya's footsteps without shame.

sentences.zh: 著清秘述聞、槐廳載筆、存素堂詩集。

translations.literal: He authored Clear Secret Narratives, Brush Notes from the Pagoda Hall, and the Cunsu Hall Poetry Collection.
translations.idiomatic: He authored Clear Secret Narratives, Brush Notes from the Pagoda Hall, and the Cunsu Hall Poetry Collection.

sentences.zh: 平生於詩所激賞者，舒位、王曇、孫原湘，作三君子詠以張之。

translations.literal: Among poets he most admired in life were Shu Wei, Wang Tan, and Sun Yuanxiang; he composed Odes to Three Gentlemen to spread their fame.
translations.idiomatic: Among poets he most admired in life were Shu Wei, Wang Tan, and Sun Yuanxiang; he composed Odes to Three Gentlemen to spread their fame.

sentences.zh: 然位艷曇狂，惟原湘以才氣寫性靈，能以韻勝，著天真閣集。

translations.literal: Yet Wei was florid and Tan wild; only Yuanxiang wrote native spirit with literary talent and could prevail through resonance; he authored the Tianzhen Pavilion Collection.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Wei was florid and Tan wild; only Yuanxiang wrote native spirit with literary talent and could prevail through resonance; he authored the Tianzhen Pavilion Collection.

sentences.zh: 原湘，字子瀟，昭文人。

translations.literal: Yuanxiang, styled Zixiao, was a man of Zhaowen.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxiang, styled Zixiao, was a native of Zhaowen.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the tenth year of Jiaqing.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the tenth year of Jiaqing.

sentences.zh: 選庶吉士，未仕。

translations.literal: He was selected as a Hanlin bachelor but never took office.
translations.idiomatic: He was selected as a Hanlin bachelor but never took office.

sentences.zh: 同時江蘇與原湘負才名者，有吳江郭麟，字祥伯。

translations.literal: At the same time in Jiangsu, one who shared Yuanxiang's reputation for talent was Guo Lin of Wujiang, styled Xiangbo.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time in Jiangsu, one who shared Yuanxiang's reputation for talent was Guo Lin of Wujiang, styled Xiangbo.

sentences.zh: 附監生。

translations.literal: He was an attached student of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He was an attached student of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 一眉瑩白如雪，風采超俊。

translations.literal: One eyebrow shone white as snow, and his bearing was surpassingly handsome.
translations.idiomatic: One eyebrow shone white as snow, and his bearing was surpassingly handsome.

sentences.zh: 家貧客遊，人爭倒屣。

translations.literal: His family was poor and he traveled as a guest; people vied to receive him with haste.
translations.idiomatic: His family was poor and he traveled as a guest; people vied to receive him with haste.

sentences.zh: 詩學李長吉、沈下賢，詞尤清婉。

translations.literal: His poetry followed Li He and Shen Quanqi, and his song lyrics were especially clear and graceful.
translations.idiomatic: His poetry followed Li He and Shen Quanqi, and his song lyrics were especially clear and graceful.

sentences.zh: 著靈芬館集。

translations.literal: He authored the Lingfen Hall Collection.
translations.idiomatic: He authored the Lingfen Hall Collection.

sentences.zh: 嘗病潘昂霄金石例之隘，因據洪氏隸釋為金石例補，又撰詞品十二則，以繼司空表聖之詩品。

translations.literal: He once found Pan Angxiao's Epigraphic Precedents too narrow and, relying on Hong Kuo's Explanation of Clerical Script, produced a Supplement to Epigraphic Precedents; he also drafted twelve rules on song lyrics to continue Sikong Tu's Grades of Poetry.
translations.idiomatic: He once found Pan Angxiao's Epigraphic Precedents too narrow and, relying on Hong Kuo's Explanation of Clerical Script, produced a Supplement to Epigraphic Precedents; he also drafted twelve rules on song lyrics to continue Sikong Tu's Grades of Poetry.

sentences.zh: 惲敬，字子居，陽湖人。

translations.literal: Yun Jing, styled Ziju, was a man of Yanghu.
translations.idiomatic: Yun Jing, styled Ziju, was a native of Yanghu.

sentences.zh: 幼從舅氏鄭環學，持論能獨出己見。

translations.literal: In youth he studied under his maternal uncle Zheng Huan and in argument could put forward views entirely his own.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he studied under his maternal uncle Zheng Huan and in argument could put forward views entirely his own.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四十八年舉人，以教習官京師。

translations.literal: In the forty-eighth year of Qianlong he became a provincial graduate and served as an instructor in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-eighth year of Qianlong he became a provincial graduate and served as an instructor in the capital.

sentences.zh: 時同縣莊述祖、有可、張惠言，海鹽陳石麟，桐城王灼集輦下，敬與為友，商榷經義，以古文鳴於時。

translations.literal: At the time Zhuang Shuzu, You Ke, and Zhang Huiyan of his county, Chen Shilin of Haiyan, and Wang Zhuo of Tongcheng all gathered in the capital; Jing befriended them, discussed classical meaning, and was renowned for ancient-style prose in his age.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Zhuang Shuzu, You Ke, and Zhang Huiyan of his county, Chen Shilin of Haiyan, and Wang Zhuo of Tongcheng all gathered in the capital; Jing befriended them, discussed classical meaning, and was renowned for ancient-style prose in his age.

sentences.zh: 既而選令富陽，銳欲圖治，不隨群輩俯仰。

translations.literal: Before long he was selected as magistrate of Fuyang and keenly sought to govern well, refusing to defer to the crowd.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was selected as magistrate of Fuyang and keenly sought to govern well, refusing to defer to the crowd.

sentences.zh: 大吏怒其強項，務裁抑之，令督解黔餉。

translations.literal: The grand official, angered by his stubbornness, sought to restrain him and ordered him to supervise the transport of Guizhou provisions.
translations.idiomatic: The grand official, angered by his stubbornness, sought to restrain him and ordered him to supervise the transport of Guizhou provisions.

sentences.zh: 敬曰：「王事也。」

translations.literal: Jing said, "It is the king's business."
translations.idiomatic: Jing said, "It is the king's business."

sentences.zh: 怡然就道。

translations.literal: He set out on the road with easy contentment.
translations.idiomatic: He set out on the road with easy contentment.

sentences.zh: 後遭父喪，服闋，選新喻。

translations.literal: Later he suffered his father's death; when mourning ended he was selected for Xinyu.
translations.idiomatic: Later he suffered his father's death; when mourning ended he was selected for Xinyu.

sentences.zh: 吏民素橫暴，繩以法，人疑其過猛。

translations.literal: Officials and people there had long been violent and overbearing; he bound them with law, and some thought him too harsh.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and people there had long been violent and overbearing; he bound them with law, and some thought him too harsh.

sentences.zh: 已乃進秀異士與論文藝，俗習大變。

translations.literal: Then he advanced outstanding scholars to discuss literature and the arts, and local custom changed greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Then he advanced outstanding scholars to discuss literature and the arts, and local custom changed greatly.

sentences.zh: 調知瑞金，有富民進千金求脫罪，峻拒之。

translations.literal: He was transferred to serve as magistrate of Ruijin; a wealthy man offered a thousand in gold to escape punishment, and he sternly refused.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as magistrate of Ruijin; a wealthy man offered a thousand in gold to escape punishment, and he sternly refused.

sentences.zh: 關說者以萬金相啗，敬曰：「節士苞苴不逮門，吾豈有遺行耶！」

translations.literal: A go-between tried to bribe him with ten thousand in gold; Jing said, "A man of integrity does not let gifts reach his door—how could I leave any stain on my conduct!"
translations.idiomatic: A go-between tried to bribe him with ten thousand in gold; Jing said, "A man of integrity does not let gifts reach his door—how could I leave any stain on my conduct!"

sentences.zh: 卒論如法。

translations.literal: In the end the case was decided according to law.
translations.idiomatic: In the end the case was decided according to law.

sentences.zh: 由是廉聲大著。

translations.literal: From this his reputation for integrity became greatly renowned.
translations.idiomatic: From this his reputation for integrity became greatly renowned.

sentences.zh: 卓異，擢南昌同知。

translations.literal: Marked as outstanding, he was promoted to vice prefect of Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: Marked as outstanding, he was promoted to vice prefect of Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 敬為人負氣，所至輒忤上官，以其才高優容之，然忌者遂銜之次骨。

translations.literal: Jing as a man was proud; wherever he went he offended superiors, yet because his talent was high they indulged him; still, the envious came to hate him to the bone.
translations.idiomatic: Jing as a man was proud; wherever he went he offended superiors, yet because his talent was high they indulged him; still, the envious came to hate him to the bone.

sentences.zh: 最後署吳城同知，坐奸民誣訴隸詐財失察被劾。

translations.literal: At last while acting as vice prefect of Wucheng he was impeached for failing to detect a clerk's extortion in a false accusation by a wicked commoner.
translations.idiomatic: At last while acting as vice prefect of Wucheng he was impeached for failing to detect a clerk's extortion in a false accusation by a wicked commoner.

sentences.zh: 忌者聞而喜曰：「惲子居大賢，乃以贓敗耶！」

translations.literal: Those who envied him heard and rejoiced, saying, "Master Ziju the great worthy—has he fallen through corruption after all!"
translations.idiomatic: Those who envied him heard and rejoiced, saying, "Master Ziju the great worthy—has he fallen through corruption after all!"

sentences.zh: 敬既罷官，益肆其力於文。

translations.literal: After Jing was dismissed from office, he devoted his strength all the more to writing.
translations.idiomatic: After Jing was dismissed from office, he devoted his strength all the more to writing.

sentences.zh: 深求前史興壞治亂之故，旁及縱橫、名法、兵農、陰陽家言。

translations.literal: He deeply sought the causes of rise, ruin, order, and disorder in former histories, and ranged also through the doctrines of strategists, legalists, military and agricultural thinkers, and yin-yang masters.
translations.idiomatic: He deeply sought the causes of rise, ruin, order, and disorder in former histories, and ranged also through the doctrines of strategists, legalists, military and agricultural thinkers, and yin-yang masters.

sentences.zh: 會其友惠言歿，於是敬慨然曰：「古文自元、明以來漸失其傳，吾向所以不多為者，有惠言在也。

translations.literal: When his friend Huiyan died, Jing said with emotion, "Ancient-style prose since the Yuan and Ming has gradually lost its transmission; the reason I have not written much hitherto is that Huiyan was still alive.
translations.idiomatic: When his friend Huiyan died, Jing said with emotion, "Ancient-style prose since the Yuan and Ming has gradually lost its transmission; the reason I have not written much hitherto is that Huiyan was still alive.

sentences.zh: 今惠言死，吾安敢不並力治之？」

translations.literal: Now that Huiyan is dead, how dare I not devote myself fully to restoring it?"
translations.idiomatic: Now that Huiyan is dead, how dare I not devote myself fully to restoring it?"

sentences.zh: 其文蓋出於韓非、李斯，與蘇洵為近。

translations.literal: His writing generally derived from Han Fei and Li Si and was close to Su Xun.
translations.idiomatic: His writing generally derived from Han Fei and Li Si and was close to Su Xun.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十一。

translations.literal: He died at the age of sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 著大雲山房稿。

translations.literal: He authored Drafts from the Great Cloud Mountain Studio.
translations.idiomatic: He authored Drafts from the Great Cloud Mountain Studio.

sentences.zh: 其治獄曰子居決事，附集後。

translations.literal: His judicial decisions, titled Ziju's Rulings, were appended after the collection.
translations.idiomatic: His judicial decisions, titled Ziju's Rulings, were appended after the collection.

sentences.zh: 趙懷玉，字億孫，武進人，尚書申喬四世孫。

translations.literal: Zhao Huaiyu, styled Yisun, was a man of Wujin and fourth-generation descendant of Minister Shen Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Huaiyu, styled Yisun, was a native of Wujin and fourth-generation descendant of Minister Shen Qiao.

sentences.zh: 乾隆中召試舉人，授中書。

translations.literal: In the Qianlong reign he was summoned to special examination as provincial graduate and appointed secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In the Qianlong reign he was summoned to special examination as provincial graduate and appointed secretary.

sentences.zh: 久之，出為青州府同知，以憂歸，終於家。

translations.literal: After a long time he went out to serve as vice prefect of Qingzhou, returned home on account of mourning, and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time he went out to serve as vice prefect of Qingzhou, returned home on account of mourning, and died at home.

sentences.zh: 性坦易，工古文辭。

translations.literal: By nature he was open and easy, and skilled at ancient-style prose.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was open and easy, and skilled at ancient-style prose.

sentences.zh: 嘗自言不敢好名為欺人之事，不敢好奇為欺世之學。

translations.literal: He once said of himself that he dared not love fame and do things that deceive people, nor dared seek novelty and pursue learning that deceives the world.
translations.idiomatic: He once said of himself that he dared not love fame and do things that deceive people, nor dared seek novelty and pursue learning that deceives the world.

sentences.zh: 惲敬稱其文無有雜言诐義離真反正者。

translations.literal: Yun Jing praised his writing as having no mixed language, crooked meaning, or departure from truth and return to the straight.
translations.idiomatic: Yun Jing praised his writing as having no mixed language, crooked meaning, or departure from truth and return to the straight.

sentences.zh: 著有生齋文集。

translations.literal: He authored the Shengsheng Studio Collected Prose.
translations.idiomatic: He authored the Shengsheng Studio Collected Prose.

sentences.zh: 黎簡，字簡民，順德人。

translations.literal: Li Jian, styled Jianmin, was a man of Shunde.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jian, styled Jianmin, was a native of Shunde.

sentences.zh: 十歲能詩。

translations.literal: At ten he could compose poetry.
translations.idiomatic: At ten he could compose poetry.

sentences.zh: 益都李文藻令朝陽，見簡詩，曰：「必傳之作也。」

translations.literal: When Li Wenzao of Yidu was magistrate of Chaoyang and saw Jian's poetry, he said, "This is work that will surely be transmitted."
translations.idiomatic: When Li Wenzao of Yidu was magistrate of Chaoyang and saw Jian's poetry, he said, "This is work that will surely be transmitted."

sentences.zh: 勸令就試。

translations.literal: He urged him to take the examinations.
translations.idiomatic: He urged him to take the examinations.

sentences.zh: 學使李調元得其擬昌黎石鼎聯句，奇賞之。

translations.literal: Education commissioner Li Tiaoyuan obtained his imitation of Han Yu's linked verses on the Stone Tripod and admired it as extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Education commissioner Li Tiaoyuan obtained his imitation of Han Yu's linked verses on the Stone Tripod and admired it as extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 補弟子員，人號之曰黎石鼎。

translations.literal: He was enrolled as a student and people styled him Li Shiding.
translations.idiomatic: He was enrolled as a student and people styled him Li Shiding.

sentences.zh: 久之，膺選拔。

translations.literal: After a long time he was selected by nomination.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time he was selected by nomination.

sentences.zh: 尋丁外艱，遂終於家，足不踰嶺。

translations.literal: Soon after he entered mourning for his maternal grandfather, he ended his days at home and his feet never crossed the mountain passes.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he went into mourning for his maternal grandfather, spent the rest of his life at home, and never again crossed the Lingnan passes.

sentences.zh: 海內名流，欽其高節。

translations.literal: Luminaries throughout the realm admired his lofty integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Leading figures across the empire admired his uncompromising integrity.

sentences.zh: 袁枚負盛名，遊羅浮，邀與相見，謝不往也。

translations.literal: Yuan Mei, bearing great fame, traveled to Luofu and invited him to meet; he declined and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Mei, then at the height of his fame, was touring Luofu and invited Li Jian to meet him; Li Jian politely declined.

sentences.zh: 著五百四峰草堂詩文鈔。

translations.literal: He authored the Five Hundred Four Peaks Thatched Hall Collected Poetry and Prose.
translations.idiomatic: He authored the Collected Poetry and Prose of the Five Hundred Four Peaks Thatched Hall.

sentences.zh: 所與交同邑張錦芳、黃丹書，番禺呂堅皆以詩名。

translations.literal: Those with whom he associated—Jinfang and Danshu of his native county and Jian of Panyu—were all famed for poetry.
translations.idiomatic: His close companions included Jinfang and Danshu of his native county and Jian of Panyu—all men renowned for their poetry.

sentences.zh: 錦芳，字粲夫。

translations.literal: Jinfang, styled Canfu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jinfang, whose style was Canfu,

sentences.zh: 乾隆中進士，官編修。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the Qianlong era, he served as compiler.
translations.idiomatic: became a metropolitan graduate during the Qianlong reign and served as a Hanlin compiler.

sentences.zh: 通說文，喜金石文字。

translations.literal: He mastered the Shuowen and delighted in bronze-and-stone inscriptions.
translations.idiomatic: He was versed in the Shuowen and devoted to bronze and stone inscriptions.

sentences.zh: 弟錦麟，字瑞夫。

translations.literal: His younger brother Jinlin, styled Ruifu.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Jinlin, whose style was Ruifu,

sentences.zh: 舉人。

translations.literal: A provincial graduate.
translations.idiomatic: was a provincial graduate.

sentences.zh: 兄弟並為翁方綱所器異。

translations.literal: Both brothers were specially valued by Weng Fanggang.
translations.idiomatic: Both brothers won special regard from Weng Fanggang.

sentences.zh: 錦麟以賦「碧天如水雁初飛」句得名，時呼張碧天。

translations.literal: Jinlin earned a name for his fu poem with the line "The blue sky is like water, and the geese first fly;" at the time people called him Zhang Biantian.
translations.idiomatic: Jinlin won renown for a fu poem containing the line "The blue sky is like water, and wild geese first take flight," and people at the time called him Zhang Biantian.

sentences.zh: 早卒。

translations.literal: He died young.
translations.idiomatic: He died in early manhood.

sentences.zh: 錦芳著逃虛閣詩鈔，與欽州馮敏昌、同邑胡亦常稱「嶺南三子」。

translations.literal: Jinfang authored the Taoxu Pavilion Collected Poetry, and together with Feng Minchang of Qinzhou and Hu Yichang of the same county was called the Three Masters of Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Jinfang authored the Collected Poetry of the Taoxu Pavilion and, together with Feng Minchang of Qinzhou and Hu Yichang of his native county, was known as one of the Three Masters of Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 丹書，字廷授。

translations.literal: Danshu, styled Tingshou.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Danshu, whose style was Tingshou,

sentences.zh: 亦以詩受知調元。

translations.literal: He too gained recognition through poetry from Tiaoyuan.
translations.idiomatic: likewise won recognition for his poetry from Li Tiaoyuan.

sentences.zh: 貢優行，事親孝，居喪能盡哀。

translations.literal: Enrolled as a tribute student of outstanding conduct, he was filial in serving his parents and, when in mourning, fully expressed grief.
translations.idiomatic: Nominated as a tribute student of outstanding conduct, he was filial toward his parents and mourned them with full depth of grief.

sentences.zh: 後舉於鄉。

translations.literal: Later he passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: He later passed the provincial examinations.

sentences.zh: 至都，朝貴爭延之，辭不就。

translations.literal: When he reached the capital, court nobles competed to summon him, but he declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: After he reached the capital, leading court figures all sought to bring him into their households, but he declined every invitation.

sentences.zh: 嘗曰：「貧與富交則損名，賤與貴交則損節。」

translations.literal: He once said, "When the poor associate with the rich, reputation is damaged; when the lowly associate with the noble, integrity is damaged."
translations.idiomatic: He once said, "When the poor consort with the rich, they lose standing; when the humble seek out the great, they lose their integrity."

sentences.zh: 晚官教諭，兼工書畫。

translations.literal: In later years he served as instructor and was also skilled at calligraphy and painting.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he served as a district instructor and was also accomplished in calligraphy and painting.

sentences.zh: 著鴻雪齋詩鈔。

translations.literal: He authored the Hongxue Studio Collected Poetry.
translations.idiomatic: He authored the Collected Poetry of the Hongxue Studio.

sentences.zh: 堅，字介卿。

translations.literal: Jian, styled Jieqing.
translations.idiomatic: Lv Jian, whose style was Jieqing,

sentences.zh: 歲貢生，窮老不遇。

translations.literal: A senior tribute student, he grew old in poverty without preferment.
translations.idiomatic: was a senior tribute student who lived out his days in poverty without ever winning office.

sentences.zh: 著遲刪集。

translations.literal: He authored the Chishan Collection.
translations.idiomatic: He authored the Chishan Collection.

sentences.zh: 亦常，字同謙。

translations.literal: Yichang, styled Tongqian.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Yichang, whose style was Tongqian,

sentences.zh: 舉人。

translations.literal: A provincial graduate.
translations.idiomatic: was a provincial graduate.

sentences.zh: 落第南歸，與戴震同舟，至富春江乃別。

translations.literal: Failing the metropolitan examination, he returned south and shared a boat with Dai Zhen; they parted only upon reaching the Fuchun River.
translations.idiomatic: After failing the metropolitan examination he traveled south, sharing a boat with Dai Zhen; the two did not part until they reached the Fuchun River.

sentences.zh: 舟中手寫震所著書，謀刊之。

translations.literal: On the boat he copied by hand the works Zhen had written, intending to publish them.
translations.idiomatic: Aboard the boat he painstakingly copied Dai Zhen's writings by hand, intending to publish them.

sentences.zh: 多敢瓜果解渴，得胃寒疾，抵家卒。

translations.literal: He ate much fruit to quench thirst, contracted a cold stomach ailment, and died upon reaching home.
translations.idiomatic: He ate too much fruit to slake his thirst, contracted a chill in the stomach, and died shortly after reaching home.

sentences.zh: 有賜書樓集。

translations.literal: He left the Cishu Studio Collection.
translations.idiomatic: His works include the Cishu Studio Collection.

sentences.zh: 張士元，字翰宣，震澤人。

translations.literal: Zhang Shiyuan, styled Hanxuan, was a man of Zhenze.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shiyuan, whose style was Hanxuan, came from Zhenze.

sentences.zh: 工古文辭，師法歸有光。

translations.literal: He was skilled at ancient-style prose, taking Gui Youguang as his model.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at ancient-style prose and took Gui Youguang as his master.

sentences.zh: 歲正，陳其集几上，北面拜之。

translations.literal: At New Year he laid out his collection on the table and bowed to it facing north.
translations.idiomatic: Each New Year he would place Gui Youguang's collected works on his desk and bow to them facing north.

sentences.zh: 又用歸氏評點史記法，上推之左氏，下逮韓、歐，無不合者。

translations.literal: He also applied the Gui family's method of annotating the Records of the Grand Historian, extending it upward to the Zuo Commentary and downward through Han Yu and the Ouyangs; nothing failed to fit.
translations.idiomatic: He also adopted the Gui family's method of annotating the Records of the Grand Historian, extending it upward to the Zuo Commentary and downward through Han Yu and the Song Ouyangs, and found that the method held throughout.

sentences.zh: 乾隆五十三年舉人，久不第，留京師館董誥第八年。

translations.literal: A provincial graduate in the fifty-third year of Qianlong, he long failed the metropolitan examination and remained in the capital tutoring in Dong Gao's household for eight years.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examination in the fifty-third year of Qianlong but failed again and again at the metropolitan level; he remained in the capital as a tutor in Dong Gao's household for eight years.

sentences.zh: 誥主會試，欲令士元出門下，不能得也。

translations.literal: Gao served as chief examiner of the metropolitan examination and wished to enroll Shiyuan as his disciple, but could not obtain this.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao served as chief examiner for the metropolitan examination, he wished to claim Shiyuan as his protégé, but could not manage it.

sentences.zh: 姚文田督學江南，士元與有舊，戒諸子勿應試。

translations.literal: Yao Wentian supervised education in Jiangnan; Shiyuan had old ties with him and warned his sons not to take the examinations.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Wentian was education commissioner for Jiangnan; Shiyuan was old friends with him and warned Yao's sons not to sit for the examinations.

sentences.zh: 年老，銓教諭，以耳聵謝不就。

translations.literal: When he grew old, he was selected for instructor but declined on account of deafness.
translations.idiomatic: In old age he was selected for a post as instructor, but he declined on the grounds that he had grown deaf.

sentences.zh: 曰：「國家設學校，使師弟子相從講學，豈漫以廩祿拯寒生哉？」

translations.literal: He said, "The state establishes schools so that teachers and students may study together—is it merely to use grain stipends to rescue impoverished scholars?"
translations.idiomatic: He said, "The state founds schools so that teachers and pupils may pursue learning together—are those posts meant only to offer grain stipends to scholars in need?"

sentences.zh: 乃歸老爛谿之上，撰述自娛。

translations.literal: He then returned to spend his old age above Lanxi and amused himself with writing.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore retired to Lanxi and spent his remaining years writing for his own pleasure.

sentences.zh: 學者稱鱸江先生。

translations.literal: Scholars called him Master Lujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars addressed him as Master Lujiang.

sentences.zh: 性澹泊寡交，獨與王芑孫、秦瀛、陳用光以學問相切劘。

translations.literal: By nature retiring and with few associations, he alone with Wang Qisun, Qin Ying, and Chen Yongguang sharpened one another through scholarly exchange.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was austere and kept few social ties; only with Wang Qisun, Qin Ying, and Chen Yongguang did he engage in earnest scholarly exchange.

sentences.zh: 姚鼐見其文，亦擬之震川。

translations.literal: Yao Nai, seeing his prose, likewise compared him to Zhenchuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Nai read his prose, he too compared it to Gui Youguang's.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十。

translations.literal: He died at seventy.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy.

sentences.zh: 著嘉樹山房集。

translations.literal: He authored the Jiashu Mountain Studio Collection.
translations.idiomatic: He authored the Jiashu Mountain Studio Collection.

sentences.zh: 同邑張海珊，字越來；

translations.literal: Zhang Haishan of the same county, styled Yuelai;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Haishan of the same county, whose style was Yuelai;

sentences.zh: 張履，字淵甫：皆舉人。

translations.literal: Zhang Lv, styled Yuanfu: both were provincial graduates.
translations.idiomatic: and Zhang Lv, whose style was Yuanfu—both were provincial graduates.

sentences.zh: 海珊道光元年鄉試解首，榜發，已前卒。

translations.literal: Haishan ranked first in the provincial examination in the first year of Daoguang; when the list was published, he had already died earlier.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Daoguang, Haishan took first place in the provincial examination; by the time the results were announced, he had already been dead for some time.

sentences.zh: 其論學以宋賢為歸，又恥迂儒寡效，自農田、河渠、兵制、天下形勢所在，及漕糧利弊，悉心究討。

translations.literal: In his scholarly views he took the Song worthies as his standard, yet he also scorned pedantic scholars of little practical effect; from field management, rivers and canals, military organization, and the strategic points of the realm to the pros and cons of grain transport, he studied all with devoted care.
translations.idiomatic: In learning he looked to the Song worthies as his guide, yet he also despised pedantic scholars who achieved little in practice; from agriculture, rivers and irrigation works, military organization, and the strategic geography of the empire to the costs and benefits of grain transport, he investigated everything with painstaking care.

sentences.zh: 三吳亢旱港涸，一日北風大作，水入，糾眾築堤儲之，歲以有秋。

translations.literal: When the Three Wu region suffered drought and the harbors dried up, one day a north wind blew fiercely, water flowed in, and he rallied the people to build dikes and store it—the year thus had a good harvest.
translations.idiomatic: When drought struck the Three Wu and the harbor channels ran dry, a fierce north wind one day drove water in; he gathered the people to build dikes and hold it back, and that year the fields yielded a full harvest.

sentences.zh: 著小安樂窩集、喪禮問答、火攻秘錄。

translations.literal: He authored the Little Anle Nest Collection, Questions and Answers on Mourning Rites, and Secret Records of Fire Attack.
translations.idiomatic: His works include the Collected Writings from the Little Anle Nest, Questions and Answers on Mourning Rites, and Secret Records on Fire Attack.

sentences.zh: 履，海珊門人也。

translations.literal: Lv was Haishan's disciple.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lv was Haishan's student.

sentences.zh: 傳海珊之學，尤精三禮。

translations.literal: He transmitted Haishan's learning and was especially expert in the Three Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He carried forward Haishan's scholarship and was especially accomplished in the Three Rites.

sentences.zh: 其議禮之文，皆犁然有當，非徒習訓詁名物者。

translations.literal: His writings on ritual all cut clearly to the point; he was no mere student of glosses and material objects.
translations.idiomatic: His essays on ritual all settled matters with unmistakable clarity; he was no mere antiquarian of glosses and nomenclature.

sentences.zh: 官句容訓導。

translations.literal: He served as assistant instructor of Jurong.
translations.idiomatic: He served as assistant instructor at Jurong.

sentences.zh: 著積石山房集。

translations.literal: He authored the Jishi Mountain Studio Collection.
translations.idiomatic: He authored the Collected Writings from the Jishi Mountain Studio.
